subject: [External] East Wing Modernization
body:
Dear Review Committee,
You don' t o fte n ge t e mail f ro m milg racias512@ gmail.c om. Le arn w hy t his  is  im po rtan t
The preservation of US History is vitally the preservation of buildings and monuments. The US White House
is iconic throughout the world. It is regrettable that the East Wing of the building was destroyed without
proper authorization.  Any parallel destruction would make the violation of the destruction clear. Imagine
tearing down a wing of the Elysee Palace (France), Kremlin (Russia) or The Presidential Complex (Turkey)
without any input, review or approvals. The US White House is "the people's house", It does not belong to
any of its temporary occupants (US Presidents and their families) to do with as they wish. The East Wing
should be reinstated to its previous design. Short of that the Commission, Congress and other entities
should exercise their rights to review and approve OR NOT any redesign of the iconic historic US WHite
House. Modernization may be warranted, but not for such an out of scale addition and not for such a self-
aggrandizing and unnecessary purpose. Please restore the People's House to its rightful place of dignity,
history and purpose.
Sincerely,
KM O'Neill, Ed.D.

body:

Hello Commissioners,
We are writing to emphatically oppose the proposed Ballroom Project at the White House.  It is appalling
that the Trump Administration demolished the East Wing without regard to the history, without
permission or oversight..  On that basis only, the building of the Ballroom should be tabled.
If the Ballroom is not tabled, the size, architecture and building plans  should be agreed upon by groups
such as The National Trust for Historic Preservation, other regulatory agencies and of course the
Congress.
The financing of the Ballroom Project should also be carefully reviewed for conflicts of interest.
Thank you for stopping the Ballroom Project until the appropriate groups form a committee and make
joint decisions regarding the scope of this project.
We also think that the Planning Commission should address the East Wing Demolition which was done
without permits or approvals.  We think that the Wing should be re-built prior to any funding going to the
Ballroom.
Sincerely,
Richard and Kristen Winn

I am writing to express how distraught I am regarding the proposed destruction of the East Wing of the
"People’s House." While I understand that a larger space may be required, the President's current proposal
is deeply problematic. This plan would render the most historic and significant parts of the White House
inconspicuous and tiny.
Furthermore, the projected costs have already doubled. Even if private supporters were to cover the initial
construction, the taxpayers would still be left to shoulder the ongoing burden of decorating, maintaining,
and staffing such an expansive space. At a time when our nation struggles to feed the hungry or provide
medical care for millions, we should not be prioritizing the construction of an enormous ballroom for
entertaining.
I firmly believe we should not be building a ballroom or an arch that would detract from the beauty of our
existing monuments dedicated to great Americans.
Thank you for your time and for considering my concerns on this matter.
Sincerely,
Margaret Cauley

I am 77 years old and have had a deeply held admiration of everything historical in D.C. since 
childhood.  My grandparents took me my first time when I was in 5th grade, and I toured the 
Whitehouse.  I feel this building, like most the landmarks are sacrosanct historical treasures.  The 
wanton way the East Wing has been destroyed is an unconscionable affront to our history, our tax 
dollars and our sense of continuity.  Please do what you can to restore this building to its previous 
beauty and stop any future desecration without oversight.   
Thank you,  
Linda Calcamuggio, Rossford, OH

subject: NCPC Website Email
body:
I'm writing to register my belated complain to the tearing down of the White House East Wing without
permission and my objections to the plans for a giant out-of-scale ballroom. I oppose the spending of
$300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization, permits, or design
review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American history. I want this
project canceled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design. No one is above the law
and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law would be an affront to
all law-abiding Americans.
Thank you for your attention to this matter,
MK Zuravleff

subject: Written Comments
name: Ellis Cohen
body:
The current President's plan for tearing down the East Wing (and the destruction that has already been
wrought) are both horrifying and illegal.
Although the White House has served as a temporary home for incumbent US Presidents since 1800, this
National Historic Landmark and National Park is owned by the American people. No US President is the
owner of the property or the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions
are limited by law and by respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight was clearly illegal. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people who were given
no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing back to its
former size and design. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible in
form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Amanda Martin
body:
As a pre-teen, back in the 20th century, I was taken by my Aunt & Uncle to visit the White House. I was told
it was the People's House, as I'm sure we all were back then. It's how I always thought of it, until last
summer, when the East Wing was suddenly demolished by President Trump, without any permission or
input, with total disregard of what the White House means to the American people.
And after, of course, President Trump had promised that nothing would be destroyed for him to build his
ballroom.
I am among the many who would like to see the East Wing rebuilt, restored to what it was. If a covered
passageway needs to be built from the East Wing to a new ballroom, why then of course - after the proper
review and pre-planning - build the necessary passageway or extension from the restored East Wing. And
any new ballroom must be approved by the NCPC, and be an appropriate size to compliment the White
House.
In addition, the new ballroom is being funded by private donors. It will not be part of the People's House,
but a private corporate structure. This feels wrong, it is wrong. There should be transparency to all of the
planning and funding.
The White House is a shared civic symbol of the United States of America. It is not the private property of
any one administration and should be, needs to be, treated as such. With oversight and standards expected
for any other federally significant project. I was so used to seeing the White House that I did not realize how
much it meant to me, until I saw pictures of the East Wing demolished. It broke my heart.

body:
I support an enforceable stop work order on any changes to publicly owned properties that have not
obtained permits in advance from the proper jurisdictions. Permitting procedures should utilize the
accepted guidelines for changes and additions to historic buildings seeking approvals as traditionally apply
to public and private property and particularly to the White House compound and all public and private
historic buildings in Washington DC.
Because the current president’s project proceeded with disregard of all the above safeguards and because
the current situation of the White House and immediate surrounding grounds is untenable, I support an
addition to the White House that does not overwhelm the historic structure and is built to complimentary
scale. In addition, I do not support gold gilding of any sort as part of the finish material unless specifically
suggested by a committee of known, respected, architectural historians skilled in such matters of design
and who are acceptable to the National Trust of Historic Places.
Thank you.

subject: Written Comments
name: Thomas Carmichael
body:
With Respect:
I am commenting on the East Wing Modernization Project. It is difficult to discuss the Project without
recalling President Trump’s attempts to interject himself (or even just his name) into national cultural
heritage as an authority on interior decoration, architectural design, construction, renovation, as well as the
Arts and battleship production.
Affairs of state ( leadership and oversight of party politics, legislation, budget issues, foreign policy
formulation and frequently hosting and/or visiting foreign dignitaries, etc.) burden President Trump greatly.
To underline his impressive skills, he needs some guidance to avoid tasks in fields that require skills he
simply does not possess. Architecture is one of those fields. A review board should provide that direction.
Certainly, he must acknowledge that the White House was not his private architecture/property due to his
election; the U.S. government owns and/or supplies housing or offices for officials around the country and
world. The bulldozer attack on the White House shot in the media at the public which he serves did not
project a sober understanding of his responsibility to our citizens. An outsized, supremely grandiose project
will not allow U.S. citizens to forget that slight.
The White House through the years has projected a symbolic message of sobriety and responsibility to
World Leaders. Those of lasting reputation certainly valued thoughtful conversation and power far above
display of wealth and conceits that have been laid before them in other countries. A White House host
shows wisdom when he/she displays with pride a pedigree of conscience and human concern. U.S. quiet
power and dignity does not need displays of opulence. The use of a classical style in a building of immense
proportions will evoke laugh and ridicule - but that is an opulence he has chosen. It is out of place both next
to the White House and in Washington, DC — itself a national capital modest in size.
I believe that fulfilling your responsibilities as a Commission Member is to help President Trump understand
the bizarre size of his proposed ballroom and glaring reference to classical culture simply does not project a
relevant cultural portrait of the United States. He would have been wise to seek and listen to neutral
judgement of its merits, and hold off on leveling an existing building long embraced by the Public.
I sincerely thank you for your service on the Commission.
Thomas Carmichael

subject: Written Comments
name: Mary Humstone
body:
I am writing to comment on the “East Wing Modernization Project.” First of all, the name of this project is
misleading. The East Wing is gone, and what is being proposed (and built) has nothing to do with the
original East Wing of the White House.
The proposed ballroom, which would replace the East Wing of the White House, defies the government’s
own standards for additions to historic buildings. It is the same height as the White House and its sheer size,
totally out of scale for the property, makes the White House look like a quaint addition. It mimics the
architectural design of the White House instead of representing its own time period. It is obvious that this
project was designed with only one thing in mind – the personal taste and desires of the president. The
design ignores the context – The White House Complex, which is a National Historic Landmark (the highest
designation for historic buildings in the U.S.) and a National Park.
I worked in historic preservation my entire career and worked with hundreds of Americans who strove to
do their best to preserve our heritage, sometimes at significant cost to themselves. Now we have the
president of the United States tearing down the East Wing of the White House, the People’s House, without
bothering to even get a permit. It is an insult to all Americans that the president has wantonly destroyed
one of our most cherished historic landmarks and is building a hideous, 90,000-square-foot, $400 million
monument to himself. One person should not be allowed to impose their personal taste on a property that
belongs to all Americans. This project should have been offered to the public and experts in historic
preservation for ideas and review long before the East Wing was demolished.
If allowed to be built as planned, the White House, a symbol of our democracy, will be overpowered by a
monument to the super-wealthy leisure class. This is especially inappropriate when a majority of Americans
are suffering from lack of adequate food, shelter, education and healthcare. I adamantly oppose this
project.

demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Cynthia Julian
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

name: Christopher Taylor
body:
As an American I am appalled at the attempt of our president to remake, rename, and rebrand our shared
landmarks that ,like the grandeur of our natural parks, are meant to be preserved for all future generations.
From renaming the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, to wanting to add his image to Mt. Rushmore,
renaming Airports, Train Stations and on and on we are witnessing an attempt of an Authoritarian self
aggrandizement.
The way he has bulldozed the East Wing, paved over the Jacqueline Kennedy Rose Garden, plastered tacky
gold plated tchotchkes all over the interior of the White House prove that in addition to seeing himself
above any restraints he has no respect for the American People.I urge you to take control of the design of
the new East Wing. A new event space isn't totally irrational, given the destruction of the existing structure
of the East Wing. Allowing a narcissistic man-child with the design sense of a used car salesman to control
the design process absurd.
The world looked on with horror and a broken heart as the Notre Dame Cathedral burned in Paris. To my
mind that day was as devastating as 9/11 or the Challenger disaster in 1986. My faith in Humanity was
restored when I saw the resurrection of that historic treasure. It is a gift to all the world. What must the
world think when it sees the sad low our institutions, our history, our cultural identity have sunk to.
I implore you to not be a willing participant in the desecration of the People's House.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kristin Weaver Bowman
body:
I was shocked and appalled when heavy machinery demolished a portion of the White House with no
warning, no oversight, and no input from the NCPC and the CFA; I do not support the construction of any
addition in the place of the East Wing that justifies overstepping those boundaries. The current president
ought to be held accountable for such a bad decision, and made to pay for damages to the East Wing. The
most important part of the project to me is that it continues to reflect the historic significance of the White
House as not just the home of our Executive, but as a symbol of our country. Since Washington stepped
down, a hallmark of our presidents has been the peaceful transfer of power from one administration to the
next, and, regardless of personal politics, each president before now has respected the guardrails of the
office. Therefore, I do not support any changes to the White House that overtly promote or aggrandize the
current president in any way. Modernization is acceptable, as long as it maintains the same look as the rest
of the building and does not stand out as an eyesore.

house, occupied temporarily by each president in turn, and does not belong to any individual president.
This project should be stopped immediately and subjected to review by all relevant historic preservation
commissions. Also, whatever is built now should NOT overshadow the rest of the building. It must remain in
proportion to the architectural environment, and should be appropriately American, not a monarchical gilt
encrusted showpiece. Also, the gold flourished recently added to the White House are tasteless and are an
embarrassment to our democratic ideals. They must be removed.

body:

preservation of our nation's history, historic places, and natural areas is of utmost importance to me. The
historic sites of Washington, DC, are at the heart of our historic preservation movement, and the White
House, as a symbol of our nation, is one of the most important historic buildings in our country. It holds the
highest honor possible of being a National Historic Landmark while also serving as a National Park. The
destruction of the East Wing of the White House without any oversight, without any public comment, was a
completely illegal action. The concept that a ballroom is wanted or needed is completely false, and all
proposals for what will be constructed in place of the East Wing are fully out of appropriate scale and
design. The White House is owned by the people of the United States, and this citizen is opposed to the
unchecked destruction of the East Wing of the White House, and I am opposed to any reconstruction that
doesn't involve rebuilding the White House back to exactly what it was.

approved the final design, this project must be canceled AND the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its
former design.

As a retired US History teacher who has ancestors who fought for our republic in every conflict in our
nation’s history for the idea of democracy and the rule of law, I strongly believe that the unlawful
destruction of the East Wing of the White House is an affront to our country’s collective memory. I taught
my students to respect the meaning of democracy and the symbolic value of the preservation of our past.
To do anything besides reconstruct the East Wing as close to what it was would be the destruction of our
collective heritage. I once had the honor of taking a tour through the public areas of the East Wing, and it is
a memory that I cherish and will forever remember. To deny that to our future generations would destroy
the idea of liberty and freedom that the People’s House represents. A ballroom can be built elsewhere.
History cannot be bulldozed. I oppose with all my being the construction of an architectural abomination
upon hallowed memory.

subject: Written Comments
name: Sue Wilbur
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns. It should be restored to its previous state. Preservation and history is important! If
we need a ballroom it should be built somewhere else on the grounds. I do not think we need one. We’ve
managed almost 250 years without one!
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Robin Douglass
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.
Thank you for your attention to this matter!
R. A. Douglass

body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project.
This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts. This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have

name: Rebecca Hickman
body:
oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion

subject: Written Comments
name: Laura Georgi
body:
I am furious that the current temporary inhabitant of the White House has acted as if he had the right to
destroy a wing of the building before even submitting a plan, let alone getting approval, for its replacement.
Although it would serve him right to have to look at the hole he made for as long as he remains there, that
might not best serve the people, the owners of the place.
I ask that there be an independent study of what the true needs and purposes should be for a replacement
for the destroyed East Wing. Once that has been determined, there must be a request for proposals for a
replacement consistent with the results of that study. Submitted proposals must be reviewed and ranked
by persons with relevant qualifications for the task. Any funding must come through the regular budgetary
process, not bribes paid by billionaire businessmen to the current inhabitant.
Any persons appointed to the commission by the current inhabitant must not be allowed to participate at
any stage in the study or the selection of the winning proposal; they clearly were selected for their loyalty
not relevant expertise. It seems that ex officio members typically do not participate in the regular business
of the commission, nevertheless, Defense Secretary Hegseth and Representative Comer have demonstrated
their complete and utter inability to serve the people in a strictly nonpartisan manner.
Chairman Will Scharf must resign. The idea that demolition didn’t require permission and could proceed
without an APPROVED design for a replacement is beyond preposterous.

accountability.

should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Dr. Nancy Andrzejczak
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and

the historical significance of the east wing and demonstrate that the USA cares about minorities.

subject: Written Comments
name: Pamela Woldow
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and the most iconic symbol of American democracy. It has
been the home of presidents since 1800 and belongs not to any temporary occupant but to the American
people in perpetuity. The current president is, in the most meaningful sense, a tenant —  entrusted with the
stewardship of a national treasure, not licensed to alter it beyond recognition.
The demolition of the historic East Wing — conducted without prior submission to the National Capital
Planning Commission, without Commission of Fine Arts review, and without Congressional authorization as
required by federal statute — was a unilateral act that defied the legal framework designed to protect this
irreplaceable property. The claim that portions of the project were of "top secret nature" does not explain
or excuse the failure to obtain required approvals before demolition began. Previous administrations,
including this one in its first term, participated in required review processes as a matter of course. That
precedent was abandoned here without justification.
The proposed replacement — a 90,000-square-foot ballroom nearly twice the footprint of the White House
itself, rising to match the height of the historic mansion — is not an addition. It is a supplanting. The
Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation are unambiguous: new construction affecting historic
properties must be compatible with existing massing, size, and scale, and must be subordinate to the
original structure. The proposed ballroom fails this standard by any reasonable measure.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to exercise its full authority and independence in this
review. Any construction approved on the demolition site must be genuinely compatible in form and
demonstrably subordinate in scale to the original Executive Mansion. The American people were given no
opportunity to comment before the East Wing was destroyed. This review is, at minimum, the process they
are owed — and it must be conducted with the rigor and independence the law requires and the People's
House deserves.

subject: Written Comments
name: Elizabeth Welch
body:
To the National Capital Planning Commission,
My name is Elizabeth Welch, and I am a graduate student at Goucher College’s MA in Historic Preservation
program I’m writing to give public comment on the White House Ballroom Construction Project. The White
House is "The People’s House," a living symbol of American democracy that belongs to the nation, not to
any single individual or administration. The recent demolition of the East Wing and East Colonnade, leveled
in just three days in October 2025, represents a reckless departure from the stewardship such a landmark
deserves. This haphazard destruction of historic fabric, conducted with little regard for materials and no
prior formal review, sets a dangerous precedent for our nation's most iconic civic sites.
While a modernized ballroom has been proposed to keep the executive residence a "beacon of American
excellence," such excellence must be built on a foundation of transparency and respect for our shared
history. Currently, the proposed 90,000 square foot ballroom threatens to dwarf the Executive Residence,
fundamentally altering the architectural character and visual balance of the White House complex. Any new
construction of this scale must be designed with rigorous oversight to ensure it harmonizes with the
proportions of the historic residence rather than overwhelming it.
Furthermore, it is imperative that the NCPC and CFA demand clear, updated plans to protect the
archaeological resources and the structural integrity of the main house during construction. The
preservation of our national heritage is a core value. Fiscal responsibility and the defense of American
institutions require us to protect the tangible history of the Republic from impulsive, non-transparent
modifications. We must ensure that this project does not result in the permanent loss of the very history
that makes the White House a symbol of our national continuity and excellence. Please consider scaling the
Ballroom down and matching the architectural style of the Executive Residence. Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Elizabeth Welch

egotistical narcissism has compelled him to attempt to "mark his territory" all over our nation's capital. He
and his ballroom need to be stopped. Just rebuild the East Wing was it was.

Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.

contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

Doug Harris

body:

watched as generations of First Ladies inhabited those halls and rooms. And now all of that is gone.
Overnight. With no notice and seemly little thought or regard.

administration to proceed with its plans for building the abomination of a massive gilded ballroom that is
neither needed nor wanted. Tens of millions of Americans struggle to afford the most basic necessities of
life. We can ill afford this price tag.
Thank you

name: Aubree Coats
body:
To Whom It May Concern,
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. Its design and appearance have been a symbol of the American presidency
since its completion. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or the
structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits, and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people,
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
Thank you for your attention to this matter,
Aubree Coats

requirements to change the White House should be even greater as the President is only a resident and not
an owner of the house. As a result, I request that the perpetrator of the destruction be fined and that the
East Wing be restored to the structure as approved previously.
Thank you for taking into consideration the wishes and respect for history of one of the 340+ million owners
of this national historic treasure, the citizens of these United States.

subject: Written Comments
name: marla felber
body:
The White House is the People’s House, not the personal property of the President. It was designed in 1792
by architect James Hoban through a public competition initiated by George Washington. Its classical
composition, with lower East and West wings, reflects Georgian and Neoclassical principles that emphasize
balance, proportion, and restraint.
In 1997, the National Park Service issued design guidelines stating that the White House and President’s
Park are foremost a public trust and an essential part of the nation’s heritage. Any changes to this historic
site must respect its architectural integrity and symbolic importance.
The proposed project totals 90,000 square feet, including a 22,000-square-foot ballroom designed to
accommodate 1,000 people. By comparison, the White House contains 55,000 square feet across multiple
levels, and typical events in the West Wing host approximately 140 guests. The scale of the proposal is
disproportionate and appears architecturally incompatible with the existing building.
The Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation provide clear federal guidance for construction
projects affecting historic properties, yet these standards have not been followed. New construction should
be compatible with existing massing, size, scale, and architectural features—criteria this project does not
meet. These principles have guided preservation of the White House since the 1792 public design
competition.
There are serious concerns regarding massing, height, proportion, and overall design harmony. As a
national and international symbol, the White House demands careful and responsible stewardship. It is
central to the American story and represents the Republic and the values it stands for.

In 1997, the National Park Service issued design guidelines stating that the White House and President’s 
Park are foremost a public trust and an essential part of the nation’s heritage. Any changes to this historic 
site must respect its architectural integrity and symbolic importance. 
 
The proposed project totals 90,000 square feet, including a 22,000-square-foot ballroom designed to 
accommodate 1,000 people. By comparison, the White House contains 55,000 square feet across multiple 
levels, and typical events in the West Wing host approximately 140 guests. The scale of the proposal is 
disproportionate and appears architecturally incompatible with the existing building. 
 
The Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation provide clear federal guidance for construction 
projects affecting historic properties, yet these standards have not been followed. New construction should 
be compatible with existing massing, size, scale, and architectural features—criteria this project does not 
meet. These principles have guided preservation of the White House since the 1792 public design 
competition. 
 
There are serious concerns regarding massing, height, proportion, and overall design harmony. As a 
national and international symbol, the White House demands careful and responsible stewardship. It is 
central to the American story and represents the Republic and the values it stands for.

body:

flying kites. Even though many people buy and tear down buildings, the White House belongs to all of us
rather than one of us. I was shocked to see the East Wing demolished without permission. It is as if they
believed if they tore it down then we would accept a new design of a gigantic ballroom without being
heartbroken. Compared to other nations, ours is still young and has such a rich history that has always been
part of DC. I hope that the East Wing is rebuilt because it balanced the look of the Whitehouse, held so
much history of our nation and is in fact considered a historic building. Please return it to its prior state or at
least keep the footprint the same as it was before the bulldozers came in.

subject: Written Comments
name: Mary Beecher
body:
After witnessing the embarrassingly unprepared presentation by the architectural firm now handling this
so-called “modernization project” last month, I am even more convinced that this proposed building is an
affront to its historic location and our shared American legacy. At an estimated cost of $300 million dollars,
what are Americans getting that will represent our country in a deserving way? Nothing. What is proposed
looks like a convention center wrapped in a rote Neoclassical gesture that a second-year architecture
student might concoct. No amount of cornice alignment will help this monstrosity fit in the area for which it
is proposed. It is astounding that it was not even designed prior to the destruction of historic East Wing.
There was no vetting, no oversight, no approval, no respect given to the heritage of the White House and its
East Wing until now, which seems late but better late than never. Clearly, the entire project is being driven
by the unimaginative whims of a developer (the president) who has no sense of history, scale, materiality,
or what it means to create a memorable spatial experience with effective sight lines and excellent acoustics.
Why not accommodate large state dinners in an area of Washington D.C. that has the space for a cutting-
edge venue; somewhere that might even benefit from the attention and focus? Why shoehorn a bloated
facility where it can’t possible honor the Classical principles of hierarchy and fitness?
That this project is allegedly funded privately is irrelevant. The White House belongs to the American
people and its grounds are part of our shared history. Yes, it has evolved, but within reason and with
oversight and a process that does not “demolish first and figure out what to build later.” If we need a large
contemporary venue for state dinners and ceremonial events, build it away from the Mall and do it right…
without a convoluted entry sequence and a ridiculous covered walkway. It is the committee’s responsibility
to stand up for good design by saying NO to this ridiculous proposal. I hope that the president’s appointees
have some concern for their own legacies and reputations. An improved rendition of the former East Wing
(complete with a 21st century bunker) is the only appropriate addition to this site after what has been
done.

body:
I am opposed to this administration's bad faith actions to construct an unnecessary and un-permitted White
House ballroom when there are so many budgetary needs to help keep community members from falling
into insurmountable debt, ill-health, and worse. I support the following message:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

body:
Until last year the White House , with its wings, had been a graceful structure showing the research,
planning, and bi-partisan passion to protect and extend its use for future generations. Perempotorily
destroying the East Wing without warning was a travesty and stained a record of House Stewardship.

should always be the focal point on the grounds. If needed, such a facility could be built off-site and serve
as a large party site for all federal services.

the House in the center. During the Truman years the architects had time to methodically rebuild the White
House. You may not have that ability, but no doubt there is a wealth of plans you can use.
And, yes, I am a White House history groupie. I watched Mrs. Kennedy give the televised tour, I trooped
through it as a ninth grade Minnesota Girl Scout, and I have watched The Residence twice on NetFlix.
Please, no ballroom, only a rebuilding of the East wing.

subject: Written Comments
name: Laura Lundin
body:
Public Comment – Response to the Proposed White House Ballroom and East\u8209 -Wing Demolition
I am writing to register my strong opposition to the planned $400\u8239 million ballroom addition to the
White House and the accompanying demolition of the historic East Wing. After reviewing the recent
renderings and the surrounding circumstances described in the press coverage, I have three primary
concerns that I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to consider before the March\u8239 5
hearing.
1. Irreversible Heritage Loss
The East Wing is an integral part of the White House complex, embodying decades of architectural history
and presidential legacy. The renderings show a massive 90,000\u8239 sq\u8239 ft structure built level with
the mansion, a scale that would visually dominate and fundamentally alter the historic silhouette of the
nation’s most iconic residence. Even if select elements—cornerstones, colonnade columns, chandeliers —
are “meticulously preserved,” the loss of the original fabric and spatial context cannot be recovered.
Historic preservation standards require that any intervention retain the character\u8209 -defining features
of a landmark; this proposal runs counter to that principle.
2. Questionable Cost and Funding Transparency
A $400\u8239 million price tag for a ceremonial ballroom, financed by a consortium of private donors and
corporations, raises serious fiscal accountability questions. While the administration claims the project is
“on budget and ahead of schedule,” there is no publicly available, independent cost\u8209 -benefit
analysis. Large\u8209 -scale demolition and new construction typically generate hidden expenses
(environmental remediation, security upgrades, long\u8209 -term maintenance) that can far exceed initial
estimates. Given competing national priorities, allocating such a sum to a luxury venue demands rigorous
scrutiny and justification.
3. Lack of Genuine Public Oversight and Broad Opposition
The rapid removal of the renderings from the NCPC website, the appointment of political allies to oversight
bodies, and the initiation of demolition before any formal review all signal a circumvention of established
procedural safeguards. The National Trust for Historic Preservation has already filed a federal lawsuit, and
the public outcry— amplified by media outlets such as CNN—demonstrates widespread concern.
Proceeding without transparent, inclusive deliberation would undermine public trust in the very
commissions tasked with protecting our heritage.
Recommendations
Pause the Project – Issue an immediate stay on demolition and construction until a comprehensive
historic\u8209 -impact assessment is completed by an independent preservation authority.
Conduct an Independent Financial Review – Require a detailed, publicly disclosed audit of the projected
costs, funding sources, and long\u8209 -term fiscal implications.
Facilitate Meaningful Public Participation – Hold open hearings, solicit written comments, and provide full
access to all project documents—including the “East Wing Modernization” rendering package—so that
stakeholders can evaluate the proposal on an informed basis.
Explore Less Intrusive Alternatives – Consider adaptive reuse of the existing East Wing or modest interior
renovations that preserve the historic envelope while meeting functional needs, thereby avoiding the
irreversible loss of heritage.
The White House is not merely a working office; it is a living monument to our nation’s democratic history.
Any alteration of its fabric must be approached with the utmost respect for preservation standards, fiscal
responsibility, and democratic oversight. I respectfully request that the NCPC give full weight to these
concerns and act to protect the integrity of the White House for current and future generations.
Thank you for your consideration.

subject: Written Comments
name: Nancy Merrick
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

body:
Demolishing the historic East Wing of the White House without review, without permits, and without
Congressional oversight clearly violated the law. The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a
National Park. The American people own it. No president owns the property or its buildings.
"The president broke not only laws but also the trust of the American people.
"I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require any reconstruction of the East Wing to maintain
it historic design and size. Anything built on the demolition site must match the style of the original
structure of the Executive Mansion, and it must be subordinate in size
"I urge, further, that any reconstruction be funded only with appropriations from Congress and that no
private money be allowed for this project. The American people own the land, not any one president or any
corporation seeking to buy favor. Do not reward a lawless president.
"If Congress does not approve funding, and if a design keeping with the building's historical character
cannot be achieved, the land should be left vacant.

approving those contracts.

unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

body:
"East Wing Modernization Project" is a misnomer. The East Wing was obliterated without oversight,
comments, consideration or permits, so that the out-of-control individual known as the President of the
United States could do whatever he wanted. Who knows what that actually is. I am a Permit Expeditor,
someone who assists developers, contractors, insurance companies or others process building permits. I
have to go through the Planning, Building, and sometimes the Fire departments just to put up a trash
enclosure around a dumpster. It is inconceivable that anyone could just order up demolition equipment and
tear down a piece of the US White House with no process, and no consequences.Even at this late phase,
this action should not stand. Any assertion that we need to keep building a ballroom "for the security of the
country" is ludicrous and suspect. Secure whatever needs to be secured, and take the appropriate time and
steps to restore the structure faithfully and properly.

should be reconstructed to restore the place that honors and serves the spouse of the president and in a
size and scale that is aesthetically proportional to the White House itself.
Thank you,
Sandy Ostendorf
Ankeny, Iowa

subject: Written Comments
name: Sharon Ferguson
body:
The sudden and unlawful destruction of the East Wing of the White House is a desecration of one of the
most significant historical and architectural icons belonging to We The People. To see it ripped apart by a
fleet of bulldozers, without discussion or permission from the owners, has caused horror and revulsion
across America.
Because Donald Trump is the criminal who has done this, Donald Trump must be barred from any planning
of the replacement structure. He must, however, be mandated to pay for it from his personal resources.
This is mandatory.
Also mandatory is for the East Wing to be in harmony with the size and style of the rest of the building that
he hasn't destroyed yet. It must serve the interest of The People, must facilitate the work of the Executive
and must reflect the egalitarianism that is foundational to the United States.
When George Washington so famously refused a monarchial title, choosing "Mr President" instead, he set
the country firmly away from emulating the aristocratic model of Europe and emphasizing the president's
status of equality with every other American (man). A ballroom is a stupid waste of space, meant for special
occasions and easily accommodated by temporary structures. The Common Man does not hold galas. The
renewed East Wing should have no gilt, no frescoes, no marbled pillars. And it must provide space for the
day to day work of bettering the nation which is the very purpose of the White House itself.
The president is not made more effective by building superfluous entertainment spaces like theaters,
gymnasiums, greenhouses, barrooms or, yes, ballrooms. These are not integral to serious government on
behalf of all Americans. It should not resemble the flourishes that typify buildings that were meant to admit
and serve only the elites of foreign countries, It must exemplify American values and our shared
responsibility for the work that supports our common good. Office spaces including an area sufficient to
support the First Spouse, improved culinary facilities to encourage good nutrition, child care space for the
children of White House workers and to serve as a reminder of the future generations for whom current
decisions are being made, perhaps a visitors' area to understand how the White House functions in the
People's interest and the changing needs and facilities over time.

subject: Written Comments
name: Mary Goforth
body:
-----------------
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

above the law and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law would be
an affront to all law-abiding Americans.

accountability. Private donations to fund this vanity project are bribes. The White House is a shared civic

standards expected of every other federally significant project. It's the People's House so our voices should
be heard. I can't even describe the sickening feeling I had when the bulldozers razed the East Wing.
Thank you,
Dolores

subject: Written Comments
name: Karen Orell
body:
I watched in horror as the entire history of the East Wing was demolished in less than 3 days by Donald
Trump. This destruction was not permitted, authorized or cleared through any government or state offices
to occur. The destruction was just a wreckless plundering of a historical landmark.
The East Wing which I myself have visited was the entrance through which visitors entered for tours at the
capitol. It was the center of the events for visiting dignataries and the offices of all the former presidents'
wives (excluding Melania who decided she didn't want to be a first lady). The entire history of the white
house has been destroyed.
Through the public information available, there were no movers in the East Wing prior to it's destruction.
The contents have simply dissapeared!
Where are:
1. The records, files and documents that were housed here
2. The artwork and historical statues that were previously located here
3. The historical furnishings that filled the East Wing
No one seems to have any concern of all the contents that were previously housed in the East Wing! These
need to be found, accounted for and preserved. If they even still exist. From watching the East Wing
bulldozers it looked like all the contents were stil in the East Wing at the time it was destroyed.
On a separate but critical note:
FUNDS:
Donald Trump has continued to accept funds from major businesses and individuals in the US and abroad
for the new "ballroom" he wants to build in place of the East Wing.
1. WHERE ARE THOSE FUNDS?
2. Who has control of those funds?
3. Are they in an interest bearing account?
4. Under what "agreement" or "contract" were those funds "given" or transferred?
5. What is owed to those individuals and businesses that sent funds for the new "ballroom?"
6. Have some of the funds sent in for the "ballromm" been spent already?
7. Who is tracking the spending of the funds sent in under the premise they are for a new "ballrom?"
8. Who is tracking who gave funds and how much did they give?
- I oppose the spending of ANY FUNDS on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. The "ballrom" project was not a "modernization" project but rather a complete
razing of American history.
- I want this project canceled
- I want the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design.
No one is above the law!
Permiting this project to proceed without penalizing those who broke the law would be an affront to all
law-abiding Americans.
STOP THE BALLROOM. STOP THE DESTRUCTION OF AMERICA!

subject: Written Comments
name: Lillian Willis
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Pamela Latos
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Tristan Louis
body:
When architect James Hoban, who had won the commission to finalize plans for the initial White House
building, he drew heavily on Palladian vocabulary focused on human-centered proportions, hierarchical
composition, axial symmetry, and measured restraint. The use of harmonic ratios so rooms relate
mathematically to each other and to the whole building resulted in a building that felt balanced rather than
monumental for its own sake. Furthermore, the control of ornamentation was key to creating a building
that felt like "The People's House," using the building as a mean to reinforcing the ideals of American
democracy.
The current proposal for the East Wing Modernization Project appears to contradict the long established
tradition of careful editing that was key to making the building one of the most enduring symbol of
American equalitarian ideals. The East Wing has historically been a secondary deferential element to the
main residence. Expanding it with larger volumes or more complex footprints risks turning it into an
accumulation of parts rather than a mathematically ordered extension. When the side element starts
competing visually with the central block, the hierarchy collapses.
Palladian estates, on which the White House is modeled, depend on a dominant central mass with
subordinate flanking elements. If a redesign increases the East Wing’s prominence (height, façade
articulation, or visual weight), the eye no longer reads the residence as the undisputed center. That violates
the piano nobile logic: important things should look important because of proportion, not decoration.
By drifting away from Palladio's rhythmic openings, clear base-middle-top ordering, and restrained
ornament, which combined to make grand buildings feel human scaled, the current design is offering an
imbalance that may result in the building feeling more bureaucratic than domestic-civic, eroding the
centrally balanced message of the White House as a representation of "people and state" and shifting the
language towards a more authoritarian view of government.
When entered into the overall design of the Washington DC layout, as envisioned by Pierre Charles
L'Enfant, the new addition create further disharmony in the layout of the US Mall. Presenting relative
dominance and proportional incoherence in the design, it disturbs a model of America that is based on
balances.
The resulting design not only demeans the building's balance but also creates an imbalance in the
presentation of what America is about, undermining principles of equality and humility established by the
founding fathers. As such, the proposed design could easily be seen as un-American, presenting a distorted
view of dominance by one wing over the rest of the state.
Since the existing building has already been destroyed and needs to be replaced, a design that would
restore symmetry between the east and west wing would be better suited to the site. If space is of
particular concern, much work could be down underground so that the external face of the people's house
remain as human-centered as as restrained as it was always intended to be.
Sincerely,
Tristan Louis
Concerned citizen

name: Carla Mueller
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.
Additionally, this "ballroom" should not dwarf the beauty of the White House.
Thank you.

body:

House and of the memory I had of visiting and thus becoming a part of its history. Ten years ago I was in
France and visited Versailles, the house built by Louis xiv. Gold, mirrors, tapestries, and opulence were
overwhelming. Although the skill and craftsmanship in the palace was overwhelming, I could not help but
think that his is why the people of France supported a revolution. To adorn our People's House" with
palatial decor is to deny the roots of what our country has stood for 250 years. Our nation's history and its
efforts to provide freedom and opportunity to all the people is not reflected in a building that is modeled
after European palaces built for the ultra powerful and ultra rich. I ask that the Planning Committee use its
influence to direct a modest renovation that reflects the values of our forefathers as well as those of the
population of our country today. We are not interested in impressing princes but in maintaining the spirit of
our own American Revolution.

subject: Written Comments
name: Linda Daignault
body:
The sorrow, disbelief, and at times anger I feel when I consider that someone—whether an individual,
organization, or oversight body—may fail to fully preserve and protect one of this nation’ s most revered
structures, the White House complex, is profound. Any decision to spend substantial funds on changes to
such an iconic national symbol must follow a transparent, rigorous process that ensures the result reflects
not only present needs, but future needs, and our shared national history. To proceed without such care
risks conveying the message that decisions about our most important public landmarks are shaped
primarily by power and wealth, rather than by thoughtful stewardship on behalf of all Americans.
As someone in my seventies, I recall the lengthy and deliberate processes that have shaped some of our
most respected national memorials. The most admired among them were not created hastily or
unilaterally; they emerged through years of public engagement, expert input, design competitions, debate,
and careful construction. That process itself is part of what gives these places their legitimacy and meaning.
If changes to the East Wing are undertaken without comparable levels of public participation, professional
oversight, and careful consideration of purpose, architectural integrity, materials, craftsmanship, and
national symbolism, the result risks being remembered not as a distinguished addition to a historic site, but
as a project defined by a single administration or personality. That would diminish both the structure and
the ideals it represents.
Should construction proceed as currently proposed, many Americans—and observers around the world —
may interpret it not as an expression of national excellence, but as a display of concentrated influence and
privilege. Our most visible public buildings should instead reflect the collective values, aspirations, and
dignity of the American people.

subject: Written Comments
name: James Caldwell
body:
The North Façade
Prior to its demolition, the East Wing served basically as an outbuilding attached to the White House by
means of a covered walkway. The East Wing was subsumed to the visual primacy of the main building.
Crucially, the roof of the covered corridor was below the sill line of the White House ground floor windows.
Under the proposed new construction, the corridor roof line reaches to the second-floor windows which
totally destroys the aesthetics of the White House east façade much like an unattractive growth on a
beautiful face. The corridor itself now becomes a major visual element elevated above ground level. What
we see is a monotonous string of thirteen blank panels separated by pilasters on bases. The pilasters are
too narrow and rather than suggesting a structural function seem more like the side rails of an empty
picture frame. Even the dentils hanging off the cornice are out of scale and serve more to remind one of a
runny nose than a classical entablature. In sum the corridor is too high and too boring.
The north façade of the new ballroom complex is a blunt instrument that competes with and diminishes the
historic presidential home. Whereas the White House has four bays on either side of its portico, the new
construction has seven bays, five of which are located on the projecting central pavilion. The design
requirement that the cornice match that of the White House results in a prominent and unattractive
basement level. Things become really weird when one turns the corner and sees the column bases of the
east side temple front below the basement level.
The East Façade
On the east façade there’s an octastyle temple front porch accessed by a flight of stairs from street level.
When one thinks of classical and neoclassical architecture, symmetry, balance, and harmony come to mind.
A fine example is just across the street from the proposed East Wing in the Treasury Building. The Shalom
Baranes proposal is more a hodgepodge of elements than anything else. The Temple front is neither
centered nor balanced with the rest of the east façade.
The South Façade
This is a total disaster. Initially this decastyle prostyle Corinthian portico contained a pediment, but
apparently one commissioner thought the pediment too massive, so the architect removed it. The result is
that the façade looks incomplete, similar to the temple of Hera I at Paestum. Decapitating the façade is a
symptom of the rush to get something built.
A temple front with ten columns is a major statement. The Pantheon only has eight for example, whereas
the Lincoln Memorial has twelve. The curved staircase leading to ground level is completely out of
proportion. On the plan it looks like a nineteenth-century moustache.
But the fundamental question is what purpose does this portico serve and the answer is none. Indeed, it
could and should be eliminated altogether. Doing so would greatly improve the eight-window east façade
especially if the wall space between the windows and temple front matched that of the building’s end. I
suppose the south lawn facing temple could be understood as a folly much like those fake classical
structures decorating eighteenth century English gardens and estates, but even so. Scaling back the East
Wing by eliminating this portico would also serve to balance better the South Lawn vista. (Originally the
Oval Office and the demolished East Wing were roughly in line.)
The NCPC continues to describe the project (8733) as East Wing Modernization. The Commission met on
January 8, 2026, for a pre-submission review of the project. The project was not considered at the February
meeting and is on the agenda for the March 5 meeting. The Commission consists of twelve members, seven
of whom are ex-officio. The president has appointed the majority of the voting members: William Schary
(Assistant to the President and WH Staff Secretary), Stuart Levenbach (Associate Director Office of
Management and Budget), and Michael Blair (White House Deputy Chief of Staff). The Mayor appointed
two voting members. The NCPC promises full biographies of the members to come soon. Thus, all the public
knows is that the majority works for and is beholden to the president. According to the NCPC website, the
Commission will consider approving the “preliminary and final site and building plans” on March 5. For
information on how to comment of attend Live Stream see https://www.ncpc.gov/review/meeting/
The motto of the Florentine Grand Duke Cosimo I was “Make haste slowly.” The NCPC and Commission of
Fine Arts would be well advised to do the same.

subject: Written Comments
name: David McNally
body:
To the National Capitol Planning Commission:
As a 7th generation Adirondacker, an owner of a home over 100 years old, a member of the Minerva
Historical Society, and as a patriotic American respectful of our history, I am writing to express my strong
opposition to the proposed construction of a permanent ballroom addition to the White House.
The White House is not merely a residence or an office; it is the preeminent symbol of American continuity.
I believe this proposal poses a significant threat to the architectural integrity and historic character of this
National Historic Landmark. It also sets a dangerous precedent for how changes to our historic properties
are made.
Points of Concern
Irreversible Alteration of the Historic Fabric: In preservation, "necessity" is sometimes offered as an excuse
to justify interventions that permanently mar historic structures. The unpermitted demolition of the East
Wing of the White House is the very definition of a self-created hardship.
Scale and Massing: I am deeply concerned about the rhythm and scale of the North and South elevations.
The White House has evolved, but it has largely maintained its iconic silhouette. A massive addition risks
"façadism," where the original structure becomes a mere backdrop for modern expansion.
The Precedent of Permanence: The beauty of the White House lies in its adherence to the 19th-century
residential form. Temporary pavilions have successfully hosted state dinners for decades. Converting a
temporary need into a permanent footprint is a fundamental violation of the Secretary of the Interior’s
Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties, specifically regarding the preservation of the building's
historic spatial relationships.
A Perspective from the Field
Living in a 100-year-old home teaches you that you are a steward, not just an owner. You learn to adapt
your lifestyle to the house, rather than forcing the house to accommodate every modern whim.
If we allow the most important house in the nation to be expanded for the sake of administrative
convenience or event logistics, we send a message to every local Historic Resources Commission in the
country that historic integrity is negotiable.
Recommendation
I urge the Commission to reject the proposal. Options remain to continue the use of temporary structures
that do not leave a permanent footprint, and to choose alternate venues for large-scale events that utilize
other historic D.C. assets.
Ultimately, the White House is federal property belonging to the American people, not personal property of
the President, who is considered a temporary resident or tenant. We must ensure that the White House
remains a residence and a monument, not a convention center.
Sincerely,

I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Michael Lundin
body:
I am writing to register my strong opposition to the planned $400\u8239 million ballroom addition to the
White House and the accompanying demolition of the historic East Wing. After reviewing the recent
renderings and the surrounding circumstances described in the press coverage, I have three primary
concerns that I urge the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) and the Commission of Fine Arts to
consider before the March\u8239 5 hearing.
1. Irreversible Heritage Loss
The East Wing is an integral part of the White House complex, embodying decades of architectural history
and presidential legacy. The renderings show a massive 90,000\u8239 sq\u8239 ft structure built level with
the mansion, a scale that would visually dominate and fundamentally alter the historic silhouette of the
nation’s most iconic residence. Even if select elements—cornerstones, colonnade columns, chandeliers —
are “meticulously preserved,” the loss of the original fabric and spatial context cannot be recovered.
Historic preservation standards require that any intervention retain the character\u8209 -defining features
of a landmark; this proposal runs counter to that principle.
2. Questionable Cost and Funding Transparency
A $400\u8239 million price tag for a ceremonial ballroom, financed by a consortium of private donors and
corporations, raises serious fiscal accountability questions. While the administration claims the project is
“on budget and ahead of schedule,” there is no publicly available, independent cost\u8209 -benefit
analysis. Large\u8209 -scale demolition and new construction typically generate hidden expenses
(environmental remediation, security upgrades, long\u8209 -term maintenance) that can far exceed initial
estimates. Given competing national priorities, allocating such a sum to a luxury venue demands rigorous
scrutiny and justification.
3. Lack of Genuine Public Oversight and Broad Opposition
The rapid removal of the renderings from the NCPC website, the appointment of political allies to oversight
bodies, and the initiation of demolition before any formal review all signal a circumvention of established
procedural safeguards. The National Trust for Historic Preservation has already filed a federal lawsuit, and
the public outcry— amplified by media outlets such as CNN—demonstrates widespread concern.
Proceeding without transparent, inclusive deliberation would undermine public trust in the very
commissions tasked with protecting our heritage.
I recommend pausing the project, conduct and independent financial review, facilitation of meaningful
public participation, and exploration of less intrusive alternatives.
The White House is not merely a working office; it is a living monument to our nation’s democratic history.
Any alteration of its fabric must be approached with the utmost respect for preservation standards, fiscal
responsibility, and democratic oversight. I respectfully request that the NCPC and the Commission of Fine
Arts give full weight to these concerns and act to protect the integrity of the White House for current and
future generations.
Thank you for your consideration.

name: Dana Christensen
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M to $400M project is being
funded by large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least
the appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
As a designer, I feel the new design, as proposed, is an abomination to the existing historic structure of the
"Peoples House", and would dwarf it both physically and metaphorically.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns. And is there a quid pro quo for such donations? The public needs to know.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability. This appears to be nothing but a vanity project by the current administration.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.
