subject: Written Comments
name: Rivka Ettinger
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is NOT THE OWNER of the property
or the structures thereon; the president is a TEMPORARY TENANT whose interventions are LIMITED BY LAW
AND BY RESPECT FOR THE PEOPLE OF THE UNITED STATES.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly A VIOLATION OF THE LAW. It is also a VIOLATION OF THE TRUST OF THE AMERICAN
PEOPLE who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal
and not as a violent fait accompli. Changes to a national historic site should occur through transparent
review, not unilateral action. I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design
review, and public accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward MUST BE
COMPATIBLE IN FORM AND SUBORDINATE IN SCALE to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Jeannette Schlegel
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Susan Farias
body:
I respectfully urge that the rebuilding of the East Wing of the White House remain consistent with the
historic scale, character, and architectural integrity of the existing structure and the broader White House
complex. Any reconstruction should honor the original intent and visual continuity of this nationally
significant site, ensuring that additions or modifications are harmonious rather than expansive or
stylistically incongruous.
At the same time, it is both appropriate and necessary that the East Wing be brought fully into compliance
with current safety standards and accessibility requirements, including ADA guidelines. Modernizing the
building to ensure safety, inclusivity, and functionality is an essential responsibility and should be
accomplished in a way that is sensitive to the historic context.
The East Wing has long served practical and ceremonial roles, including providing workspace for the Office
of the First Spouse and associated staff. Any redesign should continue to accommodate these essential
functions, ensuring that necessary offices and support spaces are included within the plan.
If event or gathering space is deemed necessary, it should be thoughtfully designed within the existing
footprint of the East Wing. Such space should reflect restraint and dignity, avoiding unnecessary expansion
or overly ornate features. The White House is a symbol of democratic governance and shared national
heritage—it should not be treated or presented as a palace.
Above all, the White House belongs to the American people. Any changes to its structures should reflect
stewardship, respect for history, and a commitment to preserving its character for future generations.
Thank you for your consideration.

subject: Written Comments
name: Sara Hobson
body:
To the National Capital Planning Commission:
I was born in Washington, D.C. and I treasure the city, its history and its buildings and monuments.
I was appalled to see the demolition of the East Wing in October 2025. I oppose the construction of a
90,000-square-foot ballroom. I want to see the faithful reconstruction of the historic East Wing.
President Trump described his plans for a ballroom to reporters on July 31, 2025. "It'll be built over on the
east side," the President said. "It won't interfere with the current building." This was not true. The
bulldozers demolished the entire East Wing less than three months later. No permits for the demoliton or
asbestos abatement were obtained. Much of the debris from the destruction of the East Wing was dumped
at East Potomac Park Golf Links, with no concern for the environmental impact of the potentially hazardous
materials that may have been contained in the structure. The park is in a flood plain, and the soil and debris
can be washed into the river and sent downstream. The fact that there were no permits sought or issued
for a government project on a government building is incomprehensible.
There is no need to build a garish White House ballroom. Tricia Nixon and Edward Cox were married in the
White House Rose Garden with a reception for 400 guests in the East Room. Princess Diana famously
danced with John Travolta in the Entrance Hall of the East Wing during a gala dinner celebrating the first
visit of the Prince and Princess of Wales to the United States in the Reagan Administration. The White
House has hosted 19 weddings and more than 300 state dinners, all without a ballroom.
Furthermore, many of the companies and individuals listed as donors to the $400 million project have
significant business interests before this Administration, which raises the obvious issue of whether the
donors are buying favor with the Administration with their donations.
The merging of a private construction project on a public building means that there may be no bidding on
any of the construction contracts, no input on the architectural design, no oversight of even the smallest
light fixture in the new ballroom. The only decision maker will be the man whose name will be engraved on
the Donald J. Trump White House Ballroom.
Harry Truman presided over a White House renovation project from 1948 to 1952 because the White House
was found to be structurally unsound and was in imminent danger of collapsing. The Truman era renovation
preserved the building's exterior while updating its plumbing and electrical systems and rebuilding the
interior with steel beams.
President Trump's destruction of the East Wing is completely different. It sets a dangerous precedent for all
future presidents who decide to remake the White House. There will be no guardrails on any demolitions or
additions that future presidents want to undertake.
President Trump, like all presidents, is a temporary tenant in the People's House. If any other tenant
bulldozed part of the building in which he or she resided, they would face immediate eviction and would
have to pay damages to the landlord. In this case, those damages are owed to the American people. The
East Wing must be rebuilt and the White House must be restored to its former historic glory.
Sincerely, Sara Hobson
Cincinnati, OH

subject: Written Comments
name: Meg Hoover
body:
I grew up in Northern Virginia and had the pleasure of being able to visit and tour the White House (the
People's House) including during the Christmas season. Every visit always included the East Wing. I was
skeptical when the first announcement was made regarding a planned ballroom. I, unfortunately, believed
the President that the East Wing would be untouched by the planned construction of a ballroom. I was
heartbroken the day the unannounced demolition began. I could hardly believe my eyes. Part of our
Nation's History destroyed and gone forever. I understand throughout the years changes have been made,
and structural modifications may be needed to maintain the integrity of such a landmark. I don't
understand how something of this scale and magnitude could happen without some approval or at least
comment/oversite by Congress. I also do not understand how a "supposed" handful of wealthy donors can
pay for something that belongs to all Americans, rich or poor. How can a donation not be seen as a
potential "payment for favor" to the Executive Branch. I would also like to have some transparency with
regard to the donors. We need a list of donors along with their actual donation amount. Has this money
been received? Is it pledged? Who is managing the financial end of this construction? Where is the
accountability and transparency? What money (taxpayer?) and how much has already been spent? Isn't this
supposed to be the most transparent President? I am happy this lawsuit is going forward. While it cannot
restore the lost East Wing, it might be able to prevent government fraud and abuse. Thankfully, I will always
have the memories of my visits to the White House and do not want a ballroom that is not needed nor
wanted. Thank you for the opportunity to comment.

name: Robert Edstrom
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project.
This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
REQUIRED by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts.
This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have
unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

preservation concerns.

permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history. I want this project canceled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design. No one is
above the law and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law would be
an affront to all law-abiding Americans.

should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project as it currently stands, which was initiated without the
proper authorization, permits, or design review. To permit this project to go ahead as currently detailed
sets a dangerous precedent of bulldoze now, get your way later.
I’m saddened that so many First Ladies, who provided the unpaid labor as they supported their husband’s
political careers from their first political race all the way to becoming President, have been so disrespected.
It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American history. I want this project to be
revised into an East Wing rebuild, restoring the East Wing to its former purpose, and updated to meet
modern needs for office flow, comfort, electricity, and security.
I want this project completed with tax dollars, not privately donated funds from individuals or corporations
in order to preserve the sanctity of The People’s House. The White House is not for sale.
I sincerely hope that there is a new understanding and recognition that not every president who is elected
will understand the weight history carries and new protections for our country’s historical properties will be
written and ratified.

name: Zain Orion
body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

name: Chris Kuykendall
body:

zero (0) voters, anywhere in the United States, who voted for him based on a campaign promise from him
to tear down the East Wing and replace it with a ballroom or anything else. The White House, I'm informed,
is a national park. As such, NCPC has authority over construction and renovation at the site. The White
House did not follow the legal requirement of getting advance permit approval for such actions, and offered
bogus justification for pursuing the egregious extent of demolition that's already happened. I agree with
former NCPC chair L. Preston Bryant, Jr., who has said, "If there’s to be demolition, that’s part of the
project.... The demolition element is inherent in the overall project. Demo is not separated from
construction. It’s part of it.” Yes, that's obvious. The NCPC has approval jurisdiction over vertical
construction. The proposed ballroom would be built vertically upward from ground level where the East
Wing has been. The only way to construct vertically from said ground level is via doing an East Wing tear-
down to start with. That is why Mr. Bryant is correct about the non-separation of the commenced
demolition from the contemplated construction. The president and White House are in legal non-
compliance with NCPC protocols.
Moreover, I oppose the ballroom idea, totally. It's just another vanity idea like trying to get Dulles Airport
re-named for him. What Trump and White House want to do, towards glorification of his ego, is a razing of
American history. The project would destroy the architectural balance, the synchronicity, of a West Wing
and East Wing. I want this project canceled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design. No
one is above the law, and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law
would be an affront to all law-abiding Americans.

subject: Written Comments
name: Pamela Muir
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
Additionally there are other options in the area with capacity to accommodate larger numbers of attendees
if necessary.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns. That speaks volumes about the lack of respect for following normal procedures
when a change is being considered.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
I personally think that the East Wing should be rebuilt using the "donors funds". I also oppose the
destruction of the rose garden and hope it will be restored. There's enough concrete in the city.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Ellen Boyne
body:
The following points are why I am TOTALLY AGAINST the tearing down of the East Wing.
Lack of Proper Review and Transparency: Opponents and the National Trust for Historic Preservation
argued the project moved forward without required, legally mandated historic preservation reviews or
approval from the National Capital Planning Commission.
Destruction of Historic Site: The demolition was criticized as a "disrespectful" alteration of a national
landmark, removing the historic space that historically housed offices for First Ladies and their staff.
Scale and Scope: The proposed 90,000-square-foot ballroom was viewed by some as excessive and out of
character for the White House, with concerns it would "dwarf" the existing executive residence.
Questionable Legitimacy and Funding: Critics characterized the funding and approval process as a "Rube
Goldberg" method intended to avoid oversight, raising concerns about opaque private donations.
Process and Procedure: Critics, including former officials, argued that the project was handled without
consulting the public and was contrary to established procedures for altering federal buildings.
Public and Political Opposition: Polls indicated significant opposition, with roughly 61% of independents and
88% of Democrats opposed to the project, calling it a "desecration" of the "People's House".
Critics argued that the project's rapid, "irreversible" nature was a major issue, allowing little room for
proper oversight.

treatment.

reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Dina Schmid
body:
To Whom It May Concern,
I am writing to express my opposition to the proposed “modernization of the East Wing and ballroom
addition” project at the White House.
The White House is not simply a residence or event venue - it is a historic symbol of our democracy. Its
architectural character reflects continuity, restraint, and service. Altering that character in a significant way
risks diminishing the very symbolism that makes it meaningful.
I am particularly concerned about the scale and purpose of adding a ballroom. The White House has never
been defined by grandeur for its own sake. It has stood, instead, as a reminder that the President serves the
public. Its dignity comes from its history, not from expansion.
There is also the matter of cost. At a time when public resources are stretched across pressing national
priorities, investing in a large-scale addition to an already functional historic building feels unnecessary and
misaligned with the spirit of stewardship that this house represents.
The White House is often called “The People’s House.” That phrase matters. Its character should remain
humble, grounded, and historically intact - a visible reminder that leadership in this country is rooted in
service, not spectacle.
I respectfully urge you to reconsider this project and prioritize retuning the East Wing to the size and scope
of what it was prior to demolition.

The White House is not simply a residence or event venue - it is a historic symbol of our democracy. Its 
architectural character reflects continuity, restraint, and service. Altering that character in a significant way 
risks diminishing the very symbolism that makes it meaningful. 
 
I am particularly concerned about the scale and purpose of adding a ballroom. The White House has never 
been defined by grandeur for its own sake. It has stood, instead, as a reminder that the President serves the 
public. Its dignity comes from its history, not from expansion. 
 
There is also the matter of cost. At a time when public resources are stretched across pressing national 
priorities, investing in a large-scale addition to an already functional historic building feels unnecessary and 
misaligned with the spirit of stewardship that this house represents. 
 
The White House is often called “The People’s House.” That phrase matters. Its character should remain 
humble, grounded, and historically intact - a visible reminder that leadership in this country is rooted in 
service, not spectacle. 
 
I respectfully urge you to reconsider this project and prioritize retuning the East Wing to the size and scope 
of what it was prior to demolition.

subject: Written Comments
name: Phoebe Lantz
body:
The East Wing was destroyed in the whim of the president to make way for a new state ballroom funded
largely by private donors. There was no review at all. I oppose this demolition of the White House East Wing
because changes to a national historic site should occur through transparent review, not unilateral action.
Additionally, this $300M project (and growing) is being funded by large private donations at the behest of
the sitting president which creates, at the very least, the appearance of influence-seeking and undermines
public trust.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project. And
please, please, no gilding!

subject: Written Comments
name: Gretchen Ziobro
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Deborah Zimmerman
body:
I am a land use and environmental attorney who has practiced nationally for more than 45 years.
It is a slap in the face to the entire country to call demolition of a significant part of the White House a
"modernization project." Complete demolition does not constitute modernization. It is simply destruction.
In this case, the destruction was accomplished in haste, without mandatory permits or evaluation of its
impacts on the publicly owned White House complex. After more than 45 years of advising clients on
compliance with federal preservation, planning, and environmental laws, I can testify that demolition of the
East Wing was undertaken in violation of law. Worse yet, it was undertaken in flagrant and knowing
violation of applicable laws and procedures. There is no question that a private property owner would be
charged with intentional violation of law under similar circumstances and appropriately subject to criminal
penalties.
The destruction violated a long list of federal statutes and regulations:
1. The President is not unilaterally entitled to demolish any federal properties, especially historic properties,
without following proper procedures. In this case, the President followed NO procedures whatsoever, after
publicly declaring the East Wing "would not be touched." In other words, the President undertook to
demolish property he does not own, and over which he does not exercise sole dominion, in the direct face
of his public assurances. In normal circumstances, the demolition company that acted at his behest would
also be subject to criminal penalties for failing to make sure the demolition project had appropriate
permits.
2. The President failed to comply with NEPA, NHPA, and the Capital Planning Commission requirements in
demolishing the East Wing and proposing to construct a new building with NO public review, based solely
on his personal desire for a mammoth and unnecessary ballroom. So, demolition of the East Wing was a
criminal act and any replacement must comply with all planning requirements. It cannot be stated strongly
enough that the White House complex does not belong to any single occupant, but it is the property of the
people of the United States. It must be treated as any other federally owned historic property. It is a
travesty to allow a single occupant to make significant changes, including demolition, without consulting
and obtaining the approval of the people's representatives.
3. To the extent the East Wing "modernization project" consists of a new ballroom, whether the President's
current design or any other design, it requires full review by ALL regulatory and review bodies. It must be
evaluated in terms of whether it is compatible with the remaining portions of the White House complex,
will meet existing unmet needs for both office and entertaining space.
4. Based on publically available information, there is no need for a ballroom of the size proposed by the
current President. The existing space has served the country well for more than 200 years. It is nonsense to
assert a deficiency because some events are hosted in tents, much like the most high-end parties and
weddings in the world. It is simply self=aggrandizement for the current President to insist on unnecessary
improvements for the sole purpose of self-aggrandizement.
5. Final plans have not been submitted for review as is required by the same requirements applicable to all
federally owned properties. There has also been no assessment of whether the office space destroyed willy-
nilly at the President's covert command is actually necessary and best provided at the location of the East
Wing. Public information demonstrating the need for a new ballroom has not been provided or assessed.
The White House and associated outbuildings have served the people of the United States for more than
200 years. Carefully planned and reviewed additions have been constructed in accordance with law
applicable at the time. The NCPC must apply the same standards to the unpermitted and deceitful
demolition of the East Wing and all replacement proposals as applicable to any and all other federally-
owned properties. The transient wishes of a single occupant of the White House cannot be allowed to
override the interest of all Americans in the future of their properties.
I look forward to the NCPC's decision to penalize the unpermitted destruction of the historic East Wing and
to thoroughly analyze any replacement in accordance with the laws applicable to all Americans. Please
notify me of all future actions or decisions.
Thank you.

subject: Written Comments
name: Jennifer Odlum
body:
The redesign and development of the White House East Wing and new ballroom should have followed
rigorous, transparent, and lawful procedures because the White House is not simply an office building — it
is a national symbol, a historic landmark, and a public trust.
I am deeply bothered by the fact that no such procedure or architectural or historical review took place. But
I implore the governing bodies to hold ground and insist on fully participating in any further design
planning.
First, the White House complex represents the continuity of American democracy. Alterations to such a
symbol should reflect careful stewardship rather than expediency. Proper procedures — including
architectural review, historic preservation assessment, and appropriate congressional oversight where
required — ensure that decisions respect both heritage and future generations.
Second, procedural rigor protects institutional legitimacy. When development decisions follow established
legal and administrative processes, they reinforce public confidence that even the most powerful
institutions operate under rules, not preferences. That principle is foundational to constitutional
governance.
Third, thoughtful planning ensures functional excellence. The East Wing houses critical offices and public-
facing operations. Structured review processes help balance security, operational needs, historical
preservation, cost control, and accessibility — all of which require deliberate coordination rather than ad
hoc decision-making.
Finally, process is not obstruction; it is protection. It protects taxpayers, preserves history, maintains
security standards, and upholds the credibility of the presidency itself.
In short, adherence to proper procedures in redesigning the East Wing is not merely bureaucratic formality
— it is an affirmation that America’s most visible institution remains governed by law, stewardship, and
accountability.

vetted for capability. This will also ensure public funds are used properly and all appropriate codes and
building standards are met.

body:
I oppose any further work on the East Wing Modernization Project, which is a vanity project for the
president. I have seen no evidence that the shocking destruction of a portion of the White House was the
result of any serious considered thought about the needs of the building, the government, or the American
people. In fact everything I have read suggests the opposite. That it is allegedly “privately funded” only
alarms me further when I look at the list of contributors to date. We do not need Mega Businesses paying
extortions to protect their future business interests because the president has created an unsafe and
unstable environment in which to conduct business. Too few Americans realize what is at risk with this
model. The project needs to be suspended and go back to square one and go through the process of
determining if an event pace is needed and if so, what the actual requirements and purposes are.
Personally I am in favor of rebuilding the East Wing funded by the contributions already in the pot. If there
is generally a need for an event space, then architecturally it should fit in with the White House and not
remotely like any of the garish unsuitable drawings that have been made public. Also, many of us would like
an accounting from the president of what happened to the art and artifacts that were in the East Wing.
THANK YOU FOR YOUR ATTENTION TO THIS MATTER.

subject: Written Comments
name: Geraldine Lipov
body:
I am devastated by the destruction of the East Wing of the White House, and more so by the planned
ballroom to take it's place. My career was in government service, and we all had to abide by laws and
regulations. They don't always make sense on a superficial level, but there's good reason for them. In this
instance, every possible safeguard was ignored. The East Wing was torn down without notice to anyone.
The ballroom design has not been approved by anyone. The White House belongs to all of us, and to
destroy it without input or review is willful ignorance. What are you going to do now that it's gone? is the
attitude. In the meantime, the President has said his friends are paying the $300 million to build the ball
room. First, there's an imminent conflict of interest and second, Congress has the role of creating the
budget. This so called ball room is a monstronsity. Its scale is obnoxious as part of the White House. Please
stop this project cold and require the appropriate reviews and clearances before the East Wing is rebuilt, to
scale, within a reasonable budget, and updated as necessary. As a young woman, I walked by the East Wing
every day on my way to work. It made me proud to know what the White House represents. I'd like to think
that another young person walking by today will be impressed and grateful for all that the White House
means to American citizens as well as the world at large. Thank you for your consideration. Geraldine Lipov

without going through proper channels. I am writing to ask you, as members of the NCPC, ensure that East

addition would not extend beyond the footprint of the original East Wing so as to maintain the structure's
balance. Finally, plans for completing this project should be reviewed like any other project undertaken by
past administrations.
Regards, Carol

name: Alice Parcel
body:
Please do not let this project continue, it was not necessary and is only a vanity project of the current
administration. It does not serve the people in any way. Only serves those that have the wealth and
prestige to be gathered it. From the inception the normal and formal rules to alter a national heritage have
been discarded and dismissed as pointless in the urgency to build the addition. All projects require specific
requirements relating to the land, water, power resources prior to actual teardown of the structure and
building of a new structure. This was not done. Any homeowner knows this when planning to remodel.
With the White House itself being a representation of our country there is more to be paid attention to. The
White House represents the "temporary" home of any President, past and future. It is not owned by any
President. A President is only a renter. No renter has the right to come in and tear down part of the house
another owns. Nor can they sell it to another party. I feel that the current President has done that, by using
donations of mixed types which are meant to curry favors from our President. The project has a projected
cost that is much larger than originally stated. Whether the extra costs is due to lack of forethought or
mismanagement is worth more than a nod of the head. I expect our government to be better and wiser
than they have been. To have more respect for the long history of the residence, the President, the people
and our country. The U.S.A. is not expected to compete with a foreign country, we do not need to have a
residence of a Sultan. We need to know that our government is not isolated from the common man or
woman. The amount of money spent so far gives no respect to the problems of those who are hungry, sick,
homeless, or jobless. It does not fix infrastructures, educate, or make life better. It is only a vanity, lustfull
thing. There is no respect from a government that caters to such projects. There is no glory nor rich history
in the plan. Just a building that hogs the property, built bigger and grander than the White House itself. In
fact, I don't see any planning. Just a scene out of an old Little Rascals episode where the kids decide to put
on show. No concern about the plan, just the doing. The White House is like that now, a decision was made,
walls torn down, ground dug up. No permission was given, no codes to follow. And unlike the Little Rascals
the costs and liability is so much greater. And so far with no approval by any government official or office. I
expect our government to stand up and say, "Wait a minute, there is a responsibility to procedure" A
responsibility to the country and it's people. Despite all of the current President's urgency we cannot allow
to disrespect the history of the White House. I expect Congress to put the halt on the project, to downscale
it in the minimum. It is past time for Congress to stop walking on glass. Restore the White House at the
current President's own cost. He was not acting for the country and it's people. Only in his own interest to
one-up other heads of countries. Restore our White House.

You Have Until March 4th to Comment on Trump’s White House Ballroom
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.
Thank you for your attention to this matter!
Deborah Stephenson
Registered Voter and Taxpayer

subject: Written Comments
name: Patrick Moore
body:
The proposed East Wing Modernization Project is being framed as progress — but progress without
transparency, fiscal restraint, and public trust is not progress at all. It is mission drift.
Modernization, in theory, sounds responsible. In practice, we have to ask: modernization for whom? At
what cost? And at what moment?
We are living in a time of deep public skepticism about institutions. Communities are asking for
accountability, not expansion. Families are tightening budgets. Essential services in cities and counties
across the country remain underfunded. Infrastructure, housing, education, and public safety all compete
for limited dollars. To move forward with a large-scale modernization project in this climate sends the
wrong signal: that aesthetics or administrative convenience take precedence over urgent human need.
Prescience requires us to look beyond ribbon cuttings and architectural renderings. It requires us to
consider long-term operating costs, security implications, and the precedent it sets. Once expanded,
bureaucracies rarely contract. Once funds are committed, they are rarely redirected to community
priorities.
This isn’t opposition to improvement. It’s opposition to misplaced priorities.
True leadership asks:
• Is this the most responsible use of public resources right now?
• Have we fully explored renovation over expansion?
• Have we meaningfully invited public input, or simply announced a decision?
Modernization without moral clarity becomes excess. Expansion without humility becomes arrogance.
At a time when trust in institutions is fragile, the most powerful statement leaders could make is restraint
— choosing stewardship over spectacle, substance over symbolism.
The East Wing does not need modernization nearly as much as our communities need investment. And
history will not judge us by how polished our buildings were, but by how wisely we chose to serve the
people beyond their walls.

attention to its previous size and style- this preserves the character and cultural significance of our house.

body:
Calling the East Wing project of modernization is a misnomer. It should be called a desecration. There was a
way to modernize without tearing down the historic East Wing.
My mother's family has been in Washington DC for generations, on Capitol Hill and also Anacostia area. I
would walk the Mall, and spent so much time in the National Gallery and the Smithsonian, soaking in the
glorious history of our country and it's connection to so many beautiful things. I even worked for the
Architect of the Capitol for a short period of time. I love DC deep inside. And to raze a historical building like
the East Wing is just a desecration. There is no other word for it. Because what are we if we do not hold the
history of our country sacred?

Calling the East Wing project of modernization is a misnomer. It should be called a desecration. There was a 
way to modernize without tearing down the historic East Wing.  
My mother's family has been in Washington DC for generations, on Capitol Hill and also Anacostia area. I 
would walk the Mall, and spent so much time in the National Gallery and the Smithsonian, soaking in the 
glorious history of our country and it's connection to so many beautiful things. I even worked for the 
Architect of the Capitol for a short period of time. I love DC deep inside. And to raze a historical building like 
the East Wing is just a desecration. There is no other word for it. Because what are we if we do not hold the 
history of our country sacred?

subject: Written Comments
name: Kathy Fiebig
body:
The East Wing was razed without any permits, without any input from the National Trust for Historic
Preservation, and without any respect for the building's history. No plans were submitted and there was no
design review. This was a travesty. I strongly oppose spending any taxpayer money on this other than to
restore it or at the very least, rebuild a functional wing. Nor do I want to see private "donations" used to
build a monument to the current President. We don't need a $300 ballroom.
Thank you.

subject: Written Comments
name: Alicia Markham Morris
body:
Growing up as the child of an architect, working on the crew of a historic preservation project as a young
adult, and now teaching history, I have always had an appreciation for America's historic places. I
remember working on the site of a residential home in Charleston, SC and being visited by the BAR folks,
dressed to the nines and poking around, asking if we were going to put the original bricks back in the wall
just so—as they were concerned that we were not following protocol. Today, I live in a neighborhood built
in the 1990s, and I am asked to write up a proposal and get the signatures of all of my neighbors if I want to
change the color of my front door. Clearly, I understand and recognize the importance and value of proper
authorization, permits, and design review for ANY building project. In the case of the destruction of the
White House, which is supposed to be the People's House, not the President's house, and certainly not a

body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

name: Margaret MacDonald-Alfoni
body:
To the Members of the National Capital Planning Commission:
I am writing to submit public comment regarding the proposed East Wing modernization and the addition
of a 90,000-square-foot ballroom to the White House.
While the demolition of the East Wing is deeply concerning in its own right, the proposal to construct a
ballroom of this scale is even more troubling. The White House is the people’s house. It carries immense
historical significance and deep sentimental value for Americans across the country. A project of this
magnitude risks undermining the character and integrity of a building that symbolizes our nation’s history
and democratic traditions.
In my view, such a large and ostentatious addition is neither necessary nor reflective of the public interest. I
urge you to carefully consider the historical importance of this site and the broader public sentiment as you
deliberate on this proposal.
The ballroom addition should be viewed unfavorably. I remain hopeful that, in the future, the East Wing
space can be restored or replaced in a manner that is more appropriate to the dignity and heritage of the
White House.
Margaret H. MacDonald-Alfoni

magnitude risks undermining the character and integrity of a building that symbolizes our nation’s history 
and democratic traditions.

urge you to carefully consider the historical importance of this site and the broader public sentiment as you 
deliberate on this proposal. 
 
The ballroom addition should be viewed unfavorably. I remain hopeful that, in the future, the East Wing 
space can be restored or replaced in a manner that is more appropriate to the dignity and heritage of the 
White House. 
 
 
Margaret H. MacDonald-Alfoni

White House will be overshadowed with the size of the proposed ballroom. We ask that this project be
halted and all historic and federal regulations be considered.

subject: Written Comments
name: Jennifer Huber
body:
The White House is 55,000 sf. The proposed addition is almost double that size at 90,000 sf. Funds were
"privately raised, or so the American people are told. My comments:
- Any addition to the White House should never dwarf the original structure. The size of the "ballroom" is
unnecessarily excessive and will diminish the historic structure and symbolism of the People's House. I am
saddened that this project was allowed to move forward without Congressional approval nor input from the
American people. The damage is done and there should be consequences for the rushed and thoughtless
demolition of our history.
- It is unlikely that this project will cost only $400k. Rarely does a capital project finish on-time or on-budget.
How will the cost overruns, caused by change orders, add alternates, and schedule slips, be funded? Were
all trades included in the $400k budget estimate? Security, IT, FF&E? If not, what is the budget for items
that are not covered by the $400k? How would any additional expenses/cost overruns be funded? Will
congressional approval be required to obtain any additional funding?
- What will this project cost the taxpayers of the United States of America?

subject: Written Comments
name: Kathleen Yancey
body:
Demolishing the historic East Wing of the White House without following the appropriate and required
processes--review, permits, and Congressional oversight--is a clear violation of the law, as visible as the ugly
destruction of this wing of the White House is now. Our White House, the people's house, is both a National
Historic Landmark and a National Park. We, the American people, own it. Full stop.
I urge you, the members of the National Capital Planning Commission, to speak for us, for the people. I ask
that you require any reconstruction of the East Wing to maintain it historic design and size and to exhibit a
design integrity aligned with our best aspirations. If a new structure is to be built, it must match the style of
the original structure of the Executive Mansion, and it must be subordinate in size.
Regarding the funding of this project that we are now forcued to design, implement, and complete: it
should be resourced only with appropriations from Congress after Congress approves the new design. No
private money be allowed for this project. We, the American people. own the land, not any one president
or any corporation seeking to buy favor.
Should Congress fail to approve funding, and if a design keeping with the building's historical character
cannot be achieved, the land should be left vacant.
Please do not reward a lawless president; please speak for us, all of us.
Thank you.

subject: Written Comments
name: Simon Berman
body:
We are responsible to those who follow us, and we have a moral obligation to leave them a country that
allows them to feel and absorb what has come before them. We do not want to be remembered for
arbitrarily destroying a delicate piece of their legacy that was a gentle symbol of the American stability we
grew up with, and then quickly replacing it with an out of proportion showpiece. It might be senseless to
recreate the East Wing exactly as it was, but a replacement of similar scale and architectural sensitivity that
evokes the original, perhaps with improved functionality, would help preserve the balance and symbolism
of the site. As for the enormous ballroom, it creates a dissonance with its surroundings that seems to reflect
the dissonance that America has created with its international community.
The America I grew up in (I am 81) always seemed to be run in a deliberative way. Its processes were not
always perfect, but there seemed to be a good faith effort to drive us toward being a better place. When I
witnessed the bulldozers suddenly appearing without notice I felt like I was living in another country where
trust in leadership had been lost. There is now an opportunity for this Commission to restore some of that
trust.

in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

determine whether to go ahead and if so, how to create a plan that will work for our taxpayers. A

government. I am devastated that the East Wing was torn down without authorization and a process to
engage all of the stakeholders, including taxpayers, in determining if the changes were welcome and if so,
how to do them in a way that reflects our country's values and commitment to Democracy.

body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Mary Margaret Kirby
body:
Dear NCP Commission,
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional
authorization and completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral
authority to demolish historic structures without following the law.
Thank you.
Sincerely,
Mary Margaret Kirby

subject: Written Comments
name: Jordan Gitelman
body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: lyn lapel
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Denise Campana
body:
I am writing to express my strenuous objection to the proposed construction of a ballroom attached to the
White House. As a taxpayer, I find the allocation of public funds for such a project to be an egregious lapse
in fiscal responsibility.
My objections are based on the following points:
Misallocation of Taxpayer Funds: At a time when the nation faces significant economic challenges, spending
millions on a luxury entertainment space is out of touch with the needs of the American people.
Historical Integrity: The White House is a national monument. Altering its architectural footprint for a non-
essential addition risks compromising the historical and aesthetic value of the site.
Maintenance and Overheads: Beyond the initial construction costs, a facility of this scale will require
permanent staffing, climate control, and maintenance— all of which will continue to drain public resources
indefinitely.
While I understand the need for the Executive Branch to host official functions, the existing facilities and
nearby historical venues are more than sufficient. I urge the administration and Congress to prioritize
essential public services and infrastructure over the creation of a private gala space.
I request that this statement be included in the official record regarding this proposal.

subject: Written Comments
name: Niels Karwatzki
body:
Hello, I am Niels, a student from Germany. I highly commend President Trump’s ambition to construct
something so magnificent for his country. From my perspective, this project could serve as a global
exemplar, demonstrating that classical beauty in architecture is still achievable in the modern era.
Compared to the austerity of modernist new-builds, the proposed Ballroom is truly impressive.
From an external viewpoint, it appears that many Americans and media outlets dismiss the project on
principle simply because of its association with President Trump. Many would likely oppose an expansion
even half this size, despite the fact that hosting state receptions in temporary tents is quite frankly
unworthy of a nation of the United States' stature. Most European nations and many others possess dozens
of buildings in every regional capital that are far more representative and grand.
I wish this endeavor every success and would like to offer a few specific technical observations for the
Board’s consideration. In my view, the White House has historically lacked harmony due to the disparate
styles of the current West Wing and the former East Wing. The proposed new East Wing—and perhaps a
corresponding West Wing in the coming decades—could permanently rectify this by creating a symmetrical
and cohesive ensemble, provided the proportions are precise. Much like classical European palaces or
manor houses with multiple wings, it could be designed to look as though it had been planned this way
from the beginning.
Architectural Recommendations:
Fenestration and Symmetry: I believe the current design of the north facade, featuring five windows plus
two additional flanking windows, is not optimal. While the two extra windows successfully reduce the
perceived width of the building, I suggest utilizing a 4 (+2) window configuration. Since the Main Residence
features four windows per side (excluding those obscured by the North Portico), a 4 (+2) arrangement for
the Ballroom would achieve perfect architectural symmetry. This could be accomplished by slightly
adjusting the intercolumniation (window spacing) or by a marginal reduction in length of no more than two
meters.
Proportions and Massing: There is a slight disproportion regarding the length. Even if a matching West Wing
were built in the future, the proportions would not yet mirror the balance found in classical three-wing
manor houses. Shortening the wing to align with the terminus of the Treasury Building—perhaps by opting
for a single-row South Portico—would be highly effective. Given that there is only one story beneath it, the
loss of interior space would be negligible. Furthermore, it should be evaluated whether an eight-column
configuration (matching the south side of the Treasury Building) would be more aesthetically pleasing.
The Rose Garden Staircase: To preserve the symmetry of the two Rose Gardens, the Board might consider
relocating the grand staircase. Rather than placing it directly in the garden, it could run adjacent to the
colonnade, originating from the corner of the Ballroom terrace. This would result in a more understated
and integrated appearance.
The South Facade and Portico: I suggest replacing the current grand staircase with a double-flight staircase
(similar to the McCrery design) situated beneath the portico. This would provide covered terraces on both
levels and reduce the overall footprint. This configuration would also allow for the integration of the side
terrace with the portico stairs, potentially eliminating the need for the smaller lateral staircase.
Regarding the height, the alignment with the Main Residence is excellent, as is the design of the West and
East facades, including the mirroring of the Treasury Building’s portico.
With best regards from Germany,
Niels

name: Ben Jay
body:
FORMAL OPPOSITION TO THE EAST WING MODERNIZATION PROJECT
Re: Recent Demolition and Proposed Replacement of the White House East Wing
I. Opening Statement
I write in firm and unequivocal opposition to the project known as the "East Wing Modernization," which is,
in truth, no modernization at all — but the deliberate and willful demolition of a piece of American history
that belongs not to any single administration, but to every citizen of the United States of America, and to
every generation yet to come.
This project must be stopped. Those who authorized it without legal standing must be held accountable.
And the East Wing must be fully rebuilt and restored to its former design, at the expense of those who
destroyed it.
II. This Is Not Modernization — It Is Erasure
Let us be honest about what this project actually is. The White House East Wing is a historic structure of
immense cultural, architectural, and civic significance. It has served the American people for generations —
as a workplace, a symbol, and a living piece of national heritage. To raze it in order to construct a private
ballroom, however lavishly funded, is not an act of improvement. It is an act of desecration.
A ballroom funded by tech billionaires does not belong in the White House. It belongs in a private estate, a
hotel, or a corporate campus. The people's house is not a venue for the ambitions of the ultra-wealthy. Its
architecture is not raw material for personal vanity projects. The East Wing was not theirs to touch.
III. Flagrant Violations of Law and Due Process
This project was initiated without proper authorization, without the required permits, and without the
mandatory design review processes that govern changes to historic federal structures. These are not
bureaucratic technicalities — they are legal safeguards deliberately established to protect the American
public from precisely this kind of unilateral, self-serving action.
The National Historic Preservation Act, the Preservation of Historic and Archaeological Data Act, and the
protocols of the National Trust for Historic Preservation exist for a reason. They exist because our shared
history is fragile, irreplaceable, and too important to be left to the whims of whoever happens to hold
power at a given moment. Those laws were violated. There must be consequences.
No president, no billionaire donor, no administration has the authority to unilaterally demolish a protected
historic federal structure. If this project is allowed to proceed — or worse, to be ratified after the fact — it
will set a devastating precedent: that the most powerful can simply bulldoze the law along with the
buildings.
IV. Private Funding Is Not a License to Destroy Public Property
It has been argued, or implied, that the involvement of private funding — reportedly in the range of $300
million — somehow legitimizes this project. It does not. Private money cannot purchase the right to destroy
public heritage. The White House and its historic components are the property of the American people,
held in public trust. They are not for sale, not for renovation at a donor's discretion, and not available as a
canvas for the aesthetics of whoever writes the largest check.
The appearance of private funding, in this context, does not reduce the public harm — it compounds it. It
raises serious questions about the nature of the relationship between the administration and those funding
this project, and whether the White House itself is being offered as a vehicle for their influence.
V. The National Trust for Historic Preservation Deserves Our Full Support
The National Trust for Historic Preservation has stood as a principled, courageous defender of this nation's
architectural and cultural legacy. Its intervention here is not merely procedurally appropriate — it is morally
necessary. The Trust is fighting not just for a building, but for the rule of law, for the integrity of our shared
civic institutions, and for the principle that history is not the property of the powerful.
Every American who values the preservation of our history, every citizen who believes in accountability, and
every person who understands that the law must apply equally to all — regardless of title or wealth —
should support the Trust's efforts and submit their own comment to this Commission before the March 4
deadline.
VI. Demands for Accountability and Restoration
I call upon the National Capital Planning Commission and all relevant federal authorities to take the
following actions:
1. Immediately halt and cancel the East Wing Modernization project in its entirety.
2. Require the full reconstruction and restoration of the East Wing to its original, historically accurate
design.
3. Compel those responsible for authorizing this illegal demolition to reimburse the Federal Government for
the full cost of reconstruction.
4. Initiate a full investigation into the legal violations committed in connection with this project, including
the bypassing of required permits, authorizations, and historic preservation review processes.
5. Ensure that no private funding arrangement —  past, present, or future — is permitted to override the
legal protections governing historic federal structures.
VII. Closing
No one is above the law. Not a president. Not a billionaire. Not an administration that believes its power
exempts it from the obligations every other American must meet. To allow this project to proceed
unchallenged and unpunished would be an affront to every law-abiding citizen, every taxpayer, and every
American who has ever placed their hand over their heart at the sight of the White House and felt, however
briefly, that this is the people's house.
It must be stopped. It must be reversed. And those responsible must be held accountable.
The East Wing belongs to America. Give it back.
Respectfully submitted,
Ben Jay
A Concerned American Citizen

subject: Written Comments
name: A Koos Fox
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
Allison Koos Fox

subject: Written Comments
name: Sigrid Berg
body:
Good morning,
I am writing as a US citizen and as someone who lived and worked in the DC area for a number of years,
often walking/biking/driving past the White House, to request that plans for a large ballroom in place of the
demolished East Wing be denied, and that if necessary for national security to rebuild something there to
allow a bunker to be in place underneath, that it be rebuilt in a respectful, historically accurate fashion, and
in such a way that it does not overwhelm architecturally the main building of the White House.
Many thanks in advance for your consideration.
Sigrid Berg
Belfast, Maine

subject: Written Comments
name: Steve Havilanf
body:
1. Questionable Priorities in a Time of Fiscal Strain
The United States is operating under persistent federal deficits and a national debt exceeding $30 trillion. In
that context, allocating tens of millions of dollars to modernize administrative office space attached to the
Executive Mansion raises legitimate concerns about fiscal stewardship.
Even if the funds are drawn from private donations (as some White House renovations historically have
been), federal oversight, security, and logistical costs inevitably involve taxpayer resources. Major federal
projects rarely confine their true cost to the headline construction figure. Security modifications, temporary
relocations, and interagency coordination often drive total costs significantly higher.
At a time when:
• Veterans’ healthcare systems face backlog challenges
• Infrastructure repair across the country remains underfunded
• Border and disaster response budgets are strained
Spending on executive office aesthetic or structural upgrades risks appearing disconnected from national
priorities.
\u11835 ?
2. Optics and Public Trust
The East Wing houses offices for the First Lady and staff. While functional improvements may be justified,
large-scale modernization projects attached to the White House carry unavoidable symbolic weight.
The White House is not merely a building — it is a national symbol. Any major renovation, especially during
periods of economic hardship for many Americans, risks reinforcing perceptions of elite insulation from
everyday financial pressures.
Public trust in institutions is fragile. High-profile modernization projects tied to executive spaces can be
interpreted as self-serving, regardless of intent. That perception alone warrants heightened scrutiny.
\u11835 ?
3. Historic Preservation Concerns
The White House complex is a historically significant site. Preservation of architectural integrity is overseen
in part by bodies such as the National Park Service and other preservation authorities.
Large modernization projects risk:
• Altering historically significant design elements
• Introducing contemporary architectural features inconsistent with original intent
• Setting precedents for further structural expansion
The White House has undergone renovations before (Truman’s full structural reconstruction being the most
dramatic example), but those were driven by structural necessity. A modernization driven by administrative
convenience is a far weaker justification.
\u11835 ?
4. Executive Creep and Institutional Expansion
Federal institutions have a long history of incremental physical and bureaucratic expansion. What begins as
“modernization” often evolves into footprint growth, expanded staffing, and permanent operational
scaling.
Critics may argue that:
• Executive branch administrative infrastructure continues to grow regardless of efficiency claims.
• Renovation projects can normalize expanding executive operations rather than streamlining them.
• Modernization may entrench structures that could instead be reevaluated for consolidation or reduction.
A renovation is not neutral — it commits the institution to maintaining that expanded or reconfigured
footprint long-term.
\u11835 ?
5. Transparency and Accountability
Major public-facing projects demand:
• Full cost disclosure
• Detailed architectural plans
• Clear articulation of necessity
• Competitive contracting transparency
Without comprehensive disclosure, skepticism is reasonable. The public deserves clarity on:
• Total lifecycle cost
• Private vs. public funding proportions
• Security cost implications
• Long-term operational savings (if any)
Absent demonstrable efficiency gains or structural necessity, modernization risks being categorized as
discretionary rather than essential.
\u11835 ?
6. The Burden of Justification
The White House complex is already among the most secure and maintained government facilities in the
country. Therefore, the burden of proof lies heavily on proponents of modernization to demonstrate:
• Structural deficiency
• Security necessity
• Cost-neutral efficiency gains
• Critical operational bottlenecks
If modernization is primarily aesthetic, symbolic, or comfort-driven, it fails the test of responsible
governance.
\u11835 ?
Conclusion
The East Wing modernization project is not controversial because construction is inherently wrong. It is
controversial because it involves:
• A national symbol
• Significant cost
• Executive branch facilities
• Optics during fiscal and social strain
In a democracy facing debt pressure, declining institutional trust, and competing infrastructure needs, even
defensible executive projects must clear a very high bar.
If modernization cannot be demonstrated as structurally necessary, fiscally disciplined, and operationally
indispensable, opposition is not partisan — it is a principled defense of priority alignment, symbolism, and
responsible governance.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kit Keller
body:
The White House complex is one of the most historically significant sites in the United States. Although the
East Wing is not as old as the main residence, its modern form dates to the 1940s and reflects wartime and
postwar expansions of the presidency. It houses offices for the First Lady and staff and has been part of
many major historical moments and public events. Preservationists argue that each structural era of the
White House tells part of the story of the presidency and American governance.
Historians and architects argue for preserving rather than demolishing historic government structures. Even
later additions like the East Wing contribute to the architectural evolution of the executive complex.
Demolition sets a precedent for removing other historically significant additions when renovation might
suffice.
The White House is owned by the federal government and managed primarily by the National Park Service
(NPS), with operational control shared with the Executive Office of the President.
No single president can unilaterally order demolition of part of the structure. Major structural changes
require coordination among:
NPS (which maintains the building and grounds)
The White House Office of the Curator
The General Services Administration (GSA)
A demolition plan should trigger a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review, to make environmental
assessments or impact statements.
It has not been made clear that the appropriate legal steps have been taken, even though the demolition
process is under way. The appropriate channels must be followed before any further changes are made to
the East Wing of the White House. It is “The People’s House.”

subject: Written Comments
name: Chaney Delaire
body:
I object to the plans to construct a ballroom at the East Wing. I am just one tiny voice. I hope the U.S.
Commission of Fine Arts (CFA) and the National Capitol Planning Commission receive (NCPC) many
comments similar to mine.
The East Wing has been demolished with little to no oversight nor any environmental review as required by
the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). The White House and grounds are a National Park and a
National Historic Landmark owned by We the People.
This public comment period is a legally required process. According to your website, the public comment
process is one of several safe guards to "ensure transparency, accountability, and meaningful public input".
Major construction projects in DC must be reviewed by NCPC and CFA and they must comply with NEPA as
well as receive congressional approval. The Trump administration has ignored the laws put in place for so
many things, that this ballroom project seems minor in the scheme of things. Still, I am compelled to voice
my opinion. Maybe someday, there will be accountability.
I object to the project for these reasons:
1. The administration should be held accountable for violating NEPA during the demolition. Fines need to be
imposed for this negligence. An investigation is needed to determine the extent of toxic debris that was
hauled away; some of which was deposited onto a nearby public golf course. Since there is ongoing, blatant
disregard for public safety, there needs to be an independent body given the authority to review the
environmental damages, impose and collect fines and monitor the new construction with the authority to
stop all work if further laws are violated.
2. Congress, CFA and NCPC must require full disclosure of funding, determine if there is any violation of the
Emoluments Act or favors granted (quid pro quo) and put in place a fiscal manager appointed by a judge for
the entire project. If this cannot be set in place, the project cannot move forward.
3. There is no need for a 90,000+ square foot ballroom at the White House. Let this empty space be just
that- a place that tells its own story; what it was, and how it was illegally demolished- a monument to how
not to do things.
4. I will repeat- There is no need for a 90,000+ square foot ballroom at the White House. If something is to
be built, let it truly be the "People's House". Build a structure for the people- something that celebrates
who we are, not who the billionaires are. Make it a place where children and families can come to visit-
maybe a revolving Smithsonian exhibit or an arboretum or maybe an art museum (you can never have too
many). Build it to scale so that it doesn't overpower the original White House structure. Include some
meeting rooms and offices but make it something we can all have access to.
Chaney Delaire
Retired urban planner and NEPA consultant

Emoluments Act or favors granted (quid pro quo) and put in place a fiscal manager appointed by a judge for 
the entire project. If this cannot be set in place, the project cannot move forward.

that- a place that tells its own story; what it was, and how it was illegally demolished- a monument to how 
not to do things.

many). Build it to scale so that it doesn't overpower the original White House structure. Include some 
meeting rooms and offices but make it something we can all have access to.

body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
America does not need a ballroom costing hundreds of millions of dollars. America needs healthcare that
works, safety and respect for all people living here, and a functioning rule of law. Please stop this rape of
our national House.
