subject: Written Comments
name: Susan Markley
body:
Thank you for providing an opportunity to comment on the White House "East Wing Modernization". The
complete destruction of the East Wing, allegedly for a fancy gilded ballroom without reviews or approvals,
is not "modernization". It is a shameful action of hubris, an erasure of history, and a costly waste of funds.
The White House is not a palace and does not belong to the elected person serving their term. It is the
'people's house'. It belongs to the people of the United States, and all of the presidents before and after any
single administration. The building and all of the activities that occurred within it are part of history. It is not
and never was meant to be a gilded hall for parties. Updates to maintain or modernize structural elements,
security, plumbing, or electrical infrastructure should always follow unbiased external reviews and
comments, to assure that the whole of the White House and its historic elements are protected. The
demolished East Wing should be restored to its prior configuration.

assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.

approving those contracts.

unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.
The immense overreach of this administration and their illegal acts must not be ignored.

want the East wing restored as it was. Alternatively, I would not be opposed to an addition as long as it 1.

the people of the country to abide by the traditions that have determined the style and substance of the
seat of power for more than two centuries.
Thank you for considering this on your process of decision-making.
Sincerely,
Iana CraneWing

subject: Written Comments
name: Terry Teigen
body:
I'm a lifelong Pacific Northwest resident. I have only been in D.C. a handful of times. Once as part of a clergy
sabbatical, I was fortunnate to spend a week in the Capitol. Three mornings I got up very early, rode public
transportation, and tried to snag a tour of the White House. To no avail. It was far too popular.
When it's said the White House is "The Peoples'" it is not hyperbole or metaphor. It's a fact. Bought,
maintained, treasured by and for all of us.
Any major change to this honored part and expression of our national heritage is, of course, under the
purview of an oversight board.
It is not the property of, and should not be subject to the whims of a particular administration, and certainly
not one person. What has happened to this point is at the least a travesty and a shame. It may be far more
nefarious.
Our capitoll is not Versailles. The White House is not a castle. If someone or some group wants to build a
monument to ostentatious hubris, let them do it on their own dime, their own property, their own time.
Thank you for stopping this insult and folly.
Rev. Terry Teigen
Olympia, Washington

American nation. They did not want a nation where an entitled few held all the wealth and power and the
masses lived lives of endless toil and misery. They wanted no palaces for those leaders. The executive’s
home would be large enough to accommodate the necessary work, but it would not be Versailles. And it
would be called, “The People’s House.”

ballroom would be a monstrosity and a mockery of what America has always been. The “modernization”
project should be halted at once and the White House returned to its previous appearance.

subject: Written Comments
name: Joshua Lessard
body:
As a licensed architect committed to the protection of our shared cultural heritage, I ask that this project
only be allowed to continue with proper authorization, permitting, and required design reviews. The laws
and regulatory frameworks that govern major capital projects, especially those involving historically and
culturally significant public buildings, exist to ensure transparency, accountability, and responsible
stewardship. Circumventing these processes undermines professional standards, erodes public trust, and
sets a dangerous precedent for the treatment of our built heritage. No project, regardless of its scale or
ambition, should be exempt from the legal and ethical obligations that protect the public interest. Thank
you.

subject: Written Comments
name: Karin Zitzewitz
body:
The razing of the East Wing of the White House without regard for proper procedure and without prior
consultation with the planning commission and bodies dedicated to historic preservation was outrageous.
Plans for this project should be placed under a bi-partisan committee of architectural, planning, and art
historical experts who can advise on how the newly built wing can best be designed, built, and function.
Strict scrutiny of the funding of this project must be undertaken in order to prevent any form of influence
peddling. The White House is a national property that is maintained for public use, and should not become
the vanity project of any single occupant.
The author is a professor of art history, but speaks here as a private citizen rather than in her capacity as an
employee of the university.

subject: Written Comments
name: Stanley Grand, Ph.D.
body:
On the proposed new, not “modernized,” East Wing. Project 8733
The North Façade
Prior to its demolition, the East Wing served basically as an outbuilding attached to the White House by
means of a covered walkway. The East Wing was subsumed to the visual primacy of the main building.
Crucially, the roof of the covered corridor was below the sill line of the White House ground floor windows.
Under the proposed new construction, the corridor roof line reaches to the second-floor windows which
totally destroys the aesthetics of the White House east façade much like an unattractive growth on a
beautiful face. The corridor itself now becomes a major visual element elevated above ground level. What
we see is a monotonous string of thirteen blank panels separated by pilasters on bases. The pilasters are
too narrow and rather than suggesting a structural function seem more like the side rails of an empty
picture frame. Even the dentils hanging off the cornice are out of scale and serve more to remind one of a
runny nose than a classical entablature. In sum the corridor is too high and too boring.
The north façade of the new ballroom complex is a blunt instrument that competes with and diminishes the
historic presidential home. Whereas the White House has four bays on either side of its portico, the new
construction has seven bays, five of which are located on the projecting central pavilion. The design
requirement that the cornice match that of the White House results in a prominent and unattractive
basement level. Things become really weird when one turns the corner and sees the column bases of the
east side temple front below the basement level.
The East Façade
On the east façade there’s an octastyle temple front porch accessed by a flight of stairs from street level.
When one thinks of classical and neoclassical architecture, symmetry, balance, and harmony come to mind.
A fine example is just across the street from the proposed East Wing in the Treasury Building. The Shalom
Baranes proposal is more a hodgepodge of elements than anything else. The Temple front is neither
centered nor balanced with the rest of the east façade.
The South Façade
This is a total disaster. Initially this decastyle prostyle Corinthian portico contained a pediment, but
apparently one commissioner thought the pediment too massive, so the architect removed it. The result is
that the façade looks incomplete, similar to the temple of Hera I at Paestum. Decapitating the façade is a
symptom of the rush to get something built.
A temple front with ten columns is a major statement. The Pantheon only has eight for example, whereas
the Lincoln Memorial has twelve. The curved staircase leading to ground level is completely out of
proportion. On the plan it looks like a nineteenth-century moustache.
But the fundamental question is what purpose does this portico serve and the answer is none. Indeed, it
could and should be eliminated altogether. Doing so would greatly improve the eight-window east façade
especially if the wall space between the windows and temple front matched that of the building’s end. I
suppose the south lawn facing temple could be understood as a folly much like those fake classical
structures decorating eighteenth century English gardens and estates, but even so. Scaling back the East
Wing by eliminating this portico would also serve to balance better the South Lawn vista. (Originally the
Oval Office and the demolished East Wing were roughly in line.)
The NCPC continues to describe the project (8733) as East Wing Modernization. The Commission met on
January 8, 2026, for a pre-submission review of the project. The project was not considered at the February
meeting and is on the agenda for the March 5 meeting. The Commission consists of twelve members, seven
of whom are ex-officio. The president has appointed the majority of the voting members: William Schary
(Assistant to the President and WH Staff Secretary), Stuart Levenbach (Associate Director Office of
Management and Budget), and Michael Blair (White House Deputy Chief of Staff). The Mayor appointed
two voting members. The NCPC promises full biographies of the members to come soon. Thus, all the public
knows is that the majority works for and is beholden to the president. According to the NCPC website, the
Commission will consider approving the “preliminary and final site and building plans” on March 5. For
information on how to comment of attend Live Stream see https://www.ncpc.gov/review/meeting/
The motto of the Florentine Grand Duke Cosimo I was “Make haste slowly.” The NCPC and Commission of
Fine Artswould be well advised to do the same.

the people’s house, the White House.

obtain permission from them as well. To my knowledge, this was not done before a wrecking ball
demolished the east wing. It seems to me that this was something down illegally and it certainly doesn’t
benefit the citizens of this nation.
Please stop this project and make whoever gave the ok, reimburse in full the cost of demolition and
reconstruction back to its former historically significant glory.

subject: Written Comments
name: Cheryl Shaw
body:
To the Members of the National Capital Planning Commission:
I am writing to formally express my strong opposition to the expenditure of any funds, reportedly currently
totaling $300 million, on the ballroom project to be built where the East Wing once stood.
The East Wing was an established and historically significant component of the White House complex and,
by extension, of our national heritage. Any action involving its demolition should have been subject to
rigorous review, full transparency, and clear legal authorization. Based on publicly available information,
this project was initiated without proper procedural safeguards, including comprehensive planning
documentation, appropriate review processes, required permits, and presentation to United States
Congress for oversight and funding authorization.
This proposal does not constitute modernization; it represents the complete removal of a historic structure.
Such action warrants the highest level of scrutiny under federal preservation standards and planning
protocols.
It appears driven by personal ego and a desire to leave a self-indulgent, ornamental legacy rather than to
preserve the dignity and integrity of a national landmark.
This project is neither necessary nor supported by a significant majority of the American people. I call for its
immediate cancellation and for the East Wing to be rebuilt and restored to its original design and historical
character.
No individual is above the law. Allowing this project to proceed without accountability would be an affront
to every law-abiding American. A failure to impose consequences for such a blatant disregard of legal
process would undermine the very principles of governance, transparency, and the rule of law that our
institutions are meant to uphold.
Thank you for your consideration and for your role in safeguarding the historic and civic integrity of the
nation’s capital.
Respectfully,
Cheryl Shaw

subject: Written Comments
name: Sheri Ketchum
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.
The National Preservation and Trust procedures should be followed to recreate the East Wing to have
modest improvements in keeping with the proportions of the White House proper. I would add that the
person, who illegally ordered it demolished,
is & should be held solely responsible for the restoration costs. Not donors, not taxpayers.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kristi Hazen
body:
I can not believe that we all woke up to the news of the East Wing of the White House being demolished
after a large portion of the American people publicly expressed their displeasure with the current
administration.
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kim Birck
body:
It is unconscionable for an individual, even the POTUS, to tear down a piece of US history - and the property
of We the People - without going through proper channels.
Demolition absolutely should require a permit as well as the seal of approval from Congress, the
representatives of the People.
The funding mechanism should not make a whit of difference when launching a project of this scale. And
beyond construction costs, the gigantic ballroom planned to take the place of the East Wing offices and
visitor services will need maintenance and heating and cooling in perpetuity, at the expense of taxpayers.
Stop the project right now and bring in experts and historians to decide where we go from here. It may not
make sense to duplicate the old East Wing, and we may actually want a larger ballroom going forward, but
a 1000-person capacity ballroom is overkill, and an ego project that will overwhelm the scale of the graceful
White House and the West Wing.
It is beyond shocking that no one is being held accountable for this executive overreach.
Do the right thing and start over, going through the proper channels.
Thank you from a concerned citizen.

project is grossly out-of-scale to the White House and historically inappropriate at its location. As
presented, the structure would significantly mar the building's classicizing symmetry and will draw the eye

experience of the White House, one of our nation's most significant and unifying symbols. A ballroom is not
an essential government structure and suggests frivolity rather than statesmanship. I strongly urge the
commission to disapprove and send the project back for reconsideration.

body:

million construction began without National Capital Planning Commission approval, without required
environmental assessments, and without congressional authorization mandated by federal law for
construction on federal parkland in Washington. These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-
fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment that should not be supported by your approval.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.
Thank you!

subject: Written Comments
name: Homer Dearmin
body:
I write today in strong opposition to any proposal to demolish the East Wing of the White House.
The White House is not merely an office building — it is a living symbol of American continuity, stability,
and constitutional governance. Every portion of that structure reflects a chapter in our national story. The
East Wing, though often viewed as secondary to the Executive Residence or West Wing, plays an essential
operational and historical role in the functioning of the Presidency.
I'll never forget visiting the White House in 1999 with the American Legion Boys Nation program, hearing
President Clinton speak in the East Room, and then getting to greet him personally in the Diplomatic
Reception room. Watching this historic part of the White House being demolished by a tyrannical individual
occupying the office of President was absolutely heartbreaking.
The East Wing housed critical offices, including those supporting the First Family and ceremonial functions
of the Presidency. It also served as a primary public entrance for visitors from across the nation and around
the world. In many ways, it represented accessibility — the bridge between the American people and their
government.
Demolition of such a historic structure sets a troubling precedent. Preservation of nationally significant
buildings has long been a bipartisan commitment rooted in respect for our shared heritage. Even when
modernization is needed, thoughtful restoration and adaptive renovation should be prioritized over
irreversible destruction.
Beyond symbolism, there are practical considerations. The cost, security implications, historical review
requirements, and potential disruption to executive operations would be substantial. It is difficult to justify
demolition when renovation or expansion alternatives may accomplish operational goals while preserving
architectural integrity.
The White House belongs to the American people — not to any one administration, party, or moment in
time. Decisions about its structure should reflect stewardship, restraint, and reverence for history.
For these reasons, I respectfully urge decision-makers to reject any proposal to demolish the East Wing and
instead pursue preservation-minded solutions that honor both function and legacy.

name: Amy Viveiros
body:
I oppose spending $300 million on this project which was initiated without proper authorization, design
review, or permits. This is no modernization project. It is a complete razing of American history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park and is owned by the American people
who have allowed presidents to live in “the people’s house” since 1800. Whoever happens to be president
at any given time is not the owner of the property or the structures thereon. A president is merely a
temporary tenant whose interactions with the property and its structures are limited by law and by respect
for the owners, the people of the United States.
The current president initiated the demolition of the historic East Wing without review, permits, or
Congressional oversight. This is a clear violation of the law. It is also a violation of the trust of the American
people who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and
not as a violent fait accompli. The demolition was not necessary and is not a modernization project. People
who do not own a building cannot decide to tear it down and build whatever they want in its place.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site must be compatible in form and
subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion and subject to proper authorization,
permits, design review, and public comment.

preserved, as they should have been, they should be incorporated into the new structure as appropriate.5.
Rigorous inspections should take place to insure approved plans are followed.

of the proposed project. However, this should not be a reason to not enforce proper reviews and
procedures now.
Regarding rumored future projects, the CFA should preemptively outline very specifically the requirements
and timeline any such projects will be expected to follow.
Thank you,

name: Holly Blash-Wood
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

body:

floor. But to tear down a third of the existing White House complex is unacceptable and a great loss of our
heritage. With all the current needs of the people in this country, a ballroom is rock bottom on the list.

should be paid for from his personal funds.

Darcie Livingston

subject: Written Comments
name: Manuela Phillips-Gann
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Dianne Tiboni
body:
Reference NCPC file # 8733
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

body:
As a citizen who loves our nation's capitol, I was dismayed by the demolishing of the East Wing and the
plans for an enormous ballroom in its place. Any remodeling should be done after consultation with historic
preservation professionals, be in keeping with federal laws, and be transparent to the public. This is not a
time for gaudy redecoration; it is a time to remember and celebrate that the US is a democracy. Federal
dollars should go to refund the many programs that have been abandoned by the current administration,
not for this unnecessary remodel. Thank you for considering this opinion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Shirley Wajda
body:
Dear Members of the National Capital Planning Commission:
The White House is not a private property. Rather, it belongs collectively to the American people. Its
temporary occupants are its stewards--as are you. The White House is as much "the People's House" as the
United States Capitol Building. As such, it is only right and proper to undertake careful study of any
substantial and long-lasting material changes to this important, public, and symbolic edifice.
I write today to register my concern and opposition to this project. As a professional historian and curator, I
understand well the vital relationship between the material, the social, and the symbolic. Place indeed has a
place in creating the collective American people. What the current presidential administration has done in
its actions in razing the East Wing is to displace the American people's sense of national identity.
The razing of the East Wing was jarringly initiated without proper authorizations, design review, and
permits. To say that it is a project to "modernize" the East Wing is a distortion of what has thus far
occurred. The East Wing was, simply, demolished. With its demolition, the sense of history associated with
the structure and its material appointments has been destroyed. This is not modernization of an extant
structure and associated meanings. This is destructive erasure.
I oppose the use of privately raised funds (reported as $300 million) for this project. Not a few of the
reported donations are the result of what appears to be political graft and only serves to erode even further
public trust in government.
No one is above the law--not the person who initiated this disastrous destruction and not the persons who
supported it with donations in exchange for political favoritism.
I hope you will act to correct this autocratic and aristocratic wrong and set a path towards the construction
of a democratic East Wing. No ballroom should tower over the history and symbolism of a free people
encapsulated in the historic and symbolic egalitarianism of the White House.
Thank you for this opportunity to exercise my duty as a citizen to share my concerns.
Shirley Wajda, Ph.D.
Canterbury, NH

subject: Written Comments
name: Joshua Liberman
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and National Park, owned by the American people and
stewarded by the National Park Service. It has been home to our presidents since 1800 and is perhaps the
most significant historic site in the United States. Before nationally significant places are permanently
altered, the public deserves an opportunity to be heard and to help shape decisions that affect our shared
national heritage.
Donald Trump has moved forward with the demolition of the East Wing of The White House; without
Congressional Approval, without approval of funding, without the approval of The People of The United
States of America, and without approved plans.
For this reason alone, as well as many, many others brought up by opponents of this project, it is my
opinion that this project be rejected by the National Capital Planning Commission. The East Wing should be
restored to its previous glory and the funding should be paid for with private funds, either from the
President's personal fortune, or the corporate leaders who put him in office. The people should not be
forced to pay for his arrogance, his ego, his illegal project, or his atrocity. Tearing down the White House
without approval of Congress and The People is yet another overreach of power by this president and his
administration. It should not and cannot be allowed.

subject: Written Comments
name: Meg Cowan
body:
I submit this comment in strong opposition to the East Wing modernization and ballroom expansion
proposal. The White House complex is a protected national asset held in trust for the American people —
not a canvas for unilateral, large-scale alteration driven by political ambition or personal legacy projects.
Any demolition, structural removal, or major expansion within this historic site demands rigorous
preservation review, interagency oversight, documented necessity, cost transparency, and meaningful
public process. Proceeding without those guardrails undermines both historic stewardship and public trust.
A 90,000-square-foot addition would permanently alter the architectural and historical balance of the
complex. That level of change requires extraordinary justification, not expedited approval. I urge the
Commission to reject or suspend this proposal until full preservation, fiscal, and public-interest standards
are demonstrably met. National heritage is not a remodeling project.

name: Catherine Albrecht
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and National Park, owned by the American people and
home to our presidents since 1800.
Major construction projects in Washington, D.C. ARE REQUIRED to undergo review by the NCPC and the
Commission of Fine Arts, comply with the National Environmental Policy Act, and receive Congressional
approval. This should have taken place BEFORE the East Wing was demolished.
President Trump should rebuild the East Wing (AT HIS OWN PERSONAL EXPENSE, as he has been profiting
corruptly from the presidency) to look from the exterior EXACTLY like the original, which he tore down
illegally. Updating the above-ground space must be limited to ADA compliance and utility infrastructure. If
additional square footage is truly needed. It should be added as a basement level.
The proposed new East Wing fails completely to respect the historic scale and design of the White House.
At 90,000 square feet, the proposed ballroom would exceed the size of the 55,000-square-foot Executive
Residence. Additions to historic properties should be compatible in scale and subordinate to the original
structure.

body:
Dear Sir or Madam,
Thank you for the opportunity to speak about the East Wing Modernization Project.
I have several concerns about this project.
First of all, the proposed funding of the new East Wing by donations is a concern, in that it is rare that a
corporation or an individual will donate such large sums (now estimated to be $300 million) without getting
something in return. It is in effect, selling influence in federal government.
Secondly, the White House belongs to the people, and no part of it should be destroyed without proper
consultation and adequate time for public input. This has been entirely lacking. The actions of this
administration are not in keeping with a democracy and deserve censure.
Lastly, a ballroom should be very low on the national priority list. There are other venues in the capitol area
better suited for that than the White House. The security concerns, let alone parking, make the White
House a very poor choice for a ballroom.
Thank you.
Kerby Rials

taken to rebuild are done with the input, approval, and oversight of the various committees, rules, and laws
that were set up to protect the physical building of the White House.

On another subject, please don’t let him build the Arch to himself. Not necessary. Not wanted. He’s wasting
government funds that we don’t have.
Thank you very much.
Sincerely yours,
Jan Albertie

history. I want this project canceled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design. No one is
above the law and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law would be
an affront to all law-abiding Americans.

body:

home to presidents since 1800. The current president -- like every president before him -- is a temporary
tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits, and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people,

a violent fait accompli.

its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

body:
The proposed new ballroom wing does not meet the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation
and Preservation. It specifically does not meet Standard for Preservation No. 4; and Standards for
Rehabilitation Nos. 2, 3, 4, 9, and 10.
The new wing will dwarf the historic main House and the West Wing, when the side wings should be smaller
and submissive to the House. The scale of the new wing will make it appear as the main building section.
The renderings show that the proposed ornamentation is bordering on Baroque in its application of several
different decorative details. The renderings also show that the wing has the character of an office building
and not a residential property.
It is a poor design, and one that does not uphold the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for the Treatment
of Historic Properties. I am concerned that it sets a precedent for the destruction of historic resources
across the country.

subject: Written Comments
name: JANICE MILLS
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kimberlee Kelly
body:
I write today not just as a concerned citizen, but as someone guided by deep respect for our shared history,
democratic process, and responsible stewardship of public resources. Over more than 15 years as an
educator, advocate, and community leader, I have learned that trust in our institutions depends on
transparency, adherence to the law, and respect for the people we serve.
That is why I strongly oppose the $300 million expenditure on the “East Wing Modernization” project.
Launching such a significant effort without proper authorization, permits, or design review violates basic
standards of governance and disregards the voices of the people who ultimately pay the bill.
Our nation’s architectural treasures, especially those honoring the roles women and countless others have
played in our governance, deserve preservation rather than rushed demolition without open review and
informed consent. Destroying parts of this history without due process, while exposing local communities to
known toxic substances through improper demolition, undermines public trust and disrespects the legacy
that binds us together.
I urge decision\u8209 -makers to halt this project immediately and instead commit to:
- Fully canceling the current modernization effort
- Entrusting the rebuilding or restoration of the East Wing to the next administration
- Establishing a transparent, legally compliant process with community and expert input at every step
Taxpayer dollars must be invested with accountability and integrity. Allowing this project to continue
without consequences for those who bypassed lawful procedures would waste resources and send a
dangerous message that rules and preservation can be ignored. All public servants and all administrations
must uphold the highest standards of responsibility and respect for our nation’s heritage, reflecting the
contributions of all genders, cultures, and races.
This project must not move forward until the rule of law, as well as the voices and contributions of the
American people, then and now, are fully honored.
Respectfully,
Kimberlee Kelly

name: Kate Corrigon
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

body:
I strongly oppose the spending of $300 million on this monstrously large and completely unnecessary
project. The President claims that money was donated, but there are no clear receipts. It very feels very
much like another corrupt pay to play scheme. Beyond the corrupt money issue, this destruction of OUR
HOUSE was initiated without the proper authorization, permits, or design review. It goes well beyond
"modernization" and is rather a complete razing of American history and more simply another of the
President's vanity projects, wasting money to glorify himself. He just took a wrecking ball to our house with
the clear intention of claiming "well, now we have to fix it so we may as well go ahead with MY plan." No
President has ever used his power of office and the people's money to satisfy his narcissistic need for
recognition. This project must canceled. The East Wing must be rebuilt and restored to its former design.
No one is above the law, especially the President! To permit this project to go ahead is complicity with law
breaking; and not penalizing those who broke the law would be an affront to all law-abiding Americans.

name: Colleen Kennedy
body:
I have owned a home built from 1753-1812 since 1982. I have carefully restored and updated my home to
retain its history and authenticity because I believe it is much more than a building. It holds the story of the
people who lived in it and that matters. I may only know them from census and property records but I can
place them at significant points in history and imagine what their lives were like.
It broke my heart to see the East Wing carelessly destroyed for no reason other than ego. While I can
understand the need to move from tents to a more stable site, it should have been planned with respect,
not ripped off in favor of a gaudy replica of Mar-Lago.
It is too late to prevent the destruction of an historic building but there is no reason not to replace it with a
historically relevant and architecturally consistent design. Please don’t let this become a shrine to Trump.
We are better than than.

name: Anne Carr
body:
I am completely opposed to the so-called "modernization" of the East Wing, and agree with those who call
for the original East Wing to be rebuilt at Trump's personal expense.
The White House is not the personal property of any President, but rather is a historic, nationally-owned
property where any elected President merely *temporarily* resides and does business. The idea that a
President would demolish an essential part of the structure without ANY public input and review is
outrageous. In this case, it's not Trump's property to do with as he pleases!. Not to mention that his sense
of taste and propriety is vulgar. Architecturally, the East Wing should be subordinate to the main central
structure of the White House -- not equal to it in height, and certainly not more visually dominant. Further,
the plans Trump has announced for private financing are utterly inappropriate, and represent a gift which
to my understanding is a violation of federal ethics, not that Trump has ANY ethical bearing whatsoever.
Finally, the habit Trump has of naming federally -funded projects for himself would also be completely
inappropriate.
If Trump is in a big hurry to build a ballroom, he has any number of resort properties where he can do so, at
his expense, of course. In the meantime, this illegal project must be stopped, and the East Wing restored to
what it was. Trying to design a new East Wing will take too long, and Trump's impact on the country and the
capitol has already been unbearable. Pry his greedy hands off the country already!

subject: Written Comments
name: Laura Million
body:
The proposed White House Ballroom project should not proceed as currently planned. The reported
demolition of the historic East Wing of the White House without prior approval or notification raises serious
concerns and warrants an immediate pause due to an apparent lack of transparency and good faith in the
project’s execution.
Additionally, reports that “private donors” are funding the project in exchange for access to the President
create the appearance of impropriety and undermine public trust. This approach is inconsistent with the
standards of accountability and integrity expected in the United States.
All plans should undergo thorough review by the appropriate oversight bodies. Potential sites should be
carefully evaluated, and any necessary funding should be formally authorized and appropriated by
Congress. Furthermore, a comprehensive environmental impact assessment should be completed before
construction begins.
If the ballroom project ultimately moves forward, its design should complement and enhance the historic
character of the White House rather than detract from or overwhelm it.

This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts.\u-4 ?
This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have
unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.\u-4 ?

body:

Peace and greetings and thanks you for your service.
I am opposed to the East Wing Project to add a huge ballroom to the White House.

been called the People's House because it is where the President lives ONLY while he or she serves the
people. For this ballroom to be added to entertain the wealthy donors of this president while so many
Americans struggle with health care, heating their homes and meeting their daily living expenses is an
excess we do not need. It is a real insult to our democracy.
Sincerely,
Todd Goodwn, A Concerned American

Upon seeing the destruction of the East Wing of the White House for the first time my initial reaction was
one of near vomiting. The impulsive destruction of a historically significant portion of a beloved building
was almost beyond belief. My second reaction was one of tears. The fact that this has happened, without
any public involvement, or prior approval, was almost beyond belief. Unfortunately & sadly, it has
happened. I DO NOT want any gaudy ballroom that pays homage to the worst president in US history. I
want the East Wing back, maybe a new & improved version, but the East Wing. I am a citizen. I am a
taxpayer. I raise my voice in protest over the unapproved actions of an out of control administration.
PROTECT this important part of our history. PROTECT & RESPECT the East Wing in the only manner befitting
the glory of not only a building, but everything it stood for & hopefully, will stand for in the future.
A testament to the fact that yes, we were tested as a Nation, but we held firm & came back even stronger
& more dedicated to the vision of what it means to be the United States of America.

"I'm not opposed to modernization or even expansion of the East Wing of the White House. However, I'm 
appalled that the Administration would choose to demolish the East Wing and assume they could proceed 
with a large expansion without going through any of the required (and appropriate) review channels. I 
believe the following principles should be applied to any construction on the East Wing site: 
--The size and extent of construction should consider the size and extent of the rest of the White House, 
and should not overwhelm or dominate the rest of the structure; 
--Modernization should be carried out to allow for functions in keeping with modern technology, with space 
set aside to house the technology, but again considering the size and extent of the rest of the structure; 
--Exterior features, treatments, and finishes should be in keeping with the historic architecture and nature 
of the remainder of the White House; 
--Before any additional work is done, an Historic Structure Report should be prepared using Historic 
American Buildings Survey standards, and should be retroactive to before the East Wing was demolished; 
--Documentation of all historic features demolished should be carried out in accordance with federal 
standards; 
--An interpretive display should be prepared, subject to National Capital Planning Commission and National 
Trust for Historic Preservation standards, regarding the features demolished; 
--Any work from this point forward should comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards. 
Thank you for your consideration."

I write in strong opposition to the proposed demolition of the East Wing of the White House and the
construction of a new ballroom.
This project represents not modernization but the irreversible destruction of an important part of American
history. The East Wing is a significant architectural and historic component of the White House complex,
and its demolition would undermine the integrity, continuity, and symbolism of one of the nation’s most
important landmarks.
Equally concerning is the apparent advancement of this proposal without appropriate authorization,
permitting, and transparent design review. No project —  regardless of sponsor or purpose — should bypass
the processes intended to protect our shared national heritage. Allowing such a precedent would weaken
public trust and disregard the rule of law that governs responsible stewardship of federal properties.
Spending hundreds of millions of dollars to erase historic fabric in favor of a new construction project is
neither justified nor consistent with preservation principles. I urge the Commission to reject this proposal,
cancel the project, and ensure that the East Wing is preserved and restored in accordance with established
historic preservation standards.

proper legal channels must be addressed. Allowing this project to proceed without accountability would
undermine public trust and the rule of law that all Americans rely on.

subject: Written Comments
name: Lynn Rozental
body:
As a graduate of the University of Vermont's masters program in historic preservation I point out that
federal laws protecting historic buildings are being ignored here.
As a citizen and proud American I would also point out that the White House belongs to the people of this
country. Never before has one of the transient residents of this house forgotten this. The current
president's unilateral decision to destroy a part of this historic building should be strongly countered by
those charged with preserving our country's history, traditions, values and laws. Likewise, the design for any
new building on the site should be subject to proper review as required by law.
The fact that wealthy individuals and corporations have made financial gifts to fund the proposed project
raises legitimate concerns about undue influence in search of political pay back, something the authors of
our Constitution worked to prevent.
As a person who was taught and in turn taught my child that might does not make right, I protest the abuse
of power in full display here.
Bullying on any level should be met with full resolve, and I challenge those with the power and resources to
counter this project to push back.

body:
This project is not needed and disturbs the view and historical significance of 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue.
Our countries founding fathers did not envision a time when a palatial ballroom would be built for an
administration that thought of itself as provincial aristocrats, building palaces to honor their kingly
ambitions.
This project dwarfs in size all the buildings on this site and can only be seen as a diaspora of ill-conceived
thought and planning, to placate the narcissism of the current White House resident.
This project has not followed American historical preservation ideals, with its grandiose facade, arches, and
symbols perfectly suited for the Kings of Europe's past and present.
Please, with all due respect, end this project as it stands and restore the East Wing as it has stood for all the
many decades.
Thank you,
Kyle

subject: Written Comments
name: Kathleen Delaney
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project.
This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts. This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have
unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I strongly urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

expected to follow the rules.

body:
I came of age under the Kennedy Administration. I had great admiration for both JFK and Jackie, Jackie's
respect for the historical importance of the White House was inspriing. I felt like THAT was what every
occupant should feel. The White House is OUR house, the People's House. The current occupant is always
temporary, they are transients living rent-free in a house OWNED by the PEOPLE of the USA. Respect for it's
history is the least we should be able to expect from transient occupants. The destruction of Jackie's Rose
Garden was distressing to me, and many others who loved and admired her.
The East Wing underwent many transformations during it's almost 100 years, it doesn't have the same
historical weight as the Main building, but it has formed and shaped it's own history and significance, and
there are LAWS on the books about how federal properties are to be maintained, and how any major
"construction" or "renovations" are to be reviewed and approved.
The wholesale destruction of the East Wing goes against the laws, the precedents, and the will of the
PEOPLE who OWN the property. Modernizing the East Wing might be a worthwhile project, but a
BALLROOM that is far outside the guidelines for construction is definitely not an improvement, nor is it
needed.

name: Wendy Allex
body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
Thank you for your consideration.

subject: Written Comments
name: Erik Cullins
body:
To the National Capital Planning Commission,
I am submitting this written objection regarding the proposed East Wing Modernization Project.
I strongly oppose approval of this project for the following reasons, which I believe directly implicate federal
interests in the National Capital Region and fall within the Commission’s statutory review responsibilities.
1. Inconsistency with Federal Planning Principles and the Comprehensive Plan
The proposed ballroom appears inconsistent with the policies and guiding principles of the Comprehensive
Plan for the National Capital. Federal projects within the monumental core and surrounding federal interest
areas must demonstrate clear public purpose, fiscal responsibility, and alignment with long-term planning
objectives.
A large ceremonial or entertainment-focused structure raises significant concerns regarding:
• Necessity relative to existing federal facilities
• Duplication of function
• Long-term operational and maintenance costs
• Impact on the symbolic and civic character of the area
The Commission has a responsibility to ensure that federal development advances enduring national
interests rather than short-term political priorities.
2. Fiscal Responsibility and Stewardship of Public Funds
As a federally reviewed project, this proposal implicates taxpayer resources — whether directly
appropriated, indirectly subsidized, or supported through federal land and infrastructure.
The National Capital Region already includes numerous federally owned and federally supported venues
capable of hosting official functions and ceremonial events. The justification for constructing a new
ballroom facility must therefore be rigorously scrutinized.
In the absence of clear, documented necessity and cost-benefit analysis, the proposal appears to represent
an unnecessary expenditure inconsistent with principles of prudent federal stewardship.
3. Procedural and Legal Concerns
There are serious concerns that this project may not have followed the full procedural path required for
federal development in the National Capital Region, including but not limited to:
• Adequate NEPA review
• Section 106 consultation under the National Historic Preservation Act
• Public engagement at the appropriate concept stage
• Transparent cost disclosure and authorization
• Compliance with statutory review sequencing required under the National Capital Planning Act
If these processes have not been fully completed prior to final approval, advancing the project would
undermine both legal safeguards and public trust.
The Commission should not approve any action until all required environmental, historic preservation, and
statutory reviews are complete and publicly documented.
4. Precedent and Institutional Integrity
NCPC plays a critical role in protecting the long-term planning integrity of the National Capital. Approving a
project that appears driven by symbolic or personal legacy considerations, rather than demonstrated
federal necessity, risks setting a precedent that weakens planning standards and erodes confidence in
federal oversight.
The Commission’s mandate is to ensure that development in the capital region reflects national purpose
and enduring civic value, not transient political objectives.
Requested Action
For the reasons stated above, I respectfully request that the Commission:
• Defer action on this proposal until all procedural requirements are fully satisfied.
• Require a detailed public justification of need and fiscal analysis.
• Ensure comprehensive compliance with NEPA and historic preservation laws.
• Consider whether this project meaningfully advances federal interests as required under the National
Capital Planning Act.
Thank you for your consideration of this comment.
Sincerely,
Erik Cullins

proportion, and architectural coherence of federal landmarks is especially important here.

name: Robert Graham
body:
I submit my comments as a Registered Architect in the state of Arizona specializing in historic preservation.
1. The East Wing of the White House was demolished in contravention of the laws of the United States,
without rational justification, public input, or legislative authorization. Construction of a replacement
cannot be allowed to proceed because illegal actions such as these should not be rewarded.
2. The demolition of the 1902(?) East wing represents a material loss to American History. Whatever comes
next on this site must respect not only the original White House but also atone for the loss of the East Wing.
3. Preferably, the East Wing should be reconstructed of modern construction and detailing and of a scale
that is respectful of the earlier East Wing as well as the remaining main White House and West Wing.
4. The proposed ballroom is radically out of scale to the historic structures remaining on site and projects
much too far in front of the White House facade. The proposed design would irrevocably alter the historic
context of the White House.

unacceptable.

established federal guidelines, including those of the National Capital Planning Commission. Circumventing

ignore statutory obligations.

bypassed required approvals would be an affront to every law-abiding American and to the integrity of our
democratic institutions.
I call for this project to be immediately halted, fully investigated, and canceled. The East Wing should be
rebuilt and restored to its former design in accordance with all applicable laws, proper permitting, and
transparent consultation with the appropriate agencies and the public.
Thank you.

unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

subject: Written Comments
name: Lonnie Hovey
body:
I greatly oppose the Executive Office of the President's (EOP) East Wing Modernization Project, especially
the proposed construction of a 90,000-square-foot ballroom addition to the White House complex. The
design and scale are completely at odds with the scale of the historic site, and disregard the Secretary of
the Interior's Rehabilitation Standards 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, and 10. Regarding standard 1, the defining
characteristics of the East Wing and East Colonnade were destroyed and a maximum change was made to
the historic character of the White House and the environment of the White House Grounds. Regarding
standard 2, the historic character was not retained and preserved. Removal of historic features and spaces
were not avoided. Regarding standard 3, the East Wing and East Colonnade were not retained as a physical
record of its time, place and use. Regarding standard 4, the historic significance of the East Wing and East
Colonnade were not retained and preserved. Regarding standard 5, the historic features, finishes and
craftsmanship of spaces within the East Wing and East Colonnade were not retained for
repair/rehabilitation or preservation. Regarding standard 6, the East Wing and East Colonnade were not in
deteriorated condition that necessitated their complete demolition. Regarding standard 9, the proposed
new construction has destroyed historic materials and spaces that characterize the property. Regarding
standard 10, the proposed addition overwhelms the historic scale of the White House, and the demolition
of the East Wing and East Colonnade has destroyed the essential form and integrity of the historic property
and the environment of the White House grounds. The destruction of the East Wing and the East Colonnade
were done without CFA and NCPC oversight and an example needs to be made that the EOP is not above
the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Catherine Weigel
body:
I am adamantly opposed to this project for the following reasons:
-It has already destroyed a historic portion of the White House, i.e., the PEOPLE'S house, without notice and
without the public being allowed any chance to weigh in.
-Was there damage done to the existing underground infrastructure, some of which was used during the
9/11 attacks, and has been meant to keep White House personnel safe & able to work during emergencies?
The public certainly hasn't been informed of it and any damage to those spaces is going to be very
expensive and delicate to fix.
-Although it is true that other presidents have made significant changes to the White House over the years,
I believe it was always with an eye toward maintaining the historical integrity of the building without the
absolute disregard shown by the current occupants of the White House for the laws regarding historic
buildings, especially THIS historic building.
-My biggest problem with the project is the use of private funding, which reporting so far seems to indicate
is all coming from parties with an interest in seeking favors from the current administration. This is a
conflict of interest, plain and simple, right out in the open. I might not be any happier if taxpayer funds
were being used but at least there is a history of past presidents (or their wives) redecorating and making
improvements. I'm old enough to remember Jackie Kennedy's famous rose garden being an addition of
which most people approved (which has now been sadly bulldozed and paved over now).
-The American public did not ask for and does not want a gigantic ballroom that dwarfs the White House, to
which the public will have little to no access, as a monument to the current White House occupant's fragile
ego, especially if it doesn't remotely fit the architecture of the existing building. The demolition of the East
Wing (have those contractors been paid yet?) made me sad and heartbroken for the entire country. It
seemed to symbolize something more spiritual being destroyed in the country, which will not be rebuilt
with a giant ballroom.

To whom it may concern,
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National

controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.

subject: Written Comments
name: Brandi McCombs
body:
Looking at the design boards for this project, the proposed addition looks like a monstrosity. The size and
scope are much larger than what is necessary. The addition looks like it will dwarf the White House, which
sends the message that lavish events and showmanship are the main purposes of the entire compound. I
believe the in history of the White House, not included in the attached documents, the forefathers agreed
that the nation’s leader would not live in a palace like a king.
From a birds-eye view, I do not like that the proposed building cuts the edge off the ellipse shape/design in
the yard that is repeated throughout so many spaces nearby (not ‘The Ellipse’ but the oval or semi-circle
shape itself).
I am also concerned with the interior design aspects, considering the changes the current tenant has
undertaken in the White House. Will each future President be allowed to redecorate according to his or her
own tastes, with the cost borne by taxpayers? Or will it be labeled “The Trump Ballroom” in perpetuity and
no changes to be made ever? As a middle class taxpayer who will never attend an event here, I feel the
entire project is a pompous monument to excess and classism (as opposed to classicism).
Thank you.

subject: Written Comments
name: A Lucio
body:
Please see my comments for the 02/19/2026 meeting on the East Wing Modernization Project and
ballroom addition.
As a community activist for preservation of our historical places, I am against this project primarily due to its
erasure of American history and our significant buildings.
Additionally, I am against this project due to the absence of required federal approvals, potential asbestos
risks, and the massive, 90,000-square-foot scale of the new, privately funded ballroom.
Destruction of Historic Fabric: The project demolished the 1902 East Wing, including its colonnade, which
was first established on the site by Thomas Jefferson. This erases a significant part of American history, with
historians describing the demolition as a "wrecking ball to tradition".
Lack of Public and Federal Review: The project moved forward without approval from Congress, the
Commission of Fine Arts, or the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC), violating standard
procedures for major federal renovations.
Ethical and Funding Concerns: Although privately funded by "patriot donors," the lack of disclosure
regarding donors—including potential interests from the crypto and tobacco industries —has raised
significant ethical questions about buying access to the administration.
Disproportionate Scale and Design: The proposed 90,000-square-foot ballroom is vastly larger than the
current, much more modest, 200-person capacity East Room. The new structure is too large, gaudy, and not
in keeping with the historical aesthetic of the White House.
Environmental and Safety Risks: The demolition of the 1942 structure was conducted without typical
environmental reviews, raising concerns about asbestos exposure to workers and the surrounding area.
Circumventing Oversight: The administration was sued by top historic preservation groups, who
emphasized the project bypassed legal, environmental, and architectural review processes.
Thank you.

Commission of Fine Arts, or the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC), violating standard 
procedures for major federal renovations. 
 
Ethical and Funding Concerns: Although privately funded by "patriot donors," the lack of disclosure 
regarding donors—including potential interests from the crypto and tobacco industries —has raised 
significant ethical questions about buying access to the administration. 
 
Disproportionate Scale and Design: The proposed 90,000-square-foot ballroom is vastly larger than the 
current, much more modest, 200-person capacity East Room. The new structure is too large, gaudy, and not 
in keeping with the historical aesthetic of the White House. 
 
Environmental and Safety Risks: The demolition of the 1942 structure was conducted without typical 
environmental reviews, raising concerns about asbestos exposure to workers and the surrounding area. 
 
Circumventing Oversight: The administration was sued by top historic preservation groups, who 
emphasized the project bypassed legal, environmental, and architectural review processes. 
 
Thank you.

through the approved process with signoff and oversight. Do not allow those who desecrated our People’s
House to get away without consequences to its lawless destruction.

Thank you.

subject: Written Comments
name: Christine Simpson
body:
I am concerned that the proposed renovation of the White House East Wing has been illegally undertaken
and if completed will be completely out of scale to the existing historic residence - essentially adding a
90,000 sq ft addition to a 55,000 sq ft. structure.
There is even talk now of trying to balance this grossly oversized ballroom by increasing the size of the
WEST Wing colonnade. This is trying to fix a bad design, one that ignored the requirement of mandatory
review by your agency, with more half-baked plans.
The National Capital Planning Commission is tasked with preserving and enhancing the extraordinary
historical resources of the National Capital Region. I can hardly think of a historical resource more
extraordinary than the White House. One of the NCPC's core activities is to review and approve changes to
historic structures. I urge the Commission to hold this proposed renovation to the highest standards so that
despite the illegal demolition of the existing East Wing, the new structure will be architecturally and
historically appropriate to the site.
Thank you

subject: Written Comments
name: Carolyn Johnson
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Susan Jacob
body:
As an American who sees value in process and accountability, I have been very concerned about the
destruction of the East Wing without forethought of its legacy and historical significance.
Any President is a temporary resident of the people's house, at our discretion, and major changes that are
more than an upgrade of standards or decor have been required to be vetted in the past.
As many of us ask "what happened?" and wonder how it happened so quickly without authorization, we
also mourn for future generations who will never be able to visit a tremendous gift of history.
Therefore, it should be reinstated as it was in size and scope as a tribute to the American people as soon as
possible. There are plenty of ballrooms available in DC to accommodate hosted events, and that would
provide respectable income support to an amazing city.
Thank you for your consideration and for creating this opportunity to provide comments.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kate Schwennsen
body:
Dear National Capital Planning Commissioners:
Thank you for the opportunity to submit comments regarding the design of the proposed White House East
Wing Modernization. I am an architect, a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects (AIA), a former
national President of the AIA (2006) a former Chancellor of the AIA College of Fellows (2025), and was an
architecture professor and administrator for over 30 years. Also, for the last almost 30 years, at least twice
per year, I have enjoyed a walk by the White House and its surrounding parks and buildings, and have
appreciated it, the People's House, as a wonderful symbol of this nation.
If any of my previous students had submitted the proposed Ballroom addition to the White House as
currently designed, I would have given them a failing grade. Why?
1. The overall scale and size of the proposed addition is totally inappropriate for its context and site. It
grossly overwhelms the White House, the building that should unquestionably be the most important
building of this composition of buildings.
2. Because the proposed building is so huge, the scale of its parts, the details of its elevations, windows,
stairs, etc., are also grossly oversized, so as to make the White House look like a miniature playhouse
awaiting replacement.
3. The Georgian, neo-classical or whatever schmaltz of the composition does not reflect anything about a
building of its time, 2026, except that the scale of its open space spans would have been more difficult to
accomplish in the time it seems to want to belong. “Modernization” is an oxymoron for this proposal.
4. The design program of use, a gargantuan ballroom, which coincidentally could also be used to privatize
Presidential Inaugurations, is an inappropriate program for this site, time and for the People's House. There
are plenty of other ballroom spaces in DC, I've been to many of them. And the Presidential Inauguration
should always and ever be more broadly accessible than any ballroom can accommodate.
5. Finally, while it may not be a design factor, the demolition and approval process for this proposal has
been horrific and again totally inappropriate.
As your request for Public Comments clearly states: “The White House is a National Historic Landmark and
National Park, owned by the American people and stewarded by the National Park Service. It has been
home to our presidents since 1800 and is perhaps the most significant historic site in the United States.
Before nationally significant places are permanently altered, the public deserves an opportunity to be heard
and to help shape decisions that affect our shared national heritage.”
I am quite certain the public is not in favor of this grotesque addition to the White House. Thank you for the
opportunity to comment. I sincerely hope that you do not recommend approval of this design as proposed.
Kate Schwennsen, FAIA
Professor Emeritus + Director Emeritus, Clemson University School of Architecture
2025 Chancellor, AIA College of Fellows
2006 President, American Institute of Architects

subject: Written Comments
name: Stephen Woolsey
body:
I am writing to implore you to block further work on the proposed ballroom and bunker, and instead to
mandate the reconstruction of the East Wing, modernizing it as needed but maintaining the architectural
style of the original structure. I am appalled and saddened that the current Republican administration
demolished the old East Wing without appropriate prior consultation with and authorization from the
bodies and groups charged with maintaining the integrity of "the people's house," with all of its historical
significance and its central importance as a symbol of the values that have made this democratic republic a
beacon of freedom, justice, and equality for all citizens. The lawless, reckless, and brazen way in which the
demolition was undertaken flies in the face of that rich history and symbolism, suggesting that one man--
the current president--has a right to do as he likes with this public building, marring it forever, when in fact
he is only a temporary resident. In destroying the old East Wing this president seems to engaging in an
intentional erasure of earlier residents who left their own marks on the building in a way that harmonized
with the original design, or even enhanced it. In contrast, the wildly-oversized ballroom and bunker design
seems to be nothing but a vanity project, overwhelming the order and harmony of the existing building in a
way that does aesthetic violence to the whole. I know it has been argued that the ball-room and bunker will
cost the American people nothing because the project is supposedly funded by private donations, but I
would counter that argument with a different cost metric: this completely unnecessary and frankly
unsightly new ballroom and bunker WOULD in fact be unacceptably costly to the citizens of this country,
since it would severely undercut public faith and trust in the agencies and groups we commission to
maintain our public monuments for the good of all, in a way that honors our shared history and values. For
all of these reasons, I ask you please to halt and reverse this destructive project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Robert Brinkmann
body:
I believe that major changes to the historic White House, which represents our common heritage, should
not be decided by one man - even if it is the president. The razing of the historic East Wing without prior
planning and an agreed upon "modernization" (really: complete replacement by something entirely
different) without the involvement of the NCPC and public comment period and discussion is not
acceptable. And that is only part of the problem...
The ballroom being proposed is out of proportion to the White House itself and would take away from the
most important and recognized building in the country, besides being an ostentatious, unsightly, and
overwhelming addition to the White House itself. Our elected officials are supposed to represent us and do
the people's work, not party in opulence and play court. This is not a club or a castle, it is the People's
House.
Everything about what is happening is wrong and needs to be stopped. Modernize what needs to be
modernized, but rebuild the original East Wing - slightly bigger if necessary - but stop the terrible idea of a
ballroom, let alone one so out of proportion with the historical structure. It's not modernization - it's
destruction of cultural heritage.

body:
