Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Lisa Perea
body:
I joined the National Trust for Historic Preservation after reading about the demolition of the East Wing of
the White House and removal of historical monuments and plaques by the current presidential
administration. As a former history teacher, I am appalled at the such blatant attacks on our nation's history
have been allowed to occur. From my Republican upbringing I was taught that our past cannot be forgotten
as it guides our future, a philosophy that I instilled in my students for 33 years. How the East Wing was
allowed to be demolished without public approval boggles my mind. The White House is a National Historic
Landmark and National Park, owned by the American people, and stewarded by the National Park Service.
The White House is not privately owned and as thus cannot be changed. The people of this country should
have been consulted, at least through our public representatives, before the demolition. I do not wish the
current president's plan for a 90,000-square-foot ballroom to erect on the east side of the White House. I
know it will be hard to reconstruct, yet reconstruction as near to the original building must be done. The
president is not above the law though he seems to be engaged in the systematic destruction of the rule of
law. The White House is a symbol of this nation, not a playground for the want to be rich and famous, and it
needs to be reconstructed to its original design.

subject: Written Comments
name: Lynn Perkins
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

I did not nor do not support the destruction of the east wing of the White House. What Mr. Trump did on
the sly is unconscionable. What he did is not just egregious to the soul of the U.S. It has spoken volumes
about his feelings for women where first and second wives did their much of their work. It was a woman's
place, among other offices. Not that Melania has had much liking for the job, but what she does do isn't
done there anymore either.
I did not nor do not I want a detached ball room, let alone a nine thousand square foot attached one just
for the glory of one man's despotic narcissism. A good ninety-eight percent of Americans would never see
the inside of it. We don't have enough money to buy tickets to a function there and wouldn't be invited
anyway. All we will see is a bloated canker on the side of Our House.
I could go on a bit more, but these are my top two considerations in regard to this deeply offensive and
highly illegal project. It must go through the proper permissions and planning, and because Trump did not
ask or receive permission he must rebuild and replace everything and return the wing to its former glory.
Yes, put in upgrades for electrical and plumbing and HVAC needs. Maybe a reinforced bunker under it. And
there should be no mention of the Trump name anywhere near it except Melania's brief and infrequent
habitation there as a first lady.

name: Daniel Christian
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project.
This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts. This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have
unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

subject: Written Comments
name: Alexandra Jones
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.

approving those contracts. This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.

unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

I'm not opposed to modernization or even expansion of the East Wing of the White House. However, I'm 
appalled that the Administration would choose to demolish the East Wing and assume they could proceed

believe the following principles should be applied to any construction on the East Wing site: 
--The size and extent of construction should consider the size and extent of the rest of the White House, 
and should not overwhelm or dominate the rest of the structure; 
--Modernization should be carried out to allow for functions in keeping with modern technology, with space 
set aside to house the technology, but again considering the size and extent of the rest of the structure; 
--Exterior features, treatments, and finishes should be in keeping with the historic architecture and nature 
of the remainder of the White House; 
--Before any additional work is done, an Historic Structure Report should be prepared using Historic 
American Buildings Survey standards, and should be retroactive to before the East Wing was demolished; 
--Documentation of all historic features demolished should be carried out in accordance with federal 
standards; 
--An interpretive display should be prepared, subject to National Capital Planning Commission and National 
Trust for Historic Preservation standards, regarding the features demolished; 
--Any work from this point forward should comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards. 
Thank you for your consideration.

subject: Written Comments
name: Rebecca Rettig
body:
After the destruction of the East Wing at The White House, the priority should be clear: restore what was
lost, not replace it with something entirely different. Proposals to build a new ballroom in place of the East
Wing ignore the historical and functional significance of that space and risk turning a restoration moment
into an unnecessary redesign.
The East Wing has long played a vital role in supporting the operations and traditions of the White House
while preserving the architectural integrity of the overall complex. Rebuilding it would respect continuity,
history, and the careful balance that defines one of the nation’s most recognizable landmarks.
Choosing to construct a ballroom instead sends the wrong message — that expansion and spectacle matter
more than preservation and stewardship. Restoring the East Wing would honor the legacy of the building
and demonstrate a commitment to safeguarding history rather than reshaping it for short-term vision.

subject: Written Comments
name: Richard Swank
body:
Dear Commissioners,
I am writing to express my strong opposition to the proposed East Wing Modernization project, which
reportedly involves an expenditure of approximately $300 million. This initiative appears to have been
undertaken without the proper authorization, permits, or design review required for such a significant and
historically sensitive building.
This is not a modernization effort—it is, rather, the destruction of a vital piece of American history. The old
structure should be rebuilt to its original design.
Moreover, allowing this project to proceed without accountability for those who disregarded established
legal and procedural safeguards would undermine the rule of law and further erode public trust. No one,
regardless of position or institution, is above the law.
I respectfully urge the Commission to halt this project, investigate the procedural violations, and require full
compliance with all laws governing design review, preservation, and funding approval.
Sincerely,
Richard Swank PhD

subject: Written Comments
name: tom carnevale
body:
I am aware that the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) has opened public comments on the
proposed modernization of the East Wing at the White House. This project is not a modernization of the
East Wing of the White House, as listed above from the drop-down menu, but rather the wholesale
destruction of a very important public building, which is the symbol of our democracy, by a single
individual. As you all know, the East Wing of our White House has demolished PRIOR to any discussion of its
removal. The proposed replacement of this important wing of the White House with a 90,000-square-foot
ballroom addition is completely out of scale and proportion to our White House and its surround grounds.
The White House is for the President to live in while they are the current President, it is not theirs "to make
in their own image" by permanently altering or destroying the building or property without permission
from the public. Yes, they can paint interior rooms, hang new curtains, change light fixtures and move
furniture around and in & out. IF a ballroom is needed (which is questionable), does it need to be attached
to and dwarf our White House? IF it is needed for 'dinner parties' & gatherings, does it need to be attached
to and dwarf our White House? Can a 'ballroom' happen somewhere else within the District and be used for
possibly other 'functions? The National Capital Planning Commission is charged with reviewing these
projects, which affect our public buildings, the Commission needs to (and MUST) review with critical eyes
and make sure that whatever is built is appropriate for the setting, building, and public, and not just the
individual that is currently living at our White House. A public design charrette or competition should be
held (with a written building program) in order to find and discover the best solution for a "90,000 Square-
foot Ballroom", for OUR HOUSE, AMERICA'S HOUSE. Thank You

subject: Written Comments
name: Beverley Harper Tinsley
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. This is not modernization, but removal and replacement. In
addition, no effort was made to preserve the special materials, or unique historical artifacts, important to
our national history and identity. We the people do not know what has become of the treasured items once
housed there. I am outraged at this contemptible violation of the trust of the American people. We were
given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal, and not as a violent
fait accompli, prior to waking to see photos of a giant pit. The speed and aggression with which this
destruction was undertaken clearly indicate those directing the damage knew it would not be acceptable to
the citizens of the country.
The current occupant of the White House is a temporary visitor, just as every United States president has
been throughout our history. No president is entitled to treat this much loved property of the citizens as if it
were his/her own house, to destroy with willful abandon, at a personal whim. Nor should either taxpayers,
or wealthy private individuals and corporations with potentially corrupt self interests pay for one powerful
person’s private aesthetic to be imposed upon our most meaningful historical structures.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
The United States does not have a king, and we will not support having a palace.

accountability. The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and
major alterations should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant
project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Maureen Brower
body:
To whom it may concern,
I am writing to express my deep concern and strong disapproval regarding the proposed construction of a
ballroom at the White House.
The White House is far more than a residence or event venue—it is a living symbol of our nation ’s history,
leadership, and democratic values. The preservation of its historical integrity should be treated as a sacred
responsibility. The idea of constructing a new ballroom, particularly one that could exceed the scale of the
existing structure where critical decisions affecting our country and the world are made every day, is deeply
troubling.
A ballroom, by its very nature, is a space intended for social gatherings and entertainment. It should never
overshadow or overpower a place of such profound national importance. Alterations of this magnitude risk
diminishing the historical character and symbolic weight of this treasured landmark.
I strongly urge you and all decision-makers involved to reconsider this proposal and to prioritize the
preservation and protection of the White House as the historic and dignified institution it has always been.
Future generations deserve to inherit it with its integrity intact.
Thank you for your time and for considering the concerns of citizens who care deeply about preserving our
nation’s history.
Respectfully,
Maureen Brower

body:

grounds. I am also requesting that instead of this ballroom, the East Wing be fully restored and rebuilt, at

processes required for any such major renovations, he had no right to destroy the East Wing in the first
place. We are a nation of laws, period. This stunt and dismissal of the processes herein, is yet another
example of his total disregard for our Democracy, our Constitution, our laws, and lastly, the power of the
peoples' voice.

ago. Its structure was in keeping with the simplicity, elegance and humility of our White House. The
proposed ballroom is a monstrosity of a structure that I'm sure will be gilded with the similar gaudiness of
Trump's defiling project for the Oval office. In other words, he turned the dignified office into the likeness
of a cheap brothel or third rate casino in Atlantic City.
The ballroom project must be stopped now.

permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history. I was shocked at the level of distruction to this historic building and the lack of respect for the
history enshrined inside the building and what was contained within the building.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

Dear Commissioners,
I am writing to express my strong opposition to the proposed East Wing Modernization project, which
reportedly involves an expenditure of approximately $300 million. This initiative appears to have been
undertaken without the proper authorization, permits, or design review required for such a significant and
historically sensitive undertaking.
This is not a true modernization effort—it is, in essence, the destruction of a vital piece of American history.
The existing structure should be restored and rebuilt to its original design rather than replaced or
substantially altered.
Moreover, allowing this project to proceed without accountability for those who disregarded established
legal and procedural safeguards would undermine the rule of law and erode public trust. No one, regardless
of position or institution, is above the law.
I respectfully urge the Commission to halt this project, investigate the procedural violations, and require full
compliance with all laws governing design review, preservation, and funding approval.
Sincerely,
Jennifer Swank

a violent fait accompli.

its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: J Cord
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project.
This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts. This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have
unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

and public trust.

subject: Written Comments
name: Susan Childress
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.
The Commission votes March 5th. The East Wing is already demolished. But the record of public opposition
matters. Make your voice heard.

subject: Written Comments
name: Pennie Kost
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project. As
mentioned above, this project was initiated without the proper authorization, permits, or design review. It
is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American history. Project approval needs to
be denied and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design.
Thank you!

modernization project but rather a destruction of American history at the hands of an administration which
prioritizes Mr. Trump’s self-promotion over the American people. I want this project canceled and the East
Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design.

permitting, zoning or code requirements because the structure is on White House grounds.” By funding the
project through donors rather than taxpayers, Mr. Trump is cutting legislators out of the process. I do not
believe he can be trusted to complete this project properly. (Source: The New York Times: Inside Trump’s
Push to Make the White House Ballroom as Big as Possible, 11/30/25)

concerned about that. President Harry S. Truman appointed a bipartisan six-person commission to oversee
renovations in the 1940s. He consulted the American Society of Civil Engineers and the Commission of Fine
Arts. However, “Mr. Trump has not taken the project to Congress for funding or debate, instead saying he
and private donors would provide the money. No bipartisan commission is overseeing the construction.
Money for the project is going into a fund that is not subject to transparency laws.” (Source: The New York
Times: Before Renovating White House, Truman Got Buy-In From Congress and Experts, 10/23/25)
Given the reckless manner in which this project has been executed thus far, I’m also concerned about
potential health hazards for anyone directly - or indirectly - exposed to the demolition/construction. My
father died from mesothelioma and I understand that dangers such as asbestos exposure must be taken
very seriously. I do not trust the leaders of this project to handle those concerns with transparency and
proper safety procedures.

subject: Written Comments
name: Sally Oldham
body:
The design of this proposed "modernization" is appalling. The White House East Wing was demolished with
no prior review. The proposed design is totally out of scale with the White House and grounds. Its
architectural design mimics that of the White House but at a far larger and grander scale which is
inappropriate for an addition to this National Park site. It violates the New Construction Standard of the
Secretary of the Interior's Standards for New Construction by its outsized scale and by making no
differentiation from the design of the White House itself. Its grand portico becomes more prominent than
the facade of the White House itself. It reduces the open space around the White House significantly. If it
were warranted to build such a monumental and mammoth structure, it should be built underground so as
to maintain the primacy of the White House which often is called the People's House.

name: TIA RIBARY
body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history, for the ego of one man.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States. This is the house of the People of the United States and NO
individual has the right to destruct or significantly change our house without Congressional approval. Stop
this chaos.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Ilana Zablow
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

should have a ballroom that strives to rival authoritarian regimes from around the world.
I've said enough, everyone knows this was wrong and done without the approval of the people he's
supposed to serve.
Sincerely,
Bridget Wilder

subject: Written Comments
name: Erin Scheessele
body:
I would quote Gerard Koskavich: "The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park,
owned by the American people and home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time
is not the owner of the property or the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose
interventions are limited by law and by respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion."

body:

permits, just tear it down. That is not HIS house-it is “We the people’s” house and I for one want it restored

deco style. It sat on really precious real estate. At the top of Fremont St. They tore that beautiful building
down & built Main Street Station. Another casino.
Please, please stop this project from going forward and rebuild the East wing of MY house. Thank you.
Regards,
Thomasine Duncan

subject: Written Comments
name: Connie Scott
body:
East Wing I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site
should occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being
funded by large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least
the appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.
Connie Scott
Sullivan, Missouri

subject: Written Comments
name: Tracey Allen
body:
Historic Preservation and the East Wing Modernization Project
The demolition of the east wing of the United States Capitol represents a serious failure of historic
stewardship and public accountability. This action was undertaken without appropriate authorization,
without required permitting, and without meaningful review or recognition of the historic value of the
structure. Such actions directly undermine the legal and ethical frameworks intended to protect nationally
significant historic resources.
The Capitol is not merely a functional government building; it is a material record of the nation’s political,
architectural, and civic history. The destruction of a historically significant portion of this structure
constitutes an irreversible loss to the public and to future generations.
Equally concerning is the broader East Wing Modernization Project, including the proposed construction of
a 90,000-square-foot ballroom addition to the White House complex. This proposal is wholly inappropriate
in scale, function, and character. It does not respect the architectural integrity of the original White House,
nor does it harmonize with the surrounding historic context.
The White House complex is defined by restraint, proportion, and symbolism. Introducing a massive new
ballroom addition would fundamentally disrupt this balance, overwhelm the existing architecture, and
erode the historic landscape. Such an intervention prioritizes spectacle over preservation and establishes a
dangerous precedent for future alterations to nationally significant sites.
Historic buildings of this importance are not interchangeable development sites. Their value lies in
authenticity, continuity, and adherence to long-standing preservation standards. Modernization cannot be
used to justify unchecked expansion or the loss of historically meaningful fabric.
As a member of the public concerned with historic preservation, I believe approval of this proposal would
undermine the standards this body is charged with upholding.
The demolition already undertaken and the proposed construction now under consideration reflect a
troubling disregard for established preservation laws, review processes, and public accountability. This body
should reject the East Wing Modernization Project in its current form and require full compliance with all
applicable historic preservation and permitting requirements.
I urge this body to deny approval of the proposed 90,000-square-foot ballroom addition. The project is
fundamentally incompatible with the historic character, scale, and setting of the White House complex and
would result in an unnecessary and irreversible alteration to a nationally significant landmark. Approval
would set a damaging precedent for future interventions at historic civic sites. This proposal should be
rejected in full.

subject: Written Comments
name: Catherine Leo
body:
The demolition of the White House East Wing is a profound loss of American history, replacing a space of
quiet, functional, and historic significance with an impractical, indulgent ballroom. It erases decades of, for
example, First Lady initiatives and public tours. This act signifies a disregard for the delicate, integrated
stewardship required for one of the nation's most crucial, symbolic, and protected landmarks.
Why the Destruction is Misguided
Irreplaceable History: The East Wing, while not part of the original 1800 structure, served as the functional
heart of modern White House activity, from Eleanor Roosevelt’s offices to the founding of the White House
Historical Association.
Symbolic Disruption: Replacing this center of "functional modesty" with a luxurious, large-scale
entertainment venue converts a place of democratic service into a space of elite spectacle, disrupting the
intended, harmonious design of the entire White House complex.
Erosion of Trust: Proceeding without full transparency or public engagement undermines the established,
protective processes for American civic architecture.
Why a Ballroom is Impractical and Improper
Tone-Deaf Luxury: Constructing a massive ballroom during times of national, economic uncertainty (such as
federal shutdowns) is viewed as profoundly insensitive, according to The Washington Informer.
Functional Misalignment: The White House is primarily a working office, home, and national museum—not
a convention center, says The New Yorker.
Ignoring Proper Stewardship: The demolition disregarded established guidelines for preserving historic
structures, prioritizing personal,, aesthetic, or event-driven changes over the preservation of the building's,
as a whole, integrity, note The Architect’s Newspaper and The American Institute of Architects: AIA.
This act is not merely an alteration; it is a dismantling of the "People’s House" to suit temporary, personal
whim rather than the enduring, public, and historic mission of the site, argue The New Yorker and The
Washington Informer.

I am utterly opposed to this project in any way, shape, or form, regardless of its cost. It was stealthily
started without any of the usual proper authorization, permitting, or design review. There is nothing
"modernizing" about it; it is a tasteless uglification proposed by a delusional man who thinks an oversized
ballroom would somehow suit HIM better. The public be damned.

the American people and the temporary residence of our sitting presidents since 1800. For over 200 years,
presidential changes and updates to the White House have been limited by law and by respect for the
people of the United States, its rightful owners.

consultation with) the National Capital Planning Commission, without permits, without design review,

deliberate insult to the American people, the White House's true owners.
I realize the difficulty of reining in the current president's illegal actions, the scale of which this nation has
never seen, but I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to REQUIRE rebuilding the East Wing as it
was, at the personal expense of the current president. I have just amazed myself by writing this request
without using the profanity waiting to burst forth. Thank you for reading this; I know that I speak for many,
many appalled Americans.

body:

Wing is the most despicable architectural action taken by any president. The White House belongs to the
citizens of the US. It is not the palace of a king. The East Wing was the office of First Ladies, and thus an
important part of the nation's heritage. We do not need a ballroom - White House events can be held in
numerous other venues in Washington DC. The addition is too big for the site. It makes the White House
looks small. The design is banal and tepid. The arrogance of this whole project is mind boggling.

subject: Written Comments
name: Marcy Woodruff
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Mary Frazer
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States. While it is certainly true that past Presidents have left their
mark on the White House and associated public properties, it must be done through proper, legal
processes.
While the White House is exempt from Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, it is still
subject to regulations regarding extensive changes. The demolition of the historic East Wing without
review, without permits, and without Congressional oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it
is a violation of the trust of the American people who were given no opportunity to comment on what
should have been presented as a proposal and not as a violent fait accompli.
I oppose this project as proposed, both because of the illegal nature of its initiation, and the questionable
nature of the scale, scope, and funding for the project. Elevation drawings presented at the meeting are
deliberately presented to diminish the size and visual impact of this structure, which will ultimately dwarf
the Executive Mansion from all viewpoints. This is not a dignified gathering space for world leaders, but a
convention center mimicking the palatial residences of monarchs, rather than a needful addition to the
People's House.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in visual scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion, as appropriate to
the preservation of historic properties.
The solicitation of private funds to to support the effort must be done with full transparency, and without
implied favors or special treatment for investors. No one is above the law and to permit this project to go
ahead without respect for that law would be an affront to all law-abiding Americans and the rule of law in
this country.

subject: Written Comments
name: Terri Toppler
body:
The White House is a historic building. Yes, it's been "renovated" under different administrations, but to
what degree have these "renovations" been and did they not first seek authorization and oversight from
Congress or The White House Historical Association or the National Park Service? Was there not a review of
the design before demolition? In this present case, there has been no authorization and no oversight.
Last summer the President said he was going to renovate the East Wing. He did not say he would have it
torn down. There's a big difference in what he said and what has happened. Again, no authorization and no
oversight. Was the National Park Service consulted? The White House Historical Association consulted? No.
When I sent a concerned email to Senator Grassley, my Iowa senator, his reply was about past presidents
who constructed a Rose Garden, built an outdoor swimming pool or an indoor bowling alley, resurfaced the
tennis court, etc. I didn't see demolition in any of these remarks nor lack of approval or oversight.
Which makes me wonder, can any president going forth demolish the White House itself and add a luxury
condo on the spot? My response would be if you don't like living in a historic building with all of its charm
and small living spaces, then don't run for the presidency, because this is "The People's House", and it
belongs to the citizens of the United States.
So, where's the oversight? If there is none, then "Houston, we have a problem."

subject: Written Comments
name: Britt Thurman
body:
The White House is not the President’s personal residence to alter at will; it is the People’s House. Every
president is a temporary steward of this building, entrusted with its care for future generations. That
stewardship comes with an obligation to respect both the history of the structure and the democratic
principles it represents.
The United States was deliberately built on a system of checks and balances to prevent the concentration of
power in any single individual. That is why we have three branches of government, and it is also why
changes to the White House are subject to review by bodies such as the National Capital Planning
Commission (NCPC), the Commission of Fine Arts (CFA), and the National Park Service (NPS). These
processes exist to ensure transparency, accountability, and public oversight — not as obstacles, but as
safeguards for a shared national asset. Disregarding them undermines the very democratic principles the
White House is meant to symbolize.
The funding model for the proposed ballroom raises serious ethical concerns. Money at this scale is never
free. Millionaires and billionaires who “donate” vast sums to a project of this nature reasonably expect
influence, access, or favorable treatment in return. Accepting such donations for alterations to the White
House creates the appearance — if not the reality — that the executive branch is for sale. This perception
erodes public trust and is fundamentally incompatible with ethical governance.
The White House is one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world and a powerful symbol of
American democracy and history. Preserving historic structures follows well-established principles:
demolition should occur only when no viable alternatives exist, and additions should never overwhelm,
diminish, or visually dominate the original building. The proposed ballroom, by its scale and design, violates
these principles.
In my view, this project reads as a vanity endeavor rather than a public necessity. We already know the
dangers of leaders who seek to immortalize themselves through monuments, oversized structures, and the
renaming of public institutions. A ballroom of this magnitude is unnecessary, visually grotesque, and out of
character with the White House’s historic integrity.
To be clear, I am not opposed to the idea of a ballroom in general. I am opposed to the scale of the one
proposed, the disregard for established review processes, and the ethically troubling manner in which it is
being funded. The White House should reflect restraint, democratic values, and respect for history — not
ego, excess, or transactional influence.

demolition of the White House’s East Wing—a project that began without proper authorization, permits, or
design review. This initiative is not a modernization effort; it amounts to the wholesale destruction of a
piece of American heritage.

public trust, not an owner with unchecked power.

participate in decisions that shape our national monuments. I urge the National Capital Planning
Commission to mandate a reconstruction that faithfully preserves the historic design and scale of the East
Wing, ensuring any new construction on the site remains compatible and subordinate to the original
structure.
Thank you for your time and attention to this important matter.

subject: Written Comments
name: John Stoner
body:
As an American historian, I'm shocked by the abrupt decision (apparently without permits or planning
permissions) to demolish the East Wing of the White House and replace it with something that stands to
overshadow the residence itself. The built environment of the government is both functional and symbolic
and thus careful planning is necessary in order to maintain or improve its function and the symbolism
attached to it. While the White House has not been a static object over the years, no recent administration
has attempted something so major without a significant consultative process beforehand. The decision
making should be collaborative, the designs should be consonant not with the aesthetic tastes of one
leader, but with the overall style of the building (and/or reflecting national architectural styles). If the White
House is expected to continue serving as the People's House, any renovation must reflect ongoing needs
and not the imperatives of the current occupant.

subject: Written Comments
name: Barbara Laws
body:
Any occupant of The White House is not a king, but a temporary tenant, living there 8 years at most, and
should not be able to rebuild it to his/her own liking no matter who is paying for it. From this point on, the
processes in place, specified in federal law, must be followed to approve and make these changes.
Neither is the White House a palace. It is the people's house, not overwhelmingly large, but prior to the
demolition commanded the space properly. Its design is unified and aesthetically pleasing with its
restrained, formal, and symmetrical Georgian-Irish architectural style. Any addition should be compatible in
scale and subordinate to the original structure. That which is proposed appears to be large enough to
overwhelm the existing building and space.
Given that the destruction of the East Wing has already taken place, a construction of similar size, shape,
and placement as the West Wing - with needed modern updates including ADA accessibility - would
maintain the integrity and symmetry of the overall design and structure thus remaining true to its
aesthetics and historical past.
The White House is not in need of a huge ballroom. DC has plenty of that kind of space in existing buildings.
If it is determined that a ballroom absolutely is needed, construct it elsewhere in the city or, if in the end a
ballroom is included in the new construction, ensure that it fit within an addition of similar size and design
as the original.

body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which has made it clear that influence has
been bought. This undermines the very thin trust we the people still have.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project. Our
history has been shat on.

subject: Written Comments
name: Elizabeth Humstone
body:
To the Commission: This project has concerned me from the moment the East Wing was demolished
without a demolition permit to this proposal for a new grandiose ballroom facility. I do think the applicant
should be penalized for not getting proper permits for the demolition. I am opposed to the project as
currently designed for the following reasons: 1)The scale of the project is enormous, too big and will
overshadow the rest of the White House dominating the landscape for the lavish parties and dinners for a
privileged few as opposed to the White House where the important policy and administrative work on
behalf of all the American people takes place. The scale proposed is consistent with this current
administration's favoring of the rich and famous over ordinary Americans. 2) The cost of the project,
regardless of the source of the funds, is excessive and such funds would be put to better use providing for
the basic needs of Americans for health care, affordable housing, child care, education and employment - a
priority national need that is not being addressed at this time. 3) The proposed project is ostentatious and
lavish consistent with its design for the rich and famous and not the average American. A more modest
proposal with less ornate embellishments and at a smaller scale might be found to be more acceptable. A
more thoughtful approach to the planning for the future of this significant national treasure, that is, the
entire White House Complex, is needed; one that prioritizes the important work of any administration in
conducting our country's domestic and foreign affairs over having extravagant parties and receptions and
one that demonstrates respect for the historic preservation of important buildings and natural landscape
features and the symbolism of this revered national monument. Elizabeth Humstone, Former Advisor from
Vermont to the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments

body:
I was appalled and heartbroken at the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a
national historic site should occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this
$300M project is being funded by large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which
creates at the very least, the appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public
trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American history.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability. The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and
major alterations should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant
project.
I want this project cancelled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design.
Thank you.

I oppose the so called “East Wing Modernization”. I believe that a modernization of a historical building
presumes that the actual structure and edifice remain intact. It is the infrastructure that is modernized
which would include everything from plumbing, heating, electrical and work space improvements to
technological and security upgrades. This is a vanity project for a single man and not for the American
people. The project defies all sensibilities, ignores the very checks and balances put in place to prevent this
corrupt and blatant abuse of power and insults our American architectural history. My heart weeps for its
destruction. If it were within my personaI power I would order the rebuilding of the East Wing, to its
original design, at the expense of those that ordered its demolition. Any “modernization” would then be
subject to congressional review and approval as dictated by law - something that all of us are supposed to
be bound by, even the President of the United States.

body:

Trump's proposed alterations show nothing but contempt for the historical significance of the White House.

modest symbol of our republic and replace it with Trumps' tasteless homage to Louis XIV . The fact that the
private money of billionaires is financing this project is also a debasement of our values as Americans. Do
not approve this project, whose scope, size, and aesthetics are extremely ugly in every sense of the word.
Sincerely,
Deborah Katz
Denver, Colorado

subject: Written Comments
name: Patricia Maurer
body:
I am strongly opposed to the plan to build a massive and architecturally inappropriate ball room as a
replacement for the East Wing of the White House. I support returning the East Wing and the Rose Garden
to their original design and purposes. A president is the custodian of the people's house and has no
authority to make sweeping changes that are not in keeping with the historical significance of any national
treasure or monument. It matters not to me that it is supposedly being paid for with donations. What
matters is the assumption that a president can do what he or she wants and likes. The proposed design is
certainly big, but I would hardly call it beautiful and, if the selected decor is anything like the Oval Office
redo, it will be gaudy and in poor taste. I remember the first time I saw the East Wing on a tour with my
mother in 1965 and the second time I saw it on a tour with my sixth grade students in 1976. We were in
awe and I wept when it was destroyed.

subject: Written Comments
name: Donna Pitts
body:
I am writing to oppose the proposed East Wing Modernization project at the White House. This project,
now estimated to cost between $300 and $400 million, was initiated without the required public notice,
proper permitting, or advance design review by this Commission. The demolition of the historic East Wing
began in October 2025 before any formal plans had been submitted, denying the public and this body the
opportunity to weigh in before irreversible damage was done.
Calling this a "modernization" misrepresents what actually occurred. The East Wing, a historic structure that
served first ladies and their offices for decades, was completely demolished. Historic magnolia trees planted
in honor of Presidents Harding and Roosevelt were removed. The Presidential Emergency Operations
Center was dismantled. This is not renovation; it is erasure.
I am also deeply concerned about the funding mechanism. Accepting hundreds of millions of dollars in
private donations from tech billionaires and other wealthy interests to reshape the People's House creates
serious conflicts of interest and the appearance, if not the reality, of purchased access to the presidency. No
single donor should have influence over the character of our national home.
The White House belongs to the American people, not to any administration or its financial backers. The
Commission exists precisely to ensure that projects of this magnitude undergo rigorous, transparent, and
lawful review. I urge this Commission to conduct a thorough, independent, and uncompromising evaluation
of this project — and to demand full accountability for the process violations that have already occurred.
No one is above the law. Approving this project without meaningful consequence for the procedural
violations that enabled it would set a dangerous precedent for future administrations and for historic
preservation nationwide.

subject: Written Comments
name: Barb Bullock
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project as currently proposed and urge the Commission to reject the
plan until proper legal processes are followed.
This project began with the demolition of a 123 year old structure before obtaining required approvals from
this Commission, before completing mandatory environmental assessments under the National
Environmental Policy Act, and before securing congressional authorization required by federal statute for
construction on federal parkland in Washington. The fact that demolition has already occurred does not
excuse these violations or create a fait accompli that forces approval.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts. This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest,
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No president should have
unilateral authority to demolish historical structures and the approve construction without following the
law and allowing input from the public.
I strongly urge the Commission to reject this project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Margaret Brown
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The sitting President is not the owner of the property or the structures. The
President is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by rules governing planning,
implementation, and oversight.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is a violation of the law.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size.
I also urge investigation into the destruction of this historic site and an accounting to Congress and to the
American people of what was removed, where it was stored, and how it is being preserved. If historic items
were not documented and preserved, I urge a thorough accoutning, through document and photo research,
of all the items that were destroyed by the sitting holder of the office of the president. While the East Wing
cannot be replaced in spirit, every effort should be made to preserve its legacy and to restore its physical
structure in a manner in keeping with the exisitng structure. In no way should the President and those who
followed his illegal orders to destroy the East Wing be rewarded for their actions through the approval and
building of a golden ballroom.

subject: Written Comments
name: Robert Randall Vosbeck, FAIA emeritus Robert Randall Vosbeck
body:
I am a former president of the American Institute of Architects, and a former member of the NCPC 1976-
1980 appointed by President Ford. MY architectural firm, VVKR, located in Alexandria, VA, provided various
"small' design projects at the West Wing of the White House being commissioned by the General Services
Administration in the President Nixon era. Two rather significant projects were the conversion of the FDR
swimming poll to the White House Press Room and the Portico to the West Wing. President Nixon's
instructions were to design the new Press Room is such a way that the FDR pool could be returned to the
same space and configuration if there was an outcry that he had removed the pool. We accomplished that
requirement in the design.
Another project by VVKR was the design of a portico for the West Wing and improve the entrance
appearance and driveway to the West Wing. We followed the basic architecture of the White House and
the portico and surrounding area was a huge visual improvement to the area. With this background, I am
now a member of the White House Historical Association.
I state all of the above to provide my credentials for commenting on the East Wing modernization project.
First off, I want to congratulate Shalom Baranes and his firm for an excellent set of preliminary drawings
showing the proposed East Wing modernization project. However, they have provided me with strong
feeling that the ballroom project is just too large and out of scale in essentially dwarfing the residence.
While the design is conscious to keep the height of the ballroom no higher than the residence, in my view, it
should be substantially lower than the residence. Alos, it appears that the oval driveway on the southwest
side of the ballroom had to be moved to accommodate the ballroom. This a serious site plan flaw I feel.
In conclusion, I feel the destruction of the East Wing was a tragedy and a huge mistake. What's done is
done, so now I strongly suggest the mass, size and height of the ballroom be reduced significantly to lessen
the impact on the remaining, existing structure.
Respectfully submitted,
R. Randall Vosbeck, FAIA Emeritus

must be followed - by the president as well as everyone else.

subject: Written Comments
name: Jeanine Hearne Barsamian
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people, not
the current temporary occupant.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not the
violent demolition on national TV.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

body:

This work appears to have moved forward without proper authorization, permits, or a meaningful design
review. That is not acceptable for any public project, and it is especially unacceptable at a site that carries
this level of national significance.
Calling this modernization does not match what has happened. What I see is a loss of history and character

as faithfully as possible.
No one is above the law. Allowing this to continue, without accountability for those who ignored the
required process, would be an insult to every law abiding American who is expected to follow the rules.

subject: Written Comments
name: Christine Gutierrez
body:
I urge you to vote NO on the East Wing “modernization” project, which is in reality a privately financed
vanity rebuild of a historic public space that has already been demolished to make room for President
Trump’s new ballroom. This project raises profound concerns about pay\u8209 -to\u8209 -play politics,
donor influence over federal decision\u8209 -making, and the erosion of basic ethics and transparency
standards.
President Trump has repeatedly boasted that the new 90,000\u8209 -square\u8209 -foot ballroom
replacing the East Wing will be built at “zero cost to the American taxpayer” and paid for entirely by private
donors and himself. He has publicly claimed they have raised between 300 and 400 million dollars in “donor
money and money that we put up,” and framed this as “many generous Patriots, Great American
Companies, and yours truly” funding his project. Trump has turned a core part of the White House complex
into a privately financed construction project, marketed as a personal achievement instead of a carefully
vetted public facility.
The White House has released a list of 30\u8209 -plus donors for the ballroom, which now replaces the
demolished East Wing, and they are not neutral charities or small civic groups. They include:
• Major tech firms with substantial federal interests and regulatory exposure, such as Amazon, Google,
Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Coinbase and Palantir.
• Defense and government contractors like Lockheed Martin, Booz Allen Hamilton, Caterpillar and others
that rely heavily on federal contracts and favorable policy.
• Powerful private individuals and billionaires with long\u8209 -standing business or political ties to Trump,
such as Harold Hamm, Stephen Schwarzman, the Adelson and Perlmutter families, and the Winklevoss
twins.
These donations are being funneled through the Trust for the National Mall as “charitable” contributions,
and many are tax\u8209 -deductible, further complicating transparency and public oversight. Ethics
watchdogs have already documented that at least two dozen of these donors are active federal lobbyists or
companies that should be disclosing these gifts on lobbying reports, but often are not.
This funding model fits a well\u8209 -established pattern in Trump’s public life: using large private
donations and personal relationships to blur the line between public policy and personal benefit. Legal and
ethics experts have already warned that Trump personally inviting executives and billionaire donors to
White House dinners, and then directly soliciting money for a project he treats as his own, creates a classic
“soft” quid\u8209 -pro\u8209 -quo situation.
As Columbia law professor Richard Briffault explained, many of these donors do “significant” business with
the federal government, and Trump’s personal solicitation “raises concerns about what these companies
will be receiving in return.” He notes that even if it is not a literal, explicit trade, the message is effectively:
if you give, the administration will look favorably on you; if you refuse, you risk being frozen out. This is
exactly the kind of coercive, transactional politics that has defined Trump’s past behavior and prior scandals
involving foreign governments, campaign donors, and personal business deals.
In this specific project, the donors are not just buying their names on a plaque.
Approving this rebuild endorses a system where:
• Corporations with active or pending federal contracts donate to the president’s pet project while
simultaneously seeking favorable treatment on procurement, regulation, antitrust scrutiny, and mergers.
• Tech companies facing antitrust investigations, AI and data\u8209 -privacy regulation, and content\u8209
-moderation fights gain a unique channel of access by bankrolling a private presidential project.
• Defense and energy donors with billions at stake in Pentagon contracts and federal leasing policies send a
signal that they are “team players,” expecting smoother paths for their deals, permits, and subsidies.
Ethics groups have already warned that a large share of these donors stand to benefit directly from White
House or federal agency decisions, and that the contributions should be disclosed as lobbying\u8209 -
adjacent influence efforts. When you combine this with Trump’s personal branding and public bragging
about the ballroom, the project looks less like civic philanthropy and more like a transactional access\u8209
-buying scheme centered on a president who has repeatedly used public office to serve himself.
By the time NCPC is being asked to approve this so\u8209 -called modernization, the East Wing has already
been demolished, and the donors have already been cultivated and thanked at White House events. A “yes”
vote now does not simply green\u8209 -light construction; it retroactively blesses an arrangement where:
• A historic wing of the White House was torn down before full, transparent review by the very planning
commission meant to oversee such work.
• A massive, privately funded presidential vanity project is allowed to proceed largely on the terms set by
the president and his donors, not the public.
• Corporations and billionaires with huge financial stakes in federal decisions are invited to “donate” in
ways that function as a quasi\u8209 -coercive loyalty test for doing business with this administration.
NCPC should not legitimize this funding scheme by approving the rebuild. Instead, you should demand full
disclosure of donor amounts, a detailed ethics review of each donor’s current and pending federal
interests, and a public accounting of how demolition was allowed to move forward before robust planning
oversight.
For all of these reasons, I urge you in the strongest possible terms to vote NO on the East Wing
Modernization Project and refuse to ratify a donor\u8209 -driven, quid\u8209 -pro\u8209 -quo\u8209 -
tainted rebuild of a public institution that should belong to the American people—not to Trump and his
benefactors.
Instead, insist on a full Environmental Impact Statement that rigorously compares “no\u8209 -build,”
smaller\u8209 -build, and off\u8209 -site alternatives before any new construction proceeds.
• Require meaningful consultation with preservation bodies like the National Trust for Historic Preservation
and the Commission of Fine Arts, which have already objected to moving ahead without proper review.
• Align any future proposal with NCPC’s submission guidelines, including full disclosure of alternatives,
master\u8209 -plan consistency, and detailed analysis of public views and access.
Preservation groups are already in court arguing that the current project should be halted until these
processes are completed; NCPC can reinforce that position.

subject: Written Comments
name: Meera White
body:
I'm amazed that the proposed building is NOT ADA-compliant. The only entrances to the ballroom are
stairs. So everyone who needs mobility aids such as wheelchairs or canes, must gain access through the
main White House entrance? So if there is a fire or another emergency, those individuals must find their
way back to the White House, rather than being able to speedily exit the ballroom directly? I implore the
architectural firm to design a ballroom that is fit to invite in all members of the U.S. public, not just those
who are able to get up stairs easily. If this ballroom is going to be a beacon of U.S. modernity and
hospitality, then the current design is very clear that disabled people are not to be invited or thought of in
ballroom events. That is such a discouraging thing to promote through design. Please find ways to make this
building accessible through ramps at entry, elevators within, and wider door frames - i.e. ADA-compliant.

subject: Written Comments
name: Beth Morsman
body:
To whom it may concern,
The tragedy of seeing The White House East Wing totally demolished with no clear, approved plan, is more
than disappointing. It is a sad representation of how our nation is being viewed on the world stage today;
destroy a place and then hope for the best.
We are not a country that flaunts our wealth. We do not cover our walls in gold. We do not build Versailles
ballrooms. We do not need to honor our democracy with baubles and diamonds. We honor our democracy
with grace and diplomacy.
We know that our present occupant described The White House despairingly during his first term and is
using this term to destroy our humble heritage. Enough damage has been done to The People’s House. We
have a patio eating area where a beautiful rose garden used to grow. We have an Oval Office that looks like
it was poorly decorated by an emir. We have “artwork” hanging on the walls that is on par with velvet
paintings. We have hotel signage identifying the Oval Office as if the occupants couldn’t find it without a
sign. And now, we have a whole wing destroyed with no historically complementary plan to replace it—just
a gapping hole.
If we need an appropriate venue for hold events to honor the nation’s guests and allies, I can understand
that need. But, please, demand that this space not become a monstrous disgrace. It’s the White HOUSE,
not a PALACE. And, please, demand it be named in keeping with the rest of The White House.
Thank you for listening.

subject: Written Comments
name: Denise Beaudoin
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

when many are poor and frightened, many more distrustful of our government. Building a gilded hall that
only the richest and most powerful will use at such a delicate time, and at such great cost, hurts us as a
Nation, with Justice and Liberty, intended For All.

Mary Hake

body:
I am writing to object to the construction of the White House East Wing ballroom. The White House does
not belong to one person or administration and decisions about structural changes must be made in
consultation with a larger group who represent the interests of the American people, not just that one
person. The White House is a public historic monument that represents our national heritage as much or
more so than other historic monuments.
There are so many more reasons that this project is wrong:
- the scale of it
- the private funding
- the overall design
- it’s questionable utility (how often is there a need for a 1000 seat ballroom?)
- the expense and sustainability to maintain it
I could go on, but I’d rather stay civil. Thank you for asking!

subject: Written Comments
name: Linda Giles
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Jane Nunn
body:
The White House is the People of the United States’ house, and the individual occupying the office of the
President of the United States is merely a tenant with no right to unilaterally change any of the White
House’s structures or designs. As proposed by the current administration, a 90,000 square foot ballroom is
not only unnecessary but does not fit in with the remaining architecture of the White House. It is
ostentatious and gauche with the feel of a Las Vegas casino or something found in one of the ornate
palaces of Europe rather than the strong, stately, and dignified design of the White House. While it is
understood that modern upgrades were needed to the original East Wing, this did not necessitate the
tearing down of this entire wing of the White House. Restore the original size, look, and interior design of
the East Wing, with modifications being done to the infrastructure (electrical, plumbing, heating, cooling,
etc) and sizes of some of the rooms as deemed necessary to appropriately carry out presidential functions.
The renovations should capture the architectural look, feel, and style of the existing White House rather
than something at the whim of one individual, regardless of the office that person holds.

subject: Written Comments
name: Christine Kenlan-Laurent
body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
Thank you,
Chris

thoughts in mind.
