body:
I have a massters degree in Community and Regional Planning, University of New Mexico, School of
Architecture and Planning. I served municipal and county administrations over some 22 years.
Reviewing the demolition of the East Wing of the White House it seems clear that this is not a renovation or
modernization project of an existing structure. There is no existing structure. The wrecking ball destroyed
an important component of American History as well as destroying the beauty and architectural
authenticity of the White House.
The reconstruction of the East Wing, as it was approved and permitted decades ago, is critically important
to restore the balance and beauty of the original construction. The historic district of Washington, DC,
stands as a testament to American history and is spectacularly beautiful architecturally. The proposed
replacement structure is not to the appropriate scale or style of the East Wing as well as the entire struction
of the White House. It will dwarf the rest of the structure, and destroy the visual balance so carefully
planned and constructed more than 100 years ago.
Please do not approve any plans for this so-called ball room. Restore the site to the original plan.
Thank you for allowing me to comment.

approving those contracts.

unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

subject: Written Comments
name: Patricia White
body:
It is very troubling that the process for making changes to a National Historic Landmark and National Park
have not been followed in the case of the East Wing of the White House. i understand that modifications
have been made by various presidents over time, but demolishing the entire East Wing with no notice or
review is shocking. Laws and procedures should be followed. The White House belongs to the American
people, not any given occupant, and the public should be consulted before wholesale destruction takes
place. it is also troubling that the plans keep changing with no input from the public. It is one thing to make
internal changes to a small area of the building, but to demolish a significant segment with no public
process feels radical, overbearing and disrespectful.
It is also very troubling that Congress is not being asked to appropriate funds to build this new structure.
Taking private donations opens the process up to mass corruption. There already seems to be enough of
that going around and we certainly don't need to encourage private donors to pour money into a non-
transparent pot from which they might well expect favors. it is just shocking to me that Congress would
permit/encourage such potential corruption.

subject: Written Comments
name: Jennifer Madigan
body:
Public Comment Opposing the East Wing Reconstruction and Ballroom Addition
I am writing to express my strong opposition to the proposed East Wing modernization and ballroom
addition project currently under review.
The White House is not merely a residence. It is a nationally significant civic landmark and a central
component of the symbolic and physical plan of the Nation’s Capital. Decisions affecting its footprint,
massing, and function must be evaluated with the utmost regard for preservation standards, long term
planning principles, and the public interest.
The demolition of the historic East Wing constitutes a substantial loss to the architectural coherence and
historic integrity of the White House complex. The appropriate planning response to that loss is accurate
reconstruction consistent with the building’s documented historic design, scale, and purpose.
Reconstruction should follow established preservation frameworks, including the Secretary of the Interior’s
Standards for Reconstruction, which are intended to restore a vanished structure as it appeared during a
defined period of significance.
The proposed ballroom represents a significant programmatic and physical expansion beyond the historic
character of the East Wing. Such an addition would permanently alter the scale, footprint, and spatial
balance of the White House grounds. This change does not restore what was removed. Instead, it
introduces a new use and massing that departs from the established historic form of the site.
Under its federal planning mandate, the National Capital Planning Commission is charged with protecting
the character of federally owned land and ensuring that development within the National Capital Region
reflects sound planning principles and respect for historic resources. I urge the Commission to require that
any reconstruction of the East Wing adhere strictly to its historically documented specifications and to
reject the proposed ballroom addition as inconsistent with the preservation and planning responsibilities
entrusted to the Commission.
The White House complex is part of the enduring civic fabric of the Nation’s Capital. Its reconstruction
should reflect continuity, restraint, and fidelity to its historic form.

subject: Written Comments
name: Ellen Ives
body:
President Trump had no right to raze the East Wing of the White House, the People's House. Any building
on that site must have oversight and approval by Congress and the National Planning Commission. The
decor inside any structure must have oversight and approval so it isn't done only as Trump would have it --
not all gold inside as he has done with the Oval Office. Exercise your authority. Do not back down.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible in form and subordinate in
scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
Thank you,
Ellen Ives

body:

House is supposed to be for the American People - as a living monument to be utilized by the President of
the United States and their family during the time they were elected. The sitting President should not be
able to tear down any Government Building without getting approval by not only the Senate and Congress
but by the American Taxpayers, who help pay for the maintenance and upkeep.
With no disregard of the history of the East Wing and the White House, the current President demolished
the East Wing because he wanted a Ballroom. As a person lucky enough to get 2 tours of the White house
and marveled at the beauty and history of 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue, I'm appalled, angry and sad at what
has happened.
When Jacqueline Kennedy worked on the restoration of the White House, she did it with the help of experts
in all the fields of Construction, Decorators and specialized trades people. It was slow and methodical and
historically accurate. It was a committee of informed and connected people whose goal was to update and
restore the White House, not one man whose goal is make it as tacky and gaudy as possible.
Do not allow President Trump to destroy the White House any further.

subject: Written Comments
name: H. Dennis Shumaker
body:
I am writing in total opposition to the East Wing Modernization. The total, needless destruction of our East
Wing was done without the required oversight, established procedures and necessary permission that was
promulgated to protect the historic integrity, symmetry and context of this vitality important national
symbol.
The proposed structure is hideous. It is so out of proportion that it would dwarf our White House and make
it appear totally irrelevant and inconsequential - as if our White House was a mere appendage to it.
The supposed purpose of this construction is so limited and unnecessary as to be laughable when compared
to the alternative that has logically and successfully been employed for generations of proportional,
temporary structures on our grounds when special events are required.
The nearly half a billion dollar cost is an abomination, and because the source of the funding would come
from a few ultra wealthy donors, we have not been told what private use of this needless facility they have
demanded.
Finally, our East Wing must be completely and immediately restored, exactly as it was designed and built,
using all those portions of the historic structure that were saved. To not do so would allow and affirm the
criminal disregard of our laws and necessary protections and procedures that every president has been
subject to and required to comply with. No one, regardless of their power or wealth, is above the law.
Thank you for your consideration of my concerns.
H. Dennis Shumaker

name: Martin Solomon
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

I oppose any modernization which does not replicate the exterior of the demolished portions of the East
Wing as it appeared on January 20, 2025. My opposition is based on three issues.

presidential mansion has been compromised and if there is contamination by asbestos or other toxic
substances.

configuration. According to the latest news reports, there is the suggestion of tampering with the West
Wing portico to add a story to it like the East wing modernization. The will overwhelm the core mansion.

3. There is no need to turn the Executive Mansion into an entertainment venue because there are many
secure sites in Washington, DC, and if they are inadequate, a separate purpose-built structure with toilets,
parking, coatrooms, would be better.

name: Cheryl Meyers
body:
I am deeply concerned that the massing and height of the proposed new East Wing modernization and
White House ballroom will overwhelm the White House itself. The current plan is a monument to one
man’s ego, and does not represent input from the American people—owners of the White House.
According to the National Trust for Historic Preservation, of which I am a member: “The federally
recognized Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation offer clear guidance for construction
projects affecting historic properties. The Standards provide that new additions should not destroy the
historic fabric of the property and that the new work should be compatible with existing massing, size,
scale, and architectural features.”
I urge you to initiate the required federal review process—with input from the public —to ensure the
preservation of the historic proportions and features of the people’s White House for future generations,
including adherence to the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards for Rehabilitation.

name: John Kersting
body:
I am a 70 year old professional contractor, teacher, community leader and parent living in Olympia, WA, but
born in Milwaukee Wisconsin. Having professionally restored historical homes and buildings alongside my
brother, who has been doing this for over 40 years, we are horrified at the illegal, immoral and traitorous
ruination of the White Hous East Wing.
After the White House was attacked and burned in 1812 by British troops, it was rebuilt and expanded in a
respectful manner, retaining the function as a house and not an entertainment hall for the express purpose
of supporting the ideal that it is "The Peoples House."
The blatantly egotistical and selfish effort by it's current tenant is absurd, poorly managed and the
antithesis of our national intent.
My family, friends and many of our community leaders in Olympia absolutely oppose the spending of $300
million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization, permits, or design review.
When most of us break the law there are consequences including imprisonment, making amends, but laws
seem to only be an inconvenience to the powerful or arrogant present admiration.
It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American history. I want this project
canceled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design. No one is above the law and to
permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law would be an affront to all law-
abiding Americans.
My family has spent hundreds of hours stripping paints, manufacturing damaged decorations and restoring
turn of the century homes and buildings into community treasures on the Historical Registers of several
states. This betrayal of history, illegal act and slap in the face of previous presidents and the American
People should be stopped and those acting illegally, with a national treasure punished to the full extent of
the law! I have enclosed a picture of the restored Stensrud Building in Missoula, Montana, where my
brother and I brought it back when 6 months from the wrecking ball. America can and does better than this
present situation. Bring our White House BACK!!!

subject: Written Comments
name: Shannon Hawkins
body:
I oppose this project —  not because I resist change, but because I care deeply about stewardship, process,
and legacy.
The proposed spending feels excessive, especially given that it appears to have moved forward without
thorough design review, appropriate authorization, or full permitting. That concerns me. When we alter a
space as symbolic as the White House, the standard should be transparency, restraint, and respect for
institutional process.
I believe the White House may very well benefit from a ballroom or event space. But if we are going to build
something new, it should feel like it belongs there — architecturally, historically, and symbolically. The
White House is not a blank canvas for personal preference. It is a living piece of American history. Any
addition should honor that continuity, even if that means scaling expectations to fit the character of the
existing structure.
Most importantly, it should be approved through proper channels — with thoughtful design review, public
accountability, and bipartisan stewardship. And it should never carry the name of a current or former
president. This is not a private estate or a branding opportunity. It is the people’s house.
Public spaces deserve humility, not personalization. Leadership is temporary. The White House is not.

subject: Written Comments
name: Chad Kennedy
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. This $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
The funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current federal
contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the president who
controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and favorable
treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.

subject: Written Comments
name: Brooke English
body:
My concerns about the modernization project range from the lack of transparency regarding design to the
range and scope of an unneeded ballroom addition. While I understand that the proposed project, which
has already involved the complete destruction of the existing East Wing, is apparently no longer
“proposed,” this very fact is what causes me to speak up and out. This is the PEOPLE’S house. We, the
people, do not need or want a 1,000-person capacity ballroom. Since the White House was erected in 1800,
our presidents have successfully entertained heads of state and others in the existing White House
complex. Why do WE need a monstrous ballroom in order to conduct the business of government? Why
have all the presidents before this one been able to entertain guests without desecrating an historic
landmark?
Are there any guardrails in place for design? Who will determine what is and isn’t appropriate for this
historic site? Regardless of the funding source, we, the people, should have a say in the design choices,
especially now that this train has left the station. Where were the arbiters of design and permitting when
this project was first announced? Was there ANY input from those who oversee construction in DC,
especially that which affects historical sites?
I ask that a pause be struck; this has been a rushed process from the beginning, and I fear little to no
oversight, on behalf of Americans at large, has been solicited or provided. It is time for that.

name: Lisa J. McClure
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park. The American people own it. No
president owns the property or its buildings. The president knowingly broke laws and implied his disdain for
the citizens of this country.
.
To the National Capital Planning Commission: I urge you to require the following:
1. All reconstruction of the East Wing to maintain its historic design and size. Anything built on the
demolition site must match the style of the original structure of the Executive Mansion, and it must be
subordinate in size.
2. All reconstruction be funded only with appropriations from Congress and that no private money be
allowed for this project. The American people own the land, not any one president or any corporation
seeking to buy favor.
If Congress does not approve funding, and if a design keeping with the building's historical character cannot
be achieved, the land should be left vacant until such time as a legal and historically appropriate design
have been approved.
Demolishing the historic East Wing of the White House without review, without permits, and without
Congressional oversight clearly violated the law.
Please restore the White House to its original level of representation and respect.

name: Barsion Sylvia
body:

to Washington, DC with my graduating high school class. I loved being in the White House, seeing the
Lincoln Memorial and visiting the Smithsonian museums. Being an American gave me a great sense of pride.
Of all the changes that could be made, demolishing the East Wing to create a Ballroom is heartbreaking. I
am all for change and improving our country. But adding a Ballroom, when we have had perfectly elegant
state dinners for visiting dignitaries in the existing White House, is unnecessary. The White House is the
people’s house, and such a dramatic change should have required a national referendum. Otherwise, every
four or eight years, we are subject to the whims of Presidents, whether a Republican or Democrat. Please
do not allow that to happen.

subject: Written Comments
name: Victoria Bonasera
body:
To the Members of the National Capital Planning Commission,
I submit this public comment to object to the demolition of the White House East Wing, the addition of a
ballroom, and to call for an immediate halt to any further work.
The demolition of the East Wing without compliance with established planning and review requirements is
fundamentally inconsistent with the principles of the Comprehensive Plan for the National Capital. The Plan
emphasizes coordinated federal planning, stewardship of nationally significant resources, transparency in
decision-making, and adherence to orderly development processes. Proceeding with irreversible actions
outside of these processes undermines the federal interest the Commission is charged with protecting.
This unauthorized demolition also sets a dangerous precedent. If projects of this national significance can
advance without coordination, review, or accountability, the integrity of the federal planning framework—
and the Commission’s role within it—is weakened. In this  context, it is unreasonable to assume that future
submissions will be implemented as approved, or that conditions imposed through review will be
respected.
The proposed ballroom similarly conflicts with the Comprehensive Plan’s emphasis on demonstrated
federal purpose and public benefit. There is no identified operational, governmental, or planning need for
such a facility. An addition of this nature does not advance federal functions, improve public access, or
serve a clear national interest, and instead further compromises the historic character of a nationally
significant site.
I urge the Commission to:
* Call for an immediate halt to all related work;
* Acknowledge and address the demolition undertaken outside established planning and review processes;
* Require accountability and corrective action before considering any additional proposals; and
* Reject the premise that a ballroom is necessary or consistent with the goals of the Comprehensive Plan.
The White House is a cornerstone of the National Capital and a federal asset of the highest significance.
Alterations made without coordination, compliance, or consequence erode public trust and weaken the
principles of stewardship and orderly development that the Comprehensive Plan is intended to uphold.
Respectfully,
Victoria Bonasera

body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

a violent fait accompli.

in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Martin W Waldron
body:
I am STRONGLY OPPOSED to the construction of a 'grand presidential ballroom' to replace the illegally
demolished East Wing.
I call into question how the decision was made and whether safeguards for historic sites were effectively
bypassed.
The East Wing demolition was not subjected to the standard review processes under the National Historic
Preservation Act that typically apply to federal projects affecting historic structures, because the White
House is exempt from some of those requirements.
I believe proceeding without meaningful public input, advance notice, or review by the public, taxpayers,
the National Capitol Planning Commission, and all other relevant district and national planning bodies
undercuts transparency and sets a dangerous and illegal precedent for unilateral alterations to key national
landmarks.
I further challenge the president’s broad authority over the White House and any and all future changes to
it, including art, furnishings, and finishes. Private parties and private funding must be constrained and
prohibited from informal and unauthorized and unfunded norms and consultations when any changes are
proposed.
In addition, beyond the immediate design and process issues, I believe the proposed project is part of a
larger cultural and political battle against the civic, historic, and democratic ideals which the Capitol
represents to all Americans.
Moreover, I contend that replacing a wing associated with the history of the East Wing, its historical
association the first ladies and their many social initiatives with a grand presidential ballroom symbolizes a
shift toward elevating the executive image of the current president over shared civic history and the
national symbolism of the White House.
For me, an ordinary citizen who has visited or seen the East Wing, the demolition feels like a personal loss
of a “living, breathing” national home, not just a routine construction project.
For these and other more personal reasons I STRONGLY OPPOSE the construction of a 'grand presidential
ballroom, and support an historic reconstruction of the original East Wing.
Sincerely,
Martin W. Waldron AIA
Retired Architect
California License C14329

subject: Written Comments
name: Amy Rock
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States. While it is certainly true that past Presidents have left their
mark on the White House and associated public properties, it must be done through proper, legal
processes.
While the White House is exempt from Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, it is still
subject to regulations regarding extensive changes. The demolition of the historic East Wing without
review, without permits, and without Congressional oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it
is a violation of the trust of the American people who were given no opportunity to comment on what
should have been presented as a proposal and not as a violent fait accompli.
I oppose this project as proposed, both because of the illegal nature of its initiation, and the questionable
nature of the scale, scope, and funding for the project. Elevation drawings presented at the meeting are
deliberately presented to diminish the size and visual impact of this structure, which will ultimately dwarf
the Executive Mansion from all viewpoints. This is not a dignified gathering space for world leaders, but a
convention center mimicking the palatial residences of monarchs, rather than a needful addition to the
People's House.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in visual scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion, as appropriate to
the preservation of historic properties.
The solicitation of private funds to to support the effort must be done with full transparency, and without
implied favors or special treatment for investors. No one is above the law and to permit this project to go
ahead without respect for that law would be an affront to all law-abiding Americans and the rule of law in
this country.

formal congressional investigations and are proposing legislation to block similar future shakedowns called
the Stop Ballroom Bribery Act. Frankly, I think the White House should be restored for free by Trump
through his personal finances...not one cent of taxpayer money to rectify the situation and the corporations
should be fined at significant levels.

subject: Written Comments
name: Martin W Waldron
body:
I am STRONGLY OPPOSED to the construction of a 'grand presidential ballroom' to replace the illegally
demolished East Wing.
I call into question how the decision was made and whether safeguards for historic sites were effectively
bypassed.
The East Wing demolition was not subjected to the standard review processes under the National Historic
Preservation Act that typically apply to federal projects affecting historic structures, because the White
House is exempt from some of those requirements.
I believe proceeding without meaningful public input, advance notice, or review by the public, taxpayers,
the National Capitol Planning Commission, and all other relevant district and national planning bodies
undercuts transparency and sets a dangerous and illegal precedent for unilateral alterations to key national
landmarks.
I further challenge the president’s broad authority over the White House and any and all future changes to
it, including art, furnishings, and finishes. Private parties and private funding must be constrained and
prohibited from informal and unauthorized and unfunded norms and consultations when any changes are
proposed.
In addition, beyond the immediate design and process issues, I believe the proposed project is part of a
larger cultural and political battle against the civic, historic, and democratic ideals which the Capitol
represents to all Americans.
Moreover, I contend that replacing a wing associated with the history of the East Wing, its historical
association the first ladies and their many social initiatives with a grand presidential ballroom symbolizes a
shift toward elevating the executive image of the current president over shared civic history and the
national symbolism of the White House.
For me, an ordinary citizen who has visited or seen the East Wing, the demolition feels like a personal loss
of a “living, breathing” national home, not just a routine construction project.
For these and other more personal reasons I STRONGLY OPPOSE the construction of a 'grand presidential
ballroom, and support an historic reconstruction of the original East Wing.
Sincerely,
Martin W. Waldron AIA
Retired Architect
California License C14329

home to presidents since 1800. Any president at any time is not the owner of the property or the structures

its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Fran Bowman
body:
Hello,
Recently I attended a meeting of the Commission of Fine Arts at which the members discussed the East
Wing project with the architect. I learned that the ballroom would extend 300 feet ( a full football field's
length) in front of the White House. Also, the architect was asked to provide a physical scale model of the
proposed design which should be available to the National Capital Planning Commission for your review.
Like many other private citizens, I object to this grandiose addition which is completely out of scale with the
setting and other buildings in the area. Please ask the architect to go "back to the drawing board" and
follow through with the advice of the public in redesigning a suitable ballroom for this historic setting.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment,
Fran Bowman, California

subject: Written Comments
name: Cassandra Cyphers
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Wendy Hayden
body:
I strongly oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing and the construction of a new ballroom in
its place. The East Wing is more than an architectural feature, it is a space deeply connected to the legacy of
American women who shaped public life and national history. From First Ladies who used the East Wing for
press conferences, advocacy, and outreach, to generations of women staffers, journalists, and citizens who
carved out a place for their voices there, this part of the White House represents progress and participation
that should be preserved, not erased.
To spend $300 million on a vanity project funded by private donors, without proper authorization, public
input, or design review, is a misuse of both process and principle. This is not modernization; it is
destruction. The East Wing should be rebuilt and restored, with attention to the women’s history it
embodies. No one, however wealthy or well-connected, is above the law or the stewardship of our shared
national heritage.

subject: Written Comments
name: Lisa Scherber
body:
The proposed demolition of the East Wing of the White House—and its replacement with a donor \u8209 -
funded “ballroom” backed by tech billionaires—represents a profound breach of public trust and a direct
threat to America’s historic heritage. The National Trust for Historic Preservation is right to fight this, and
every American who values the rule of law and the preservation of our national identity should stand with
them.
I strongly oppose the allocation of $300 million for this project. It was launched without the legally required
authorization, permits, or design review— processes that exist specifically to protect national landmarks
from reckless alteration. Calling this a “modernization” is misleading. It is not an update or improvement; it
is a wholesale destruction of an irreplaceable piece of American history.
This project must be canceled. The East Wing should be rebuilt and restored to its original architectural
design, honoring the craftsmanship, symbolism, and national significance that it represents. No individual,
donor group, or administration is above the law. Allowing a project of this scale to proceed without
accountability for the violations already committed would undermine every principle of fair governance and
send the message that wealth and influence can override the legal protections that safeguard our shared
heritage.
Defending the East Wing is not merely about preserving a building—it is about preserving the integrity of
our institutions and the rule of law that binds us together as a nation.

subject: Written Comments
name: Kathryn McCluskey
body:
Dear Members of the National Capital Planning Commission,
I am submitting this comment for your March 5 meeting regarding the proposed East Wing modernization
and ballroom addition to the White House complex.
I strongly oppose this proposal.
The White House is one of the most historically and architecturally significant structures in the nation. Its
proportions, setting, and architectural integrity are central to its symbolic and civic importance. A
substantial addition—particularly one that alters the scale or character of the complex — risks permanently
changing a landmark that should be preserved with exceptional restraint.
My concerns include:
• Compatibility with historic character: The White House complex is not an open canvas for expansion. Any
large new addition threatens the established massing and visual harmony of the site.
• Long-term precedent: Approval of a major structural expansion could lower the threshold for future
alterations, gradually eroding the historic integrity of the complex.
• Necessity and proportionality: Functional or ceremonial needs should be evaluated against less intrusive
alternatives before introducing new construction of this scale.
The Commission plays a critical role in safeguarding the long-term planning and historic character of the
nation’s capital. I hope these responsibilities remain central to your deliberations.
Thank you for considering my comment.

body:
The Trump administration has ignored the laws put in place for so many things, that this ballroom project
seems to matter less, but is emblematic of many of the gross injustices being carried out by the Trump
administration.
I object to the demolition of the East Wing and the proposed ballroom for multiple reasons.
First, the haste at which the demolition occurred almost certainly means that environmental and other
protection measures were ignored, causing untold damage to both the environment and the workers who
have and will participate in this demolition and rebuilding. An investigation should determine the extent of
toxic debris that was hauled away; some of which was deposited onto a nearby public golf course. Since
there is ongoing, blatant disregard for public safety, there needs to be an independent body given the
authority to review the environmental damages, impose and collect fines and monitor the new construction
with the authority to stop all work if further laws are violated.
Second, congress must require full disclosure of funding, determine if there is any violation of the
Emoluments Act or favors granted (quid pro quo) and put in place a fiscal manager appointed by a judge for
the entire project.
Finally, while the damage is done and the historic East Wing has been destroyed, there is no need for a
90,000+ square foot ballroom at the White House. Let this empty space be just that, empty. It can be turned
into a space that the people can visit. If not, then certainly rebuilt to reflect what was lost and to serve the
people.

body:

modernization is required, pipes get old, a roof leaks, a foundation starts to fail, or many other senecios I
could name. This modernization project does not fall into one of those scenarios. The White House has a
space used as a ballroom, and it has served as such for many presidents. If a new ballroom is requires then
facts should be presented and a case made. The proposed space is unnecessary and overly extravagant. The
White House is not a palace and the president is not a king. The renderings I have seen remind me very
much of the French Renaissance not 2025. Also there is no reason for a new ballroom to be larger then the
White House, the new construction should compliment the existing buildings and not overwhelm them.
Besides the design, the money reported spent on this renovation is obscene and could be put to far better
use.
The part of all of this that, for me, is so tragic, is that the East Wing has already been torn down and cannot
be recovered.

next?

fact that the cost has ballooned from $200 million to as much as $400 million suggests that not enough
thought was put into the needs and design of the project in the first place.

construction. Ideally, approval should be declined on the basis that it is completely unnecessary. The
government’s purpose is not to throw large lavish parties save for state dinners which the existing WH has

design is too large and out of scale with the central colonnade and this diminishes the central colonnade as
the focus of the building. Furthermore, the larger it is the more it will cost to tear it down after Trump is
gone.

should occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being
funded by large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least,

preservation concerns. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American history.

accountability. The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and
major alterations should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant
project.

Thank you.
Marilyn Martella
Oakland, CA

subject: Written Comments
name: Susan LoFurno
body:
This articulates ALL the reasons this project was illegally executed.
The East Wing has been demolished with little to no oversight nor any environmental review as required by
the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). The White House and grounds are a National Park and a
National Historic Landmark owned by We the People.
This public comment period is a legally required process. According to your website, the public comment
process is one of several safe guards to "ensure transparency, accountability, and meaningful public input".
Major construction projects in DC must be reviewed by NCPC and CFA and they must comply with NEPA as
well as receive congressional approval. The Trump administration has ignored the laws put in place for so
many things, that this ballroom project seems minor in the scheme of things. Still, I am compelled to voice
my opinion. Maybe someday, there will be accountability.
I object to the project for these reasons:
1. The administration should be held accountable for violating NEPA during the demolition. Fines need to be
imposed for this negligence. An investigation is needed to determine the extent of toxic debris that was
hauled away; some of which was deposited onto a nearby public golf course. Since there is ongoing, blatant
disregard for public safety, there needs to be an independent body given the authority to review the
environmental damages, impose and collect fines and monitor the new construction with the authority to
stop all work if further laws are violated.
2. Congress, CFA and NCPC must require full disclosure of funding, determine if there is any violation of the
Emoluments Act or favors granted (quid pro quo) and put in place a fiscal manager appointed by a judge for
the entire project. If this cannot be set in place, the project cannot move forward.
3. There is no need for a 90,000+ square foot ballroom at the White House. Let this empty space be just
that- a place that tells its own story; what it was, and how it was illegally demolished- a monument to how
not to do things.
4. I will repeat- There is no need for a 90,000+ square foot ballroom at the White House. If something is to
be built, let it truly be the "People's House". Build a structure for the people- something that celebrates
who we are, not who the billionaires are. Make it a place where children and families can come to visit-
maybe a revolving Smithsonian exhibit or an arboretum or maybe an art museum (you can never have too
many). Build it to scale so that it doesn't overpower the original White House structure. Include some
meeting rooms and offices but make it something we can all have access to.

body:
"East Wing Modernization Project"?! How can you modernize something that has been destroyed?
This project must be decisively cancelled. It was a crime that the President illegally tore down an historic
wing of an historic federally owned building with no permission, no permit, and no plan.
I hope that the East Wing will be rebuilt at some point, in some fashion. But NOT as a gargantuan gilded
monument to one man's vanity, an unnecessary, ahistorical, poorly planned (that is giving it too much
credit - it was not planned at all, not designed by an architect, went through zero periods of public
comment or approval, and is a largely imaginary phantasm) abomination.
There is a long, thoughtful, interesting discussion to be had about how to restore the desecrated White
House. That discussion must in no way involve its desecrator. Whether to recreate a 125-year-old building
or design an appropriate new one is going to be a fraught and fascinating argument, and I look forward to
it, though I lament the unforgivable crime that prompts it. Trump must have no role and no say in this
decision. It is a question for the American public, for American architects and designers and historians, to
take up, with deliberation and responsibility and historical context and environmental care - qualities and
values that our current president is incapable of.

subject: Written Comments
name: Michelle Mayer
body:
I vehemently oppose this project in its entirety and expect the NCPC to protect the PEOPLE's HOUSE from
the current lawless and treasonous administration.
The White House is federal property, and structural modifications must comply with statutes governing
federal real estate regardless of funding source. 40 U.S.C. Chapter 31 governs public buildings management,
while 18 U.S.C. § 1361 prohibits willful damage to federal property. Private financing does not eliminate
these obligations because the property remains federally owned and legally protected. Demolition
reportedly commenced before formal submissions were filed, in clear violation of the governing statutes.
The National Historic Preservation Act mandates review for federal undertakings affecting historic
properties. Section 106 of the NHPA, overseen by the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, requires
assessment of effects on historic properties, consultation with preservation officials and stakeholders,
public comment opportunities and consideration of alternatives to avoid or mitigate harm. Demolition and
rebuilding in the manner that has been demanded is NOT what the American people want and is not in
keeping with the Historic character of the building .
The National Capital Planning Commission reviews federal development in the capital region under 40
U.S.C. §§ 8701-8737. The administration apparently argues demolition falls outside NCPC jurisdiction. Legal
experts counter that demolition enabling new construction is inherently part of that project and requires
integrated review. Separating demolition from construction to avoid oversight undermines the purpose of
planning law and is inherently underhanded. The current administration is making every attempt to
undermine the NCPC at every turn, because they know they are circumventing the law (at best) and
outright breaking it at every turn.
The National Capital Planning Commission MUST issue cease-and-desist orders, refuse permits for
subsequent construction phases and initiate formal Section 106 compliance reviews. YOU WORK for the
PEOPLE of the UNITED STATES and WE expect you to DO YOUR JOB ACCORDING TO THE LAW, NOT the
current lawless administration. Put an end to this nonsense and restore the EAST WING IN ITS ENTIRETY,
exactly as it was.

subject: Written Comments
name: Ravindra Athale
body:
Dear Members of NCPC:
I am writing this comment to formally register my disapproval of the proposed design for the new ballroom
extension to the White House. There are many dimensions to my distress and anger.
1. Total Disregard for the Process:
The demolition was carried out WITHOUT any discussion of approval of the plan of what will replace it. The
thinking was to present the citizens with fait accompli. This totally inconsistent with any democratic norms.
2. The proposed design is GROTESQUELY disproportionate with the original and historic structure of the
White House. A question arises as to how many times this massive ballroom will be utilized and how will the
space be used otherwise.
3. The funding source for this project appears to be an out and out lobbying effort by the rich and powerful
to curry favors from the President. While public-private partnership is central in updating and modernizing
any public space, that should and MUST happen once the design has been approved with public inputs such
as the one I am giving and public expenditure has been authorized and appropriated by the congress.
For these reasons I urge members of NCPC to disapprove the proposed design and launch a fully
transparent and open process to decide the future of the addition (made imperative by the illegal
destruction of existing structure).
Ravindra Athale

subject: Written Comments
name: Shawn Olson
body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project. The $400 million construction began without National
Capital Planning Commission approval, without required environmental assessments, and without
congressional authorization mandated by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
These violations should not be rewarded with after-the-fact approval.
In addition, the funding creates unacceptable conflicts of interest. Corporations holding billions in current
federal contracts with this administration are funding a construction project at the residence of the
president who controls those contracts. This is not charitable giving. This is an investment in access and
favorable treatment.
The White House belongs to the American people, not any individual president. I urge the Commission to
reject this proposal until full legal compliance is achieved, including congressional authorization and
completed environmental assessments. No temporary occupant should possess unilateral authority to
demolish historic structures without following the law.
Respectfully,
Shawn Olson

name: Joan Mushrush
body:
There is absolutely no need for the expansion and grotesquely opulent redesign of the East Wing. The
United States of America does not need a ballroom of this size attached to the existing White House. Not
now, not ever. The priorities of this administration are so out of line with what the general public is in need
of. The amount of money this is costing could pay for affordable healthcare for countless Americans who
are struggling to afford even the most basic care. The destruction of the existing East Wing mimics the
destruction done to our heritage and culture throughout the nation. A wrecking ball has been taken to the
country we all have known and loved our entire lives. It is unrecognizable to many and the American dream
is lost for those who find themselves in the bottom tier of the social ladder.
This is damaged, the legacy of the presidency beyond measure. Our nation’s leader is to be an example to
all of someone who deeply cares about every American. That includes those who have immigrated here and
are in the process of becoming naturalized citizens. In conclusion, this symbol of Americana, the People’s
House, should never have been altered without a thorough examination of its current condition, its use, its
value as a historical landmark, and without obtaining the required permissions done through the proper
laws and regulations.

subject: Written Comments
name: Olivia Kaiser
body:
I oppose the demolition of the White House East Wing because changes to a national historic site should
occur through transparent review, not unilateral action. Additionally, this $300M project is being funded by
large private donations at the behest of the sitting administration which creates at the very least the
appearance of influence-seeking or preferential access, and undermines public trust.
The East Wing was destroyed to make way for a new state ballroom funded largely by private donors, with
demolition beginning before review by the National Capital Planning Commission and amid unresolved
preservation concerns.
I am asking for clear disclosure of donor funding, environmental and design review, and public
accountability.
The White House is a shared civic symbol, not the property of any one administration, and major alterations
should follow the same oversight standards expected of every other federally significant project.

subject: Written Comments
name: Mary Saunders
body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

name: Amber Doran
body:
Hello, I am writing to inform you that I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which I would
be shocked if not everyone opposed it. It was initiated without the proper authorization, permits, or design
review. That’s absolutely appalling. It is not a modernization project, but rather a complete razing of our
American history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president, at any given time, is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Rosemarie Grant
body:
As an architect I understand the desire for a large formal meeting space on the White House grounds. But, I
am also a staunch advocate for historic preservation, having received my master’s degree in Adaptive
Reuse of historic structures.
The White House as a National Historic Landmark and symbol of our nation is one of the most recognized
buildings on the planet. I visit D.C. often and have a heartfelt attraction to the White House and all her
glory. It represents so much for the American people and embodies so much of our history. It is, in my
opinion the most significant historic site in the United States (and I have been to a lot of them).
As an architect I know that there are more sensitive, more functional, and more aesthetically pleasing
solutions that can be developed for the site. I cried when I witnessed the demolition of the East Wing and
will be horrified if the ballroom addition goes forth as it is currently envisioned.
I know from experience that a project of this type takes time to plan. You cannot develop a program that
satisfies the critical security requirements, the use requirements (large multi-functional meeting space, with
food service), meets the requirements of the International Building Code, and has been reviewed for
historic accuracy (or at least a sensitivity for alignment).
The planning of a project of this size and type would require several years. It should not be haphazardly
dashed together as the current proposal seems to have been done. We are not building a pole barn! We,
the people, who will live with the results for decades to come, should not see this project treated as some
developer fast-tack design-build exercise.
No one person should be entrusted with the power to alter, deface, or demolish a building that is so
important to our nation. Please listen to the American people when we say that the People's House, the
White House, deserves to be preserved and cared for so that future generations can enjoy this living,
breathing monument to the history of our Republic. And, We the People have a right and duty to provide
input into the process and shape the outcome.

subject: Written Comments
name: Shannon Koistinen
body:
Dear Members of the Commission,
I am writing to express my strenuous opposition to the proposed 90,000-square-foot "State Ballroom" and
East Wing reconstruction. While the administration frames this as a modernization, the design constitutes a
fundamental violation of the architectural integrity of the White House complex.
The total demolition of the East Wing in October 2025 was a betrayal of the public trust and a surgical strike
against American heritage. To claim that a 1942 historic landmark was 'excellently preserved' while reduced
to a pile of rubble is an insult to our collective intelligence.
We are replacing a functional, historic wing— the symbolic home of the Office of the First Lady— with a
90,000-square-foot 'State Ballroom' that is nearly double the size of the original Executive Mansion. This
isn't a renovation; it’s an annexation of public history by private interests. By bypassing Congressional
oversight and the National Historic Preservation Act, this administration has set a terrifying precedent: that
the 'People’s House' can be reconfigured at the whim of a single individual.
I urge the Commission to reject the current proposal based on the following design concerns:
Scale and Massing: The proposed 90,000-square-foot structure is nearly double the size of the original
Executive Mansion. This excessive massing overwhelms the historic residence, turning a globally recognized
neoclassical monument into a secondary attachment to a modern event space.
Disruption of the L’Enfant Plan: Renderings submitted on February 13 show that the ballroom’s height and
eastern expansion will permanently obstruct protected views and sightlines from 15th Street NW. This
diminishes the "Temple of Liberty" silhouette intended by the city’s original planners.
Architectural Incongruity: The use of modern bulletproof glazing and gilded neoclassical mimicry creates a
"theme park" aesthetic that clashes with the authentic Aquia Creek sandstone and historic character of the
North and South Porticos.
Loss of the East Colonnade’s Integrity: The October 2025 demolition of the East Garden Room and Family
Theater has already destroyed the delicate transition between the residence and the grounds. A 1,000-seat
ballroom cannot replicate the subservient, graceful proportions of the original Jeffersonian-inspired wings.
The White House belongs to the American people, not to private donors or a single administration’s
temporary needs. I request that the Commission require a significant reduction in the project's scale to
ensure the Executive Mansion remains the dominant feature of the site.
Respectfully,
Shannon Koistinen
La Crosse, Wisconsin

responsibility: to rebuild it with the same architectural integrity, historical fidelity, and craftsmanship that
define the White House.

important symbols. The American people deserve a restoration that honors the original design, respects
established preservation standards, and reflects the timeless character of the Executive Residence.
There must be full transparency, strict adherence to preservation guidelines, and independent oversight to
ensure the rebuilt East Wing is worthy of the White House itself.
Anything less would diminish a structure that belongs to history — and to the American people.
Respectfully,
Robbie McConnell

name: Jeremy Shaw
body:
To the Members of the National Capital Planning Commission:
I strongly oppose the expenditure of any funds on this project—let alone a reported $300 million. The
demolition of the East Wing, a historic and irreplaceable part of our national heritage, was initiated without
proper authorization. There were no approved plans, no formal reviews, no permits, no lawful
authorization, and no presentation to United States Congress.
This is not a modernization project. It is the complete destruction of American history. It appears driven by
personal ego and a desire to leave a self-indulgent, ornamental legacy rather than to preserve the dignity
and integrity of a national landmark.
This project is neither necessary nor supported by a significant majority of the American people. I call for its
immediate cancellation and for the East Wing to be rebuilt and restored to its original design and historical
character.
No individual is above the law. Allowing this project to proceed without accountability would be an affront
to every law-abiding American. A failure to impose consequences for such a blatant disregard of legal
process would undermine the very principles of governance, transparency, and the rule of law that our
institutions are meant to uphold.
Respectfully,
Jeremy Shaw

subject: Written Comments
name: HOPE HARRINGTON
body:
I am a resident of Washington, DC and was born in the city at Columbia Hospital for Women. My mother,
grandmother and grandfather were also born in this city. As were my great-grandfather and great-
grandmother.
It is unfortunate and inappropriate that the former east wing of the White House has been demolished.
Equally unfortunate and inappropriate are the current plans for a ballroom to take the place of the east
wing. That the proposed building will be larger than the White House itself is laughable...and an
embarrassment. This plan should be scrapped, with provision made for space to house White House staff
and records and for welcoming guests to the White House. A new east wing should complement the
architecture of the White House, not dwarf it. Or overshadow it. Washington, like Paris, is a beautiful city
with historic structures and green spaces that enhance its beauty for visitors and residents to enjoy. The
aesthetic of the city is its calling card. That this has been deliberately maintained during my life, that of my
parents and forbears is a lesson for those who temporarily reside in the city. "If it isn't broken, don't fix it" is
a well-known saying that applies.!
Respectfully submitted,
Hope Harrington
2/17/26

body:
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or

respect for the people of the United States.

oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Tammeron Jonesfrancis
body:
Under any other administration the demolition of the east wing and the threat of the construction of a
ballroom adjacent to the White House proper, as described by President Trump, would have been
stopped before the work commenced.
President Trump’s demolishing of the East wing as well as the ballroom addition is unacceptable. The White
House is “the house of the people” and has significant symbolic weight as the face of democracy. Because
of this designation, the building needs to be treated with all of the deference equivalent to its place within
the story of this nation; every opportunity needs to be made for recommendations by laymen and relevant
professionals before the building and site is modified. Thus far there has been no serious attempt to solicit
the professional advice of historians, preservationists, architects or interested laymen. Further, funds for
the construction of the Ballroom have not been allocated through congress but by private donations leaving
an obvious opportunity for exposure to corruption.
Almost every county in the United States has buildings within it that are designated in one way or another
as ‘historic.’ Historic structures are granted particular care by the counties’ citizens, officers and experts
not merely because they are old but because they hold a key to the story of a community. Because historic
buildings hold these stories they are dear and cared about by the community. Thus, they are protected by a
panel of caring individuals as well local and national regulations intending to protect the stories that these
buildings represent. The White House, because it is dear to the nation, has been likewise protected by
committees of citizens, professional experts, local and national laws. But, President Trump has willfully
ignored regulations as well as the review process intending to protect “the house of the people.”
It is common knowledge that the White House is intended as a temporary office for an administrator not a
palace for a king. Some criticize the ballroom’s design as an unaesthetic overpowering of the White House
proper. Indeed, the relationship between the existing White House and the proposed ballroom addition is
grotesquely improper. Frequently, this relationship has been described by critics as “the tail wagging the
dog.” Even so, this still misses the point. The proportional relationship displayed would be bad for any
building and its addition. Here we are considering a building that lends Americans and the world the
revolutionary story of American democracy. The White House is not gilded with gold, it does not have
imposing hallways nor is it stuffed with marble busts of the current leader because the White House is not
intended to intimidate. This is in obvious contrast to other buildings representing seats of government
standing at the time of White House’s construction. A ballroom addition would be a violent rewriting of the
intended democratic story that the White House's design intends to tell.

respect for the people of the United States.

a violent fait accompli.

in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

name: Ruth Hayes
body:
I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

body:
I oppose the East Wing Modernization Project.
This project began without required National Capital Planning Commission approval, without environmental
assessments mandated by the National Environmental Policy Act, and without congressional authorization
required by federal law for construction on federal parkland in Washington.
The $400 million cost is funded by corporations holding billions in federal contracts with the administration
approving those contracts.
This creates an unacceptable conflict of interest.
The White House is not private property. It belongs to the American people. No President should have
unilateral authority to demolish historic structures and approve construction without following the law and
allowing public input.
I urge the Commission to reject this proposal.

subject: Written Comments
name: Dan Shoemaker
body:
I wish to voice my opposition to the project. As someone who has worked with documenting historical
structures for the Tennessee Historic Commission, I understand the need for modernization vs the desire to
maintain a historic structure. This project took no effort to preserve the historic elements of the East Wing
and simply destroyed the structure without thought or consideration for the historic nature of the building.
As a result, we have an excellent opportunity to rebuild this East Wing in historically sensitive style and to
bring about those modernizations that are deemed necessary. Proper scale should be maintained in order
to preserve the historic facade of the entire White House grounds. Please take into consideration the
overall historic perspective of this important site.
V/R
Dr. Dan Shoemaker

homeowner did the same demolition and/or rebuild to their home without valid permits)

administration promised that they had private funds to demolish & build the ballroom, so please ensure
they use these same funds to rebuild the East Wing to its pre-demolition condition. Many thanks for your
attention.

body:
I STRONGLY oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper
authorization, permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of
American history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

subject: Written Comments
name: Doc Grauberger
body:
Greetings,
Thank you for considering my thoughts.
I realize that the White House and the it’s east and west wings have historically gone through many
changes over the years, but when it has been done it was done in a considered way, and being the peoples
house, done in consultation with the people. This was not the case here.
The White House was never meant to be a castle, it was never meant to be huge and ostentatious, it was
meant to be just enough, to support the term limited leadership of the land, see them off back into private
life once completed, and then open its doors to the next team. A building for the people, by the people, a
working building to get the job done, with some comfort and stately style, but not a mansion to impress or
impose upon others.
The east wing needs to be returned to its original footprint, with consultation with measured professionals
of history and architecture. Back to a symbol of balance, with a central house with equal east and west
wings, that represents what our country should be. Yes, modernization is needed, to bring things up to
modern code, technology and standards, but it should be done in a manner that respects the original look
and plan. Whatever national security needs below ground can obviously be addressed.
A giant ballroom, that dwarfs the rest of the building, paid for by enriched special interests, does not serve
the people, but turns the site into some sort of event center, to host fundraising galas of future
administrations.
The original ballroom was enough, the original footprint of the east wing was enough, we do not need the
grandiosity of kings. Let us return to measure and balance. Return the east wing to its previous basic design
and size.
Thank you for your time,
D. R. Grauberger

I oppose the spending of $300 million on this project, which was initiated without the proper authorization,
permits, or design review. It is not a modernization project but rather a complete razing of American
history.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.

original mansion should be so large as to overshadow the original building. In addition, an East Wing
building should be roughly equal in size and structure to the existing West Wing to create visual symmetry
and harmony.

subject: Written Comments
name: Candace Gruber
body:
I concur completely with the opinion of many others who may be submitting similar statements. Please
read this again, in case it has not yet sunk in! Pay special attention to the final paragraph.
The White House is a National Historic Landmark and a National Park, owned by the American people and
home to presidents since 1800. The current president at any given time is not the owner of the property or
the structures thereon; the president is a temporary tenant whose interventions are limited by law and by
respect for the people of the United States.
The demolition of the historic East Wing without review, without permits and without Congressional
oversight is clearly a violation of the law. In addition, it is a violation of the trust of the American people
who were given no opportunity to comment on what should have been presented as a proposal and not as
a violent fait accompli.
I urge the National Capital Planning Commission to require reconstruction of the East Wing in keeping with
its historic design and size. Anything constructed on the demolition site going forward must be compatible
in form and subordinate in scale to the original structure of the Executive Mansion.
I, too, want this project canceled, and the East Wing rebuilt and restored to its former design. No one is
above the law and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing those who broke the law would be
an affront to all law-abiding Americans!
Sincerely,
Candace Gruber

subject: Written Comments
name: Eugene Aleci
body:
I strongly oppose the spending of $300 million on this project. The project was initiated and demolition fully
executed to a point of destruction, well beyond retrieval of the structure, all without the proper
authorization, consideration permits, or preservation and design review.
It is not a modernization project but rather a complete disregard and razing of American history. All
presidents reside and use facilities temporarily - acting as occupants and watchful stewards of the site (only
for a period of some 4 to 8 years) at the White House. The property and structures are owned by the People
of the USA, and all costs are typically paid for by the US Taxpayers, only when authorized by Congress. NO
President owns or can possess this property, nor can have ANY right to alter the facilities to her / his tastes,
desires, or needs, without prior approval from the designated bodies such as yours which are there to look
after the Public's interest. NO President has the legitimate power to overtake OUR ownership, nor YOUR
review process and authorization. If these points may not be concretely established in laws, they are set
and recognized by all as operating standards over many decades. All other presidents and staffs have
respected these rules and this property, even as substantial alterations have been made. NO president has
any unique or special privileges to alter the ground or buildings as desired or needed without advance
discussion and ultimately acknowledging and following YOUR review and approval on behalf of the
American People.
I consider the recent planning and demolition actions taken by the current occupants to be on effect
"illegal" - even if not strictly prohibited by our laws - a dubious proposition I strongly question. Decades,
even more than a century of precedent have established this.
I want this project entirely canceled, and the East Wing must be rebuilt and restored in close alignment to
its former design. I also expect the reconstruction to be done properly and WITHOUT ANY COST to the
Taxpayers, because the damage and erasure of our heritage was done in haste, decided by a few individuals
absent the public, and without legitimate consultation and in direct and intentional avoidance of
established procedures. No one is above the law, and to permit this project to go ahead without penalizing
those who broke the law would be an affront to ALL law-abiding Americans; it would also "award" the law-
breakers with their desired outcome. It can therefore NOT stand. The outcome here will surely have major
ripple effects for ALL such public properties. This Administration MUST be fully affected by their glaring and
intentional violation of these public rules, to be sure that we re-establish - BEYOND ANY QUESTION OR
DOUBT - the public property rights and cultural heritage rights of ALL Americans. Further, denial of
permission for this demolition MUST be complete to allow the public to retain power over the expenditures
of any current or future public or private funds affecting all the properties of We, the People, and to retain
our rights to protect our history, heritage and public properties.
If I may be af any further service in this matter, I would be pleased to make my further knowledge and
information on this matter available to you at your request.
Thank you,
Eugene L. Aleci,
ARCHITECT,
CONSULTANT IN PRESERVATION AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT
